St. Hannibal was born to a knight and a noblewoman in Messina, Italy on July 5, 1851. He was orphaned at a tender age. As a young man, he had been given the intuition of the necessity of Prayer for Vocations. When he became a priest (March 16, 1878), he committed himself to the moral and spiritual redemption of the poorest area in his city, giving up all his inherited wealth to the service of God through his manifold works of charity among the poor children. He is known as the “Apostle of Prayer for Vocations” because he focused all his works on the promotion of the ROGATE (Latin for “pray”), following the evangelical call of our Lord as told by two evangelists: Matthew (9:37-38) and Luke (10:2) – “THE HARVEST IS GREAT, BUT THE WORKERS ARE FEW, PRAY THEREFORE THE LORD OF THE HARVEST TO SEND GOOD WORKERS INTO HIS HARVEST.” Pondering upon the meaning and message of the sacred words, he saw in them the ineffable solution for the salvation of the many poor children whom he learned to love with tender and divine affection. Fr. Hannibal founded two religious congregations, the Rogationists of the Heart of Jesus and the Daughters of Divine Zeal, to help him carry out and propagate the prayer for vocations.

Fr. Hannibal passed to eternity on June 1, 1927, but his spirit remains alive in the hearts and minds of all his spiritual sons and daughters. He was beatified on October 7, 1990 during the Synod of Bishops and was canonized on May 16, 2004 in Rome, Italy by His Holiness, Pope John Paul II.

A wholesome educational formation is possible only through cooperative efforts extended by both the home and the school. Consistency of purpose and manner in realizing this formation is best achieved through policies and regulations. This handbook is intended for the purpose of this realization. It aims to summarize in an orderly and readable manner all the salient information and the policies and regulations of Rogationist College. Through this, it is expected that: 1. Students will acquaint themselves with the objectives, policies, procedures and regulations of Rogationist College; 2. Administrators and teachers will acquire working knowledge in guiding the education community to realize the vision-mission and goals of the school as they promote the observance of its policies and regulations; and 3. Parents will understand their role in promoting and realizing the educational and institutional objectives of the school. The policies, rules and regulations in this handbook are intended to promote an atmosphere that is conducive to the students’ personal growth founded on Christ and His Gospel to pursue God’s call, in obedience to the Rogate, and in accordance with the ideals of St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia.

Like any family or community, Rogationist College (RC) has a rich historical heritage which every RC student should be proud of. To appreciate more deeply the roots of an RC community, an overview of the history of the congregation of the Rogationists, and more particularly that of RC, is presented here.

The Rogationists of the Heart of Jesus (RCJ) is a religious congregation of priests and brothers founded by St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia in 1887 in Messina, Italy. Both the Rogationists of the Heart of Jesus and its sister congregation, the Daughters of Divine Zeal, are devoted to prayer and promotion of vocations in the Church, and to the education of young people, particularly the poor and disadvantaged. The legacy of St. Hannibal is kept alive by these congregations present today in Europe (Italy, Spain, Albania and Poland); in South America (Brazil, Argentina and Paraguay); in North America (USA and Mexico); in Africa (Rwanda and Cameroun); in Oceania (Papua New Guinea); and in Asia (the Philippines, India, Korea, Vietnam, and Indonesia).

The Rogationists established their first missionary activities in the Philippines in November 1976 to promote a culture of vocation and to assist the poor especially the children. Their long term strategy was to prepare young Filipinos to be agents of social growth and transformation driven by the ideals of St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia. Milestones in the development of the Rogationist Philippine Delegation: - October 1977 - opening of the first Rogationist Formation Center in Merville Park (Parañaque); - November 1979 - construction of a parish church in Multinational Village (Parañaque); - June 1980 – profession of the religious vows of the first three Filipino Rogationist novices; - December 1981 - opening of a second and larger Rogationist Formation Center in Merville Park; - June 1987 - opening of St. Anthony’s Boys Village and Rogationist Academy (High School) in Silang, Cavite; - April 1990 - opening of the Rogationist Formation Center for the Visayan Region in Cebu City; - January 1999 - start of the new mission in Toril, Davao City with Fr. Hannibal Children’s Home, a charitable institution for children;

- December 1999 - inauguration of the Fr. Di Francia Center of Studies for Religious Formation in Theology in Parañaque City; - January 2002- opening of the Oasis of Prayer and Retreat House in Silang, Cavite; - May 2002 - acceptance of the Parish of Our Lady of Del Pilar in Zaragoza, Pangasinan; - June 2004 - beginning of the St. Hannibal Empowerment Center in Pasay; - June 2005 - establishment of a parish in Parang, Bataan.

section_title: SAINT ANTHONY’S BOYS VILLAGE and ROGATIONIST COLLEGE
content: The Saint Anthony’s Boys Village (SABV) in Silang, Cavite is the first “Anthonian Boys Village” of the Rogationists in the Philippines, a proof of St. Hannibal’s love for children. This religious charitable institution serves as home to indigent boys who desire to pursue quality education. The village complex was acquired by Rev. Fr. Antonio Barbangelo, RCJ during the term of former Superior General Fr. Gaetano Ciranni, RCJ and was built under the supervision of Fr. Salvatore Ciranni, RCJ. Milestones in the history of St. Anthony’s Boys Village and Rogationist College: - March 2, 1985 – The cornerstone was blessed by the late Bishop of Imus, Cavite, His Excellency Felix Perez, in the presence of civic, religious and government representatives. - May 1987 - Rogationist Academy (RA) in SABV was established as a co-educational Catholic High School to meet the educational needs of the first batch of 35 interns in SABV and of the youth in the surrounding communities. - June 13, 1987 - The complex was inaugurated during the feast of St. Anthony of Padua by the Papal Nuncio, His Excellency Bruno Torpigliani, and His Eminence Jaime Cardinal L. Sin under the sponsorship of Mr. Francisco Eizmendi, President of San Miguel Corporation, and with the presence of His Excellency Mario Crema, the Ambassador of Italy to the Philippines. The new Father General, Fr. Pietro Cifuni, RCJ appointed Fr. Carmelo Capizzi, RCJ as SABV’s first Rector.

section_title: SAINT ANTHONY’S BOYS VILLAGE and ROGATIONIST COLLEGE
content: - June 1987 – With a permit to operate from the Department of Education, Culture and Sports (DECS), the High School Department was opened. - 1990 - The complex had new facilities built such as the Telesco Library and Art Gallery, the Miserior-funded carpentry, and the housing facilities for the assisted boys. The high school department was granted Government Recognition, signifying the school’s capability to offer quality secondary education. - 1990-1991 - The SABV Gymnasium was constructed. - 1991 - The Cassetti Computer Laboratory was built and the standby 100-kW electric generator was acquired. Rogationist Academy held its 1st Commencement Exercises with 66 graduates, 25 of whom were interns, in April 1991. It was also in this year when the Rogationist Academy Technical School opened with TESDA-approved post-secondary vocational and technical courses in Computer Programming, Typing, Drafting, Electronics Technology and Electrical Technology. - 1993 – 1994 - Under the Rectorship of Fr. Bruno Rampazzo, RCJ, Mechanical and Automotive Technology courses were added, through the generosity of the Ministerio de AsuntosExteriores of Spain (SECIPE) and the NGO Manos Unidas. - 1994 – With financing from the Italian government, the Technical School building, with laboratories and modern equipment, was constructed. The Di Francia Auditorium and additional classrooms were built.

section_title: SAINT ANTHONY’S BOYS VILLAGE and ROGATIONIST COLLEGE
content: - 1995 - A Learning Resource Center was established. The Belgian government and Comide from Bruxelles financed the Rogate Press. This made it possible for the school to offer courses in Graphic Arts and Printing Technology. Government recognition was issued to the Technical School in these three-year courses: Computer Technology, Electrical Technology, Electronics Technology and Graphic Arts and Printing Technology. - 1996-1997 - The local PHINMA group provided new boarding facilities to SABV. Three-year Mechanical Technology, two-year Office Management with Computer and one-year Computer Technician courses were offered. - 1997 – 1998 – Three-year Automotive Technology and Electronics Technology courses were added. - 1999 – 2000 – TVET issued Program Registration Certificates to three-year Mechanical Technology, Automotive Technology & Office Management with Computer courses. The Dual Training Program (DTP) started during this period. Temporary permits to offer the first year level of BS in Information Technology and BS in Industrial Technology major in Electronics, Electrical, Graphic Arts and Printing, Mechanical and Automotive Technology were obtained from the Commission on Higher Education (CHED). On August 21, 1999, the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) conferred to the Rogationist Academy Technical School the 1999 “Kabalikat Award” for being an outstanding training institution, recognizing its role as a partner of the government in the promotion and development of the country’s manpower.

section_title: SAINT ANTHONY’S BOYS VILLAGE and ROGATIONIST COLLEGE
content: - February 26, 1999 to February 26, 2011 – Rogationist Academy Technical School served as an accredited assessment venue for Electric Motor Repair and Industrial Electricity. - 2001 – 2002 - During the term of Fr. Mariano Rondael Jr., RCJ as Superior and Rector, Rogationist Academy became Rogationist College (RC) upon the approval of the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) which issued the Permits to Operate (PTO) for the Bachelor of Science degree courses in Information Technology and Industrial Technology. It also became an authorized Testing Center for Microsoft Office Specialist Certification. The Automotive Technical Training Center was expanded, through a new contribution of Manos Unidas and the assistance of AECI. A third floor was built at the college building to accommodate a growing population of students. The Oasis of Prayer was also opened to cater to the spiritual needs of the populace, particularly of the RC community. - 2002-2003 - CHED granted Government Recognition for the courses BS in Information Technology and BS in Industrial Technology. New degree programs were also offered: BS in Computer Science, BS in Electronics and Communications Engineering, BS in Computer Engineering, BS in Hotel and Restaurant Management, BS in Business Administration and Associate in Computer Technology.

section_title: SAINT ANTHONY’S BOYS VILLAGE and ROGATIONIST COLLEGE
content: During this school year, the High School Department adopted the DepEd-prescribed Basic Education Curriculum (BEC). - 2003-2004 - Fr. Gabriel Flores, RCJ assumed the Rectorship with Fr. Carmelo Capizzi, RCJ as Superior. A short list of developments includes: three buses for school service; lightings for the gymnasium and football field; a bar for the HRM courses; construction of the “Glorietta” (fully funded by High School-Student Body Organization and the Parent-Teachers Association); the new St. Hannibal School Clinic, equipped with modern dental facilities, emergency and ECG rooms; and additional classrooms to accommodate the increasing population of the college. The College Department programs were enriched to respond to the growing needs of the community. In the CHED programs new courses with licensure were also offered like Bachelor of Secondary Education Major in Mathematics and English, and Bachelor of Science in Accountancy. Likewise, TED offered programs to make education more affordable to the less privileged youth without downgrading the quality and exposure of the students to the skills component of the course. Short-term training programs in the various trade areas like Automotive, Mechanical, Electronics, Electrical and Computer Technology were also offered to address the needs of out-of-school youths and even professionals to enhance their skills and cope with the rapidly changing technology. During its initial year of implementation, the TED conducted trainings on Basic Engine Troubleshooting with Petron employees; Cable Termination with Shimizu, an electrical engineering/contracting firm; and Pneumatics/Hydraulics to engineering students from different schools in Cavite.

section_title: SAINT ANTHONY’S BOYS VILLAGE and ROGATIONIST COLLEGE
content: Consortium arrangements were made with some colleges in Region IV-A for the sharing of manpower, resources, facilities and technical expertise. The Dual Training System approach to technical training was also revitalized by intensifying campaigns for partnership with various companies for the full implementation of this modality of skills training delivery. - 2004 – 2005 – The High School Department introduced the career tracking scheme through its elective offerings and by upgrading its Technology and Livelihood Education programs. - 2005 -2006 – TVET issued Program Registration Certification to Tourism, Hotel & Restaurant Operation course. On July 18, 2005, the Bureau of Immigration granted the school the authority to accept foreign students. - 2006 – 2007 – Additional courses in the college department were also offered: BS in Secondary Education Major in Religious Education, BS in Hospitality Management Major in HRM with Certificate in Culinary Arts, and BS in Hospitality Management Major in Tourism Management with Certificate in Tour Guiding and Operations. The second batch of HRM students had their international on-the-job training in Singapore. In line with the program of President Gloria Macapacal Arroyo, TESDA and CHED awarded RC a Certificate of Recognition as a pioneering institution in the implementation of Ladderized Education System under E.O. 358 “To Institutionalize a Ladderized Interface between Technical Vocational Education and Training and Higher Education”. The certificate was given on July 12, 2006 in Malacañan Palace, Manila.

section_title: SAINT ANTHONY’S BOYS VILLAGE and ROGATIONIST COLLEGE
content: Rogationist College was assessed by CHED, RQAT (Regional Quality Assessment Team) and TESDA supervisors and inspectors as one of the schools in Region IV-A to have the best facilities, equipment and instruments in the different technical laboratories. Also in this school year, TVET issued Program Registration Certificates to two-year courses (which were previously 3-year courses) with corresponding program qualifications, in order to upgrade the program and fulfill TVET requirements. These were: Automotive Technology (Automotive Servicing NCII, Automotive Body Repairing NCII, Automotive Body Painting NCII and Automotive Engine Rebuilding NCII); Mechanical Technology (Machining NCII); Electrical Technology (Building Wiring Installation NCII), PC Operations (Office Clerks and Assistants NCII); and Graphic Arts and Printing Technology courses. - 2007 – 2008 – Government Recognition was granted to the College for Bachelor in Elementary Education (BEEd). The TED pioneered the TESDA E-Learning Program (Distance Learning Program) for Automotive, Mechanical and Electronics Technology and the Caregiving Program. In this school year, TVET issued Program Registration Certificates to two-year Electronics Technology (Consumer Electronics Servicing NCII), PC Operations with Office Management and Caregiving NCII courses. - 2008 – 2009 –TVET issued Program Registration Certificates to Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SWAM NC Level I and II) and Computer Hardware Servicing (NCII Level) courses.

section_title: SAINT ANTHONY’S BOYS VILLAGE and ROGATIONIST COLLEGE
content: - 2009 – 2010 – RC/SABV had new administrators in the persons of Fr. Herman Abcede, RCJ as the Superior and Fr. Eduardo Fernandez, RCJ as the Rector. Bachelor of Science in Office Administration was given permit to open. Transfer of the HS Library, Accounting, HRD, Cashier’s, Registrar’s and Dean’s offices to the new building took place. - 2010 – 2011 – The High School Department started the adoption of the Understanding by Design (UbD) approach. - 2011 – 2012 – BS in Accounting Technology was opened. BSE Religious Education was changed to AB Religious Education and BS in Office Administration was given government recognition. - 2012 – 2013 – The K-12 program was opened. All these achievements and improvements are chapters in the living history of SABV and Rogationist College written by the hand of the Divine Providence. Success in higher quality of education for the indigent youth and the more privileged sons and daughters of the community is assured by the guidance of St. Anthony of Padua and the inspiration of the Founder, St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia.

[] The Official RC logo represents man’s total human and Christian formation. The three Latin terms Fides, Sapientia and Virtus stand for Faith, Wisdom and Virtue, which are indicative of the three pillars (Religion, Reason, and Love) upon which the Rogationist College System of Education rests. The cross represents Christ, the living Foundation of the whole Rogationist educational community. The four vertical columns sustaining the cross signify the four core values (Rogate, Love of God and neighbor, Patriotism, Integrity and Excellence) anchored on the Rogationist educational philosophy. The curved lines leaning on one of the pillars of the cross symbolize the secondary education. The gear of the industrial wheel stands for the formation offered by the College and Technical Education Departments. The open book represents the Word of God – The HOLY BIBLE – the source of inspiration, knowledge and strength of all those who are part of the Institution. The Latin words Deus et Proximus (God and neighbor) stand for the direction of Rogationist College education.

Rogationist College exists primarily to enable the youth, especially the poor and underprivileged assisted by the St. Anthony’s Boys Village Foundation, to discover in their life the project of God by becoming good Christians and responsible members of society through Secondary, Technical and Tertiary education anchored on the formative philosophy of the Rogationists.

Rogationist College (RC) in St. Anthony’s Boys Village in Silang, Cavite is a Catholic co-educational community committed to the formation of the whole human person. RC, in its mission to help the youth, bases its educative system on a philosophy of education which is attentive to the instances of human life. It is both personalistic and vocational in nature. RC forms its students to the proper understanding and dynamics of self. The process brings them to a serene enjoyment of life according to the dictum of responsible acting and sharing. The vocational nature of the RC system facilitates its students in the acquisition of a realistic life perspective. It is a view which is sensitive to life’s origin and destiny. RC believes and professes that every person is called not only to live but also to fulfill life as God’s gift. RC is convinced that real education is not just academic education. It espouses a style of forming that opens avenues to the proper exercise of love of God and neighbor, patriotism, integrity, and excellence. The educative formation of RC is always considered an encounter between the teachers and their students. In doing the personalistic and vocational approach to education, RC individuates three interrelated moments of the meeting, which ends in the mature choices for the life orientation of its students.

The first moment is ORGANIZATION. Here, the organizing student is met by a teacher who is a guide. In this moment, the students are initiated to find and form the most important instances of their life and then cherish them. The second moment is IDENTIFICATION. Here teachers are models. St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia, founder of the Rogationist, wants all institutions of the Rogationists to educate through good examples. RC believes that for students to grow in the right direction, the edifying life of teachers is very important. The third moment is DECISION. Self-fulfillment is also self-determination. At the end of the formative process, students of RC should have already acquired a certain degree of independence. Knowing better to distinguish right from wrong, they should be capable of pursuing not just terrestrial but also personal and possibly celestial good. RC’s philosophy of education, following the teachings of St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia and inspired by the Gospel of the Christ of the Rogate, goes therefore to the roots of the human person.
Rogationist College is a prime Catholic educational community dedicated to the formation of culturally competent and socially responsible persons driven by the ideals of St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia.

Rogationist College commits itself to: 1. Form its members toward Love of God and neighbor, patriotism, integrity, and excellence; 2. Offer a balanced and technically-oriented curriculum, as well as excellent instruction, learning environment and facilities; 3. Prepare well-rounded graduates who are agents of social growth and transformation; and 4. Promote a culture of vocation and good workers who, like St. Hannibal, will be espousing the cause of the poor especially the children.

It promotes research and extension programs according to RC vision-mission. It monitors and evaluates the implementation of strategic and tactical plans of the school. 3. It animates the human, spiritual, and Rogationist Formation of the education community according to spirit and ideals of St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia. The arm of the DSA is the Campus Ministry Office which is established for the facilitation, animation and accompaniment of the community’s spiritual and religious activities. 4. It is responsible for the safeguarding of all records, documents and personal files of students in the high school, college and technical education departments. It keeps the government permits/memoranda/circulars and other related official documents. It facilitates the admission, enrollment, retention, transferring of students, scholarship and graduation activities. It coordinates with school-regulating government agencies (DepEd, CHED and TESDA).

5. Office of the Director for Academic Affairs The Office of the Director for Academic Affairs is located in Fr. Vitale Building. It is responsible for the overall directions of the academic programs of the high school, college and technical education departments. 6. Office of the Principal The Office of the JHS Principal is located in HS Building B of Fr. Vitale Building. It is responsible for the instructional leadership and supervision of the high school faculty members and the promotion of activities for the realization of the school’s vision-mission. 7. Office of the College Dean The Office of the College Dean is located in Fr. Vitale Building. It is responsible for the implementation of the academic program in accordance with CHED regulations. 8. Office of the Technical Education Head The Office of the Technical Education Head is located in Fr. Levi Building. It is responsible for the operation of the technical education programs in accordance with TESDA regulations. 9. Office of the Director for Student Services The Office of the Director for Student Services is located in Fr. Vitale Building. 10. Office for Guidance and Counseling The Office for Guidance and Counseling is located in HS Building B, Fr. Vitale Building for the junior high school department and in Fr. Levi Building for the senior high school, college and technical education departments. It aims to address the guidance and counseling needs of students to help them achieve their development as persons. The Office formulates and implements various programs in line with the school’s vision-mission. The following are the services provided by the Guidance Office: - Individual Inventory and Testing - Counseling - Referral - Follow-up - Evaluation - Information - Wellness and Prevention 11. Office for Student Discipline The Office for Student Discipline is located on the ground floor of Fr. Palma Building. Vitale Building and Pope John XXIII LRC is found on the 3^(rd) floor of Fr. Palma Building. The LRC supports the information needs of all the members of the institution. It helps the school personnel and students to transform information into knowledge and practice by providing quality and updated library information and learning services.

13. Avignone Clinic The clinic is adjacent to the St. Francis Sports Center. It promotes the well-being of the school community. It is administered by qualified health practitioners to address the health needs of the education community. 13.1. Medical Services: - first-aid treatment - health monitoring - personal care - health education program - referrals 13.2. Dental Services: - dental consultation and referrals - dental health education program - emergency dental treatment 14. Office for Student Affairs The Office for Student Affairs is located on the ground floor of Fr. Palma Building for college and technical education departments. The high school’s OSA is located on the 2^(nd) floor of HS Building A, Fr. Vitale Building. It supervises, evaluates and oversees the co-curricular activities and programs through the club moderators/advisers in coordination with the department heads and related offices. 15. 16. Office of the Finance and Administration Director The Office of the Finance and Administration Director is located in Fr. Vitale Building. Vitale Building. It handles the financial transactions of the school. It ensures accuracy and completeness of accounting data, adherence to policies and safeguarding of assets. Palma Building.
