Office for School Physical Plant and General Services The Office for School Physical Plant and General Services is located in Fr. Vitale Building. It is responsible for ensuring the integrity of the school physical plant and general services. 20. Office for Scholarship

The Office for Scholarship is located in Fr. Vitale Building. It handles the processing of academic scholarship applications of the high school, college and technical education departments. It coordinates with agencies such as DepEd, CHED and TESDA and other government and non-government organizations to assist students in availing of scholarships.

1. St. Anthony’s Chapel The St. Anthony’s Chapel is located in HS Building B, Fr. Vitale Building and is considered the heart of the school. It is a House of God and therefore a place for prayer. Students are encouraged to spend some moments with Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. The following shall be observed in the Chapel: 1.1. Silence should be maintained at all times. 1.2. Proper attire should be worn. 1.3. Cleanliness and orderliness of the chapel should be maintained. 2. Canteen and Food Services RC has two canteens to accommodate all the students and personnel. The college canteen is located near the entrance gate while the high school canteen is located near the St. Francis Sports Center. 3. St. Francis Sports Center The sports center is equipped with the following facilities: 3 indoor basketball courts, 2 volleyball courts, a soccer field, sound system, digital score board, shower rooms, dance hall, fitness room and other indoor games facilities. This is where most of the Physical Education classes are held. Students, after seeking permission from concerned school authorities. , may use the gymnasium for playing basketball, volleyball, badminton, and table tennis, and for dancing and other physical fitness activities provided they are in proper sports attire.

4. Conference Rooms and Multi-media Rooms 4.1. John Paul II Conference Room - located on the 3^(rd) floor of Fr. Palma Building. It can accommodate 100 persons. 4.2. Fr. GaspareGallitto Conference Room – located on the ground floor of Fr. Palma Building. It can accommodate 15 persons. 4.3. Fr. Joseph Aveni Conference Room – located in Fr. Vitale Building. It is usually used for School Board and School Council meetings. It can accommodate 20 persons. 4.4. St. Therese Multimedia Room – located on the 2^(nd) floor of HS Building A, Fr. Vitale Building. It can accommodate 40 persons . -The St. Therese Multi-media Room serves as the SHS guidance office 4.5. St. Bernadette Multi-media Room – located on the ground floor of Fr. Levi Building. It can accommodate 40 persons. 4.6. St. Claire Multi-media Room – located in Fr. Levi Building. It can accommodate 40 persons. Reservation of the conference rooms should be made with the Property Custodian three (3) days before their use. The HS Multi-media rooms may be reserved through the faculty in-charge. Students’ request for the use of conference rooms and multi-media rooms is honored only if noted by the teachers/instructors in-charge of the subject.

I. Audio-Visual Materials and Equipment 1. The faculty and students can borrow any of the audio-visual materials. 2. All audio-visual materials are for school, library, and classroom use only. 3. Request and reservation of the audio-visual materials should be forwarded to the Librarian at least three (3) days before their use. 4. Request of students for audio-visual materials is honored only if noted by the teachers/instructors in charge of the subject. 5. For teachers/instructors, audio-visual materials can be taken out only for an overnight use. Penalty for overdue materials will be imposed. II. Di Francia Auditorium and Audio-Visual Room (AVR) 1. The reservation/request slip for the use of the Di Francia Auditorium or Audio-Visual Room must be accomplished and submitted to the Property Custodian at least one week before the proposed activity (program, film viewing, etc.) 2. The program of activities and list of audio-visual materials needed must be given to the Property Custodian before the activity. 3. Facilities and other materials and equipment should be cleaned and properly arranged after their use. 4. Lights and air conditioning units should be turned off after the activity.

5. The “NO EATING, NO DRINKING” policy shall be strictly implemented. 6. Any problem encountered during the activity, especially equipment which is not functioning properly, should be immediately brought to the attention of the control room technician/library staff. 7. Students and teachers shall be held accountable for any damage done to any of the equipment used. III. Learning Resource Centers (LRC) 1. LRC schedule: Monday to Friday (7:30 am - 6:00 pm); Saturday (8:00 am- 12:00 noon) 2. Students may avail of the following services: 2.1. Library Orientation 2.2. Library Instruction 2.3. Library Exhibits 2.4. Library Guides 2.5. Reference and Information Services 2.6. Current Events Awareness 2.7. Reader Advisory Guidance 2.8. Searching, Reserving and Stack Service 2.9. Inter-Library Loan 2.10. Compiling Bibliographies upon request 2.11. Reader Word Power Corner 2.12. Film Viewing 3. The following non-print materials/services are available at the Instructional Media Center (IMC): 3.1. Overhead Projectors 3.2. Multimedia Materials 3.3. Visual Aids 4. A photocopying machine is also available at the LRC. 5. Rules Governing the Use of the Internet Access Room: 5.1. To access information from the internet access room, faculty and students should present their validated school ID at the circulation counter before using the internet terminals.

5.2. The Internet is used strictly for researches. 5.3. Use of computer is limited to one hour per session. (Repetition is possible but not in immediate succession.) 5.4. Preparing/typing of projects such as reaction and term papers, thesis or drawing in the computer is not allowed. 5.5. Printing and downloading of researched data or information may be requested at the circulation counter. 5.6. The “NO EATING, NO DRINKING” policy shall be strictly implemented. 5.7. CD-ROM formats and other multi-media software are available upon request at the circulation counter. 5.8. Students who violate these rules shall be subjected to disciplinary action. 6. Rules and Regulations in the LRC 6.1. All students of Rogationist College may borrow any learning resource material from the LRC by presenting a valid school ID. 6.2. SILENCE must be strictly observed. 6.3. The following are strictly prohibited inside the LRC: a. sleeping b. littering c. using electronic gadgets (cellphones, camera, MP3 players, Ipod, etc.) 6.4. Group study or group research may be done in the Discussion Room with reservation. 6.5. The library implements the Open Shelves Control System and uses the Online Public Access Catalogue (OPAC).

6.6. General references, pamphlets, newspapers, magazines or other periodical materials (loose or bound) and rare collections are read only inside the LRC. 6.7. Students are not allowed to bring camera or cellphone with camera inside the Thesis Collections Area. 6.8. Students are held responsible for the loss or damage of any learning material borrowed from the LRC. 6.9. No student is allowed to use the LRC and any of its resources unless all due accounts are settled. 6.10. Chairs and tables should be arranged properly after use. 6.11. Any problem encountered in the LRC should be reported to the Librarian or any of his staff for assistance. 6.12. No photograph may be taken in the reading areas without authorized permission from the Librarian. 6.13. Students must deposit their belongings at the baggage area. 6.14. Any student found violating any of the above-stated policies shall be referred to the Office of Student Discipline. 7. Rule on Circulation Books may be borrowed for three (3) days and may be renewed for another three (3) days provided they are not in demand. 8. Rules on “Reserved” Books

8.1. Due to limited copies, “Reserved” books may be used only for a certain time (1 hour) in the LRC. 8.2. “Reserved” books may be borrowed only during the last period in the afternoon. These should be returned not later than 9:00 a.m. the following day. 9. Materials for “Library Use Only” 9.1. General Reference Materials 9.1.1. Encyclopedia 9.1.2. Dictionaries 9.1.3. Atlases 9.1.4. Almanac 9.1.5. Periodicals 9.2. Non-Print Materials

9.2.2. Audio CD/DVD 9.2.3. Multimedia CDs 9.2.4. Audio cassettes tapes 9.2.5. Transparencies 9.2.6. Slides 9.2.7. VHS tapes 10. Fines and Other Penalties 10.1. For overdue regular, fiction and reference books, a fine of P5.00/day including Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays will be charged. 10.2. For overdue reserved books, a fine of P5.00/hour including Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays will be charged. 10.3. Unauthorized taking out of LRC materials is punishable by suspension of LRC privileges. In addition, the case will be reported to the Office of Student Discipline. 11. Lost Books Lost books should be reported immediately to the Librarian. Otherwise, the lost book will be considered as overdue and the borrower will have to pay the overdue fine. Aside from the cost of the lost book (or replacement with the same book), a processing fee of P200.00 shall also be charged. 12. Disfiguring of Library Materials Students who disfigure (mutilate and/or mark) any library materials, whether book or periodical, shall be suspended from borrowing books for one month and will be fined P100.00 per page or replacement of the same material. In addition, the case will be referred to the Office for Student Discipline.
All penalties and fines should be settled and paid at the Cashier’s Office.

1. Computer Laboratories There are six computer laboratories: two computer laboratories for the high school department, three for the college and technical education departments and one for speech classes. The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the Computer Laboratories: 1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their computer class. 2. The following are prohibited inside the computer rooms: 1.2.1. Food and drinks 1.2.2. Laptops and other electronic gadgets 1.2.3. Using of computer for games 1.2.4. Playing with computer peripherals/accessories 1.2.5. Copying (uploading/downloading) any program from the computer 1.2.6. Opening and attempting to repair any computer 1.2.7. Use of computer hardware and accessories outside the laboratory 1.3.Students should use only their designated computer units. 1.4. Care must be observed while using the equipment in the laboratory. Everything must be returned to its proper place after use. 3. Science Laboratories There are two science laboratories for the College Department, the Chemistry and Physics Laboratories. For the High School Department, there are four science laboratories: General Science, Biology, Chemistry and Physics Laboratories. These are provided with the necessary equipment, instruments, gadgets, utensils, tools, supplies and materials. These laboratories enable the students to gain adequate learning experiences on the theories and principles taught in the classroom through laboratory exercises and experiments.

The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the Science Laboratories: 3.1. Unauthorized persons are not allowed to enter the laboratories. 3.2. Vandalism and littering as well as eating and drinking are prohibited in the laboratories. 3.3. Laboratory seats should be arranged at all times. 3.4. Bags, books and the like should be placed on designated areas. Working tables should be reserved for laboratory materials/equipment needed in the experiment. 3.5. Cabinets in the laboratories can only be used as storage for laboratory paraphernalia. 3.6. Laboratory gowns and/or protective gear such as masks, goggles and gloves should be worn whenever necessary during experimentation. 3.7. After each laboratory activity, the subject teacher/students should check that: 3.7.1. All borrowed laboratory equipment/materials are returned clean, dry and in good working condition. 3.7.2. Working tables are clean and dry. 3.7.3. Sinks are free from lumps. Faucets, gas outlets, lights and ceiling fans are turned off. 3.7.4. Chairs are properly arranged. 3.7.5. Writing on the boards is erased. 3.7.6. Laboratory wastes, chemicals and plant and animal specimens are disposed at designated areas of the laboratory.

3.8. Any untoward incident related to laboratory activities shall be reported by the students to the subject teacher/instructor or laboratory assistant in charge. 3.9. A subject teacher/instructor/laboratory assistant who has knowledge of any untoward incident should prepare a concise incident report which contains the exact date, time and persons involved. 3.10. Any subject teacher/instructor/laboratory assistant who fails to submit the incident report within 48 hours shall be held accountable for the cost of the damage. 3.11. The incident report shall be submitted in 3 copies to the Property Custodian, Science Subject Area Coordinator and Principal or Cluster Coordinator/TED Head for appropriate action. 3.12. In cases of breakage of materials or damage to equipment/facilities, policies stipulated in the Students Manual shall be applied. 3.13. Students who fail to return borrowed material/equipment will not be allowed to borrow again without first settling their responsibility. 3.14. For loss/breakage/damage of laboratory material/equipment, the student should pay through the Cashier’s Office the exact amount as determined by the Property Custodian/Purchasing Officer. The official receipt (O.R.) should then be presented to the Laboratory Assistant/Subject Teacher/Instructor for clearance signing.

4. Technical Laboratories There are six technical laboratories. The Automotive, Mechanical, Welding, and Pneumatics Laboratories are located in Fr. Levi Building. The Electronics and Electrical Laboratories are found in Fr. Palma Building. These are equipped with industry standard facilities and training materials to ensure transfer of learning and skills to students. These laboratories are also made available to High School students for their Technology and Livelihood Education subjects. The following are the rules and regulations inside the Technical Laboratories: 4.1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their technical and practical classes.All scientific and technical works or projects must be performed in the respective laboratories. 4.2. Procedures prescribed by the subject teacher or instructor must be strictly followed. 4.3. Equipment, tools or materials may be borrowed from the stockroom only after accomplishing a borrower’s slip. 4.4. Utmost care must be observed when using any of the equipment, tools or chemicals in the laboratories. The students shall be held responsible for any damage done to any of the equipment, instruments or tools used. 4.5. Students are not allowed to use or take any of the equipment, tools or materials outside the laboratories.

4.6. Students should deposit their personal belongings in the lockers provided outside the laboratories. 5. Technology and Livelihood Education (TLE) Laboratory The TLE Laboratory is located in Fr. Bonarrigo Building. It is equipped with sewing, housekeeping, baking, and cooking equipment. The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the TLE Laboratory: 5.1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their TLE class. 5.2. Students should wear proper attire while doing the activities in the laboratory. 5.3. Moving from one working area to another without the permission of the subject teacher, and playing or running are strictly prohibited. 5.4. Care must be observed while using any of the utensils and equipment in the laboratory. In case a student or a group of students accidentally or intentionally breaks an equipment or utensil, the said student or group is required to replace it. 5.5. Students should use equipment in the laboratory under the supervision of the subject teacher. 5.6. Students should provide their own cleaning materials (i.e. dishwashing liquid, dishwashing foam/pad, cleaning rags and garbage bag). 5.7. Order and cleanliness must be observed in the laboratory. Trash must be properly disposed.

5.8. Unauthorized taking out of any utensil or equipment is considered a major offense with corresponding disciplinary action. 6. Drawing Rooms There are two drawing rooms located on the second floor of Fr. Palma Building. Each room contains sixteen drawing tables and is provided with necessary drawing tools. Rules and Regulations on the Use of the Drawing Room: 6.1. Only students with drawing subjects are allowed to use the room and borrow drawing instruments. 6.2. Borrowed instruments should be used only inside the drawing room. 6.3. Students must maintain the orderliness and cleanliness of the drawing room. 6.4. Students are responsible for any damage or loss of the instruments and tables assigned to them. 7. Cassetti Mini-Hotel The mini-hotel is one of the laboratories for THRM students. It has a front office, a reception area, a tourism office, two standard bedrooms with comfort rooms, a suite complete with a receiving area, a kitchen, comfort room, porch and household appliances and furnishings. Rules and Regulations on the Use of the Cassetti Mini-Hotel: 7.1. The management is not responsible for any loss of personal properties.

7.2. Guests and students should not move furnishings or interfere with the electrical network or any other installations in the hotel. 7.3. Equipment and appliances should be turned off before leaving. 7.4. Order and cleanliness must be observed in the mini-hotel. Trash must be properly disposed. 7.5. Students are responsible for any damage or loss in the mini-hotel. 8. Hotel and Restaurant Management Laboratory Together with the Mini-Hotel, the HRM laboratory is used to facilitate the learning of skills associated with restaurant management. It is adjacent to the Munch Canteen and is provided with the necessary equipment for restaurant operations. The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the HRM Laboratory: 8.1. Students must wear the prescribed laboratory uniform during working sessions. 8.2. Students are required to stay in their assigned working areas. 8.3. Cleanliness and orderliness must be maintained in the laboratory. 9. Caregiving Laboratory This is located adjacent to AvignoneClinic and is equipped with training facilities for Caregiving and Health Care services. The following rules and regulations must be observed in the Caregiving Laboratory: 9.1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their Caregiving class.

9.2. Students should wear proper attire while doing the activities in the laboratory. 9.3. Care must be observed while using the equipment in the laboratory. In case a student or a group of students accidentally or intentionally breaks a piece of equipment, the said student or group is required to replace it. 9.4. Order and cleanliness must be observed in the laboratory. Trash must be properly disposed of.

The home shall fully support the school in the implementation of the total school program - curricular and co-curricular - toward the proper physical, social, intellectual and moral development of the child. -Article76. The Child and Youth Welfare Code (Presidential Decree No. 603, s. 1974)

1. The rules and regulations of RC as stated in this Handbook are intended to enhance the life in school of an RC student as he/she relates and interacts with the members of the school community. As such, it is understood that they are mutual good role models of each other. 2. It is the duty and responsibility of the parents and/or guardians to keep track of the progress of their children/wards in school. The parents and/or guardians are encouraged to confer with the school authorities at their own volition or whenever calls for conference are issued to them. This is to enhance the harmonious working relationship between the school and the home for the welfare of the student. 3. The enrollment of a student in RC is taken as an expressed willingness on his/her part, and consequently of his/her parents and/or guardians, to abide by all rules and regulations of the school. Thus, the student and his/her parents and/or guardians are committed to the strict observance of the same. 4. RC reserves the right to admit, readmit, refuse admission or exclude a student or drop the name of an erring student from the school rolls on the basis of his/her academic performance, conduct or attendance.

5. RC acknowledges its obligations to exercise reasonable supervision over the conduct of the student and to cultivate the best potentialities of the heart and mind of the student. Its role in “loco parentis” is the exercise of substitute parental authority over students in the school and in school-related activities (Civil Code, Art. 349). 6. RC, as a Catholic school, strongly respects and adheres to the practice of holy sacrament (matrimony) and does not tolerate sexual indiscretions. Violation of this policy would merit the student appropriate disciplinary action, including but not limited to, requiring the student to go on leave or will be excluded or dropped from the school rolls. 7. RC expects its students to uphold the standards of responsibility and dignity. When a student of RC does not measure up to these standards, he/she will be excluded or dropped from the school rolls after due process. 8. Students, either as individuals or as a group, must not use the name and seal of the school without official authorization. 9. Students who are using the social media in their respective homes are not to make inappropriate comments (including in private messages) about the school personnel or other students.

10. Parents or guardians may consult or confer with teachers and instructors provided they secure appointments with the Department Head (Principal, Dean or TED Head) two days before the actual date of appointment. 10.1 Concerns and/or complaints must be written and directly addressed to proper school authority rather than posting them on social media – whether on their own pages, in closed groups (e.g. groups set up for school parents to communicate with each other) or on the school's pages. Complaint posted on social media will not be entertained by the school. 11. Parents, guardians or visitors are not allowed to go to the classrooms. Messages and allowance for the students must be coursed through the Guidance Office. 12. Students may be called out of the classrooms provided an approved written permission/call slip is issued by either of the following: 12.1. Rector/Vice-Rector 12.2. Director for Academic Affairs (DAA) 12.3. Director for Student Services (DSS) 12.4. Director for Spiritual Affairs (DSA) 12.4. Principal/Dean/Technical Education Department Head (TED Head) 12.5. Vice Principal/Vice Dean 12.6. Guidance Counselor/Facilitator 12.7. Prefect of Discipline/Discipline Officer 12.8. Health Services Coordinator/Nurse

13. As a Catholic School, with Rogationist Formation as the core of the curriculum, RC requires all students to attend and pass all the requirements of Christian Living Education or Religious Education subjects. Students also need to attend masses and/or similar activities and complete spiritual recollections and retreats scheduled by the institution. In addition, parents of High School students are required to follow the agreement (to attend/participate in parents’ formation programs, PTA assemblies, etc.) signed during the enrolment of their children. 14. The “No ID, no entry” policy is strictly implemented. The school ID is required for the admittance of students and personnel to the school premises. For parents or other visitors, a visitor’s ID is issued by the guard in exchange for a valid identification card, which is returned after a legitimate business transaction or visit inside the campus. Visitors will be charged for lost visitor’s ID. 15. High School students will stay inside the campus from the moment of their arrival in the morning until their dismissal time in the afternoon. They cannot leave the school premises unless they have written permission from their parents and/or they have secured a gate pass from the Discipline Office duly noted by the Homeroom Adviser and approved by the Principal. In the absence of

both, the Prefect of Discipline signs the gate pass. In case of sickness/medical concern, the School Nurse will issue the gate pass. 16. The privacy of certain areas in the campus should be respected by the students. The areas where students are not allowed to stay or loiter are: 16.1. Religious community’s residence and interns’ dormitories 16.2. Refectory, kitchen, lavatory, and carpentry shop 16.3. All laboratories except during scheduled classes and/or when permitted by the Principal/Dean/TED Head 16.4. Fr. Vitale Administration Building, except for official business 16.5. Faculty rooms 16.6. High School classrooms, and corridors during recess, lunch and after dismissal time, unless under the supervision of a teacher or with specific permission from the Prefect of Discipline/Discipline Officer. 17. Everyone is enjoined to keep the campus clean at all times. Thus, littering is strictly prohibited. There are waste bins around the campus for proper waste disposal. 18. Everybody should respect, maintain and safeguard the school physical plant. Any damages must be reported immediately to the Office of the General Services. 19. Students are obliged to use English as a medium of communication.

20. Everyone is expected to be courteous and respectful at all times especially to visitors and treat others in a positive and considerate manner. 21. Students must exhibit proper behavior at all times in all places. When the behavior of a student adversely affects the integrity and objectives of the school, he will be subjected to disciplinary action. 22. Using the school website, official Facebook page, school publication, or LMS RC ID System, announcements are made from time to time to keep the students, parents/guardians abreast of school concerns and procedures. Students should relay to their parents all announcements which concern them. Likewise, the school gives out regular and/or timely communications or correspondence to parents. The parents are earnestly requested to acknowledge every communication by filling-up out the reply/return slips/parental consents and returning them to the school through their children. 23. Parents/Students/School Personnels are discouraged to post photos or videos that include other children at the school on their personal social media account. 24. In case of misunderstanding between or among the students, parents of the concerned students should not do any drastic action or in any way harass the other concerned students. Such occurrences will be settled according to the policies and guidelines stipulated in this handbook. In addition to this, cooperation of all stakeholders is needed to maintain and promote trust, respect, and dignity of all students, parents/guardians, teachers, and administrators of the school.

25. An activity permit signed by the teacher-in-charge, noted by the Student Affairs Coordinator, and approved by the Principal/Dean/TED Head must be secured by students at least two days before any school activity/practice during non-class days. This form which can be obtained from the Student Affairs Coordinator should be signed by their parents and returned to the teacher-in-charge a day before the approved activity/practice. In this way, parents are properly informed and could monitor their children’s activities. 26. Students who wish to participate in any outside activity as representatives of the school should secure approval from the school administration. 27. In cases of emergency, or for valid reasons, high school students may bring cellular phones or other gadgets provided there is a letter of permission from the parents. These gadgets will be surrendered to the subject teacher, adviser or discipline officer right after the morning assembly and will be retrieved after classes in the afternoonCollege students however, may bring their cellular phones but they should refrain from using these inside the classrooms, library or during school hours and liturgical celebrations.

28. High School students permitted to bring cellphone, laptop, netbook, camera or any gadget/device must deposit the gadget/device to the Office for Student Discipline or to the subject teacher during the first period. The gadget/device must be used only during the class activity and only by its owner. Unauthorized/improper use of a gadget/device may result in disciplinary action and confiscation of the gadget/device. A confiscated item shall be released only to the student’s parent/legal guardian. 29. Taking into consideration the educational system of RC and the promotion of an environment that is conducive to learning, the Discipline Officer, together with the subject teacher or adviser, may conduct inspection as the need arises. 30. Parents or students who wish to request for school forms or documents such as ESC Certificates, Form 137/ SF10, Certificate of Enrolment, Certificate of Grades, Certification of Good Moral Character and/or Rank, and Recommendation Letter, must apply for these at least a week before actual claim to give ample time for the preparation of such forms or documents. Formal request letter must be submitted to the concerned offices and attach proof of requirements. Online (e-mail) or phone call request may be accommodated provided that proof of requirement is presented upon claiming. A minimal amount will be charged.

31. In order to be allowed to enter the school premises, students’ vehicles/school service vehicles must have the official school sticker which may be secured at the Accounting Office. 32. The Office for Student Discipline will inform parents/guardians in writing about a student’s case and may require the parents to come personally for proper disposition of the said case. 33. Parents visiting the school are required to wear modest/proper clothes. 34. No students or visitors, including parents or guardians, shall be allowed inside the school building and the premises after the last class period has ended. (DepEd Order No. 11 s. 2011) 35. A student shall be responsible for informing his/her parents/guardians of the following: 35.1. School policies, and guidelines stated in this handbook. 35.2. Student’s academic standing and the possible consequences of his/her excessive absences, dropping, failures or gross misbehavior.

Classes are suspended in the following situations: 1. Typhoon warning signal is raised by PAGASA in the area of Cavite. Signal no. 2 automatically suspends classes in the secondary level while signal no. 3 automatically suspends classes in the tertiary level. Depending on signal numbers declared at 10:00 pm and 4:30 am of the following day, classes in appropriate levels for the whole day are deemed automatically cancelled/suspended. (DepEd Order No. 43 series 2012). 2. Natural calamities or disturbances compromising the safety of the students; 3. Rector’s announcement; 4. Cancellation of classes by DepEd, TESDA or CHED; 5. National, Provincial, and Municipal proclamations N.B. Afternoon classes in the appropriate levels in areas with signal numbers declared at 11:00 am that day will be cancelled or suspended at 2:00 pm to ensure the safety of the students and to provide ample time for the school authorities to contact school service providers and/or the parents. In addition to this, during heavy rains affecting the health or safety of their children, parents have the discretion not to send their children to school;

1. Tuition fees and other charges are prescribed by the school authorities. These charges are posted in the Bulletin of Information. 2. Parents and students enter into agreement with the school regarding the mode of payment of tuition and other fees. 3. It is the obligation of the parents and students to update themselves with regard to the status of their accounts by consulting the Finance and Administration Department 4. Examination permit for the JHS & SHS and by the Cashier for the College/TED students. This should be signed by the Cashier two weeks before each major examination. It is recommended that accounts be settled at least two weeks before the scheduled examination period to avoid inconvenience and delay. 5. Tuition fees and other charges for transferring or withdrawing students shall be governed by the following provisions:

When a student registers in a school, it is understood that he/she is enrolling for the entire school year for secondary courses. (DepEd Order No. 88 series 2010: Revised Manual of Regulations for Private Schools. Section 119. Rules for Registration) thus, a student who transfers or otherwise withdraws, in writing, within two weeks after the beginning of classes and who has already paid the pertinent tuition and other fees in full or for any length of time longer than one month may be charged 10% of the total amount due for the term if he withdraws within the 1^(st) week of classes, or 20% if within the 2^(nd) week of classes, regardless of whether or not he has actually attended classes. The student may be charged in full if he withdraws any time after the 2^(nd) week of classes. However, if the transfer or withdrawal is due to justifiable reason, the student shall be charged the pertinent fees only up to and including the last month of attendance.

For College students: Manual of Regulations for Private Higher Education Section 100. Tuition Charges – A student who transfers or otherwise withdraws, in writing, within two weeks after the beginning of classes and who has already paid the pertinent tuition and other fees in full or for any length of time longer than one month may be charged 25% of the total amount due for the term if he withdraws within the 1^(st) week of classes, or 50% if within the 2^(nd) week of classes, regardless of whether or not he has actually attended classes. The student may be charged all the school fees in full if he withdraws any time after the 2^(nd) week of classes.

Junior High School Department Vision The Junior High School Department is a leading secondary educational community dedicated to the holistic formation of the students in faith love and wisdom inspired by the ideals of St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia. Mission Integrate the school’s VMG to the learning instruction; - Offer a balanced curriculum through the integration of spiritual, social, cultural, technical and academic programs; - Provide student formative programs gearing towards development of life long skills and socially oriented citizens; - Nurture the value of charity through students’ exposure to socially relevant activities; and - Promote a culture of prayer and deep appreciation of the importance of vocation.

Admission for incoming Grade 7 students is open to all elementary graduates with satisfactory academic qualification (a final average of at least 80% in the Grade 6 report card), intellectual ability (average I.Q.), normal personality and good conduct (conduct grade of Satisfactory/Good/B/85). The Junior High School Department accepts transferees who meet the requirements and pass the screening process for Grades 8, 9 and 10 provided there are available slots. Grades 8, 9 and 10 applicants should have at least Approaching Proficiency (80% – 84%) general average in the previous grade level and good conduct (conduct grade of Satisfactory/Good /B/85). Prior to the admission, the school may require a list of documents or clearances for evaluation with regard to character or medical history of a student. Only until the student has completed all admission requirements shall he/she be considered officially enrolled. I. Admission Procedure for Grade 7 Applicants 1. Application for Entrance Test 1.1. Secure an application form from the Registrar’s Office. This form is free of charge and can be photocopied. 1.2. Fill-out the form completely and attach: 1.2.1. a clear photocopy of the applicant’s Grade 5 and latest Grade 6 report cards

1.2.2. two (2) pieces of 2x2 colored I.D. pictures (with white background and name tag) 1.3. Pay the testing fee to the Cashier. 1.4. Submit the form with the above requirements and receipt to the Registrar’s Office. Thereafter, a test permit indicating the schedule of entrance test will be issued to the applicant. 1.5. Entrance examinations usually start on the 4^(th) Saturday of October and every Saturday thereafter until April. 1.6. Applicants should report on their scheduled examination date at least 10 minutes earlier than their scheduled examination time. They should bring the test permit, pencil and eraser. 1.7. Applicants should follow-up on the application two weeks after taking the examination. A list of qualifiers and other possible candidates will be posted on the bulletin boards. 1.8. Qualified Grade 7 applicants will be advised to report for pre-enrolment. 2. Pre-enrollment Qualified incoming Grade 7 students and their parents who are interested to push through with their application have to confirm personally their intention of reserving their slot for the next school year. They must follow the following procedure: 2.1. Fill-out the registration form, medical interview form, guidance folder and ID application form;

2.2. Report to the school nurse for the medical interview; 2.3. Submit the Guidance folder to the Guidance Office and get the interpretation of test results; 2.4. Proceed to the Office of the Principal for interview. 2.5. Pay a non-refundable reservation fee, which is deductible from the total tuition fee upon enrolment. 2.6. Get the List of Requirements for Enrollment from the Registrar’s Office. 3. Enrollment Enrollment usually falls on the last week of April. Pre-enrollees or pre-registrants have to report with their parents on the scheduled dates and submit the following requirements: 3.1. Original Grade 6 report card, duly signed by the parents and the Grade School Principal 3.2. A photocopy of PSA Birth Certificate 3.3. A photocopy of Elementary School Graduation Certificate 3.4. Four (4) pieces of 2”x2” colored I.D. pictures (with white background and name tag) 3.5. Medical Certificates/Immunization Record for those with health concerns or special conditions 3.6. Full or partial payment of school fees II. Admission Procedure for Transferees 1. Application 1.1. Entrance examinations for transferees usually start on the 2^(nd) Thursday of February and every Thursday thereafter until May.

1.2. Transfer applicants for Grade 8 must present to the Registrar a clear photocopy of Report Cards. Those applying for; 1.2.1. Grade 8 - Grade 6 and latest Grade 7 Report Cards 1.2.2. Grade 9 - Grade 7 and latest Grade 8 Report Cards 12.3. Grade 10 - Grade 8 and latest Grade 9 Report Cards. 1.3. Transfer applicants will undergo preliminary interview with the Principal. After passing the interview, the applicants can proceed with their application. 1.4 Secure an application form from the Registrar’s Office. 1.5. Fill out the form completely and attach: 1.5.1. clear photocopy of required Report Cards 1.5.2. original Good Moral Character Certificate 1.5.3. two (2) pieces of 2x2 colored I.D. pictures (with white background and name tag) 1.5.4. accomplished RC Recommendation Form from previous school’s Principal or Counselor 1.5.5. ESC Certificate (for Grantees) 1.6. Pay the testing fee at the Cashier’s Office. 1.7. Submit the form with the above requirements and receipt to the Registrar’s Office and wait for the test permit. 1.8. Report for testing on the date specified in the test permit issued.

1.9. Result of test will be released two weeks after the date of examination. Qualified transfer-applicants will then be informed of the date of pre-enrolment. 2. Pre-enrollment Qualified transfer applicants must follow the following procedure: 2.1. Report to the Registrar’s Office and fill out the Pre-enrolment and medical forms and guidance folder. 2.2. Report for interview with the Vice-Principal / Principal, Guidance Counselor/Facilitator, and Nurse. 2.3. Pay the reservation fee at the Cashier’s Office. 2.4. Submit the completed forms to the Registrar and get a copy of the steps to be followed and list of requirements for enrolment. 3. Enrollment On the scheduled date of enrolment, qualified transfer-applicants must present to the Registrar the following requirements: 3.1. Original Grade 7, Grade 8 or Grade 9 Report Card, duly signed by the parents and the School Principal 3.2. A photocopy of PSA Birth Certificate 3.3. Four (4) pieces of 2”x2” colored I.D. pictures (with white background and name tag) 3.4. Medical Certificate/Immunization Record for those with health problems or special conditions 3.5. Full or partial payment of school fees 3. Application

3.1. Foreign/Filipino student-applicants must present to the Registrar a clear photocopy of their credentials or certified true copy of their scholastic records. 3.2. Foreign/Filipino student-applicants will undergo a preliminary interview with the Principal to evaluate the subjects they have finished abroad before they can secure an application form. After passing the interview, the applicants can proceed with their application. 3.3. Secure an application form from the Registrar’s Office. 3.4. Fill-out the form completely and attach: 3.4.1. clear photocopy of required credentials 3.4.2. original Good Moral Character Certificate/Recommendation Form 3.4.3. two (2) pieces of 2x2 colored I.D. pictures (with white background and name tag) 3.5. Pay the testing fee at the Cashier’s Office. 3.6 Submit the form with the above requirements and receipt to the Registrar’s Office and wait for the test permit. 3.7 Report for testing on the date specified in the test permit issued. 3.8 Result of test will be released two weeks after the date of exam. 3.9 Qualified Foreign/Filipino student-applicants will then be informed of the date of pre-enrolment. 4. Pre-enrolment and Enrolment All qualified Foreign/Filipino student-applicants must follow the same procedure as that for transferees.

IV. Admission Procedure for Old Students All old students are required to submit SF 9 (report card) duly signed by parents for enrolment. V. Admission Procedure for Returning Students Only former students of Rogationist College who were not advised to transfer and who wish to re-enroll may do so. They should follow the same procedure as that for the transfer-applicants. VI. Temporary Enrolment (DepEd Order No. 3 s. 2018) Students from public or private schools in the Philippines who failed to submit the SF9 (formerly Form 138) during early registration or upon enrolment shall only be temporarily enrolled until the submission of required documents on or before August 31^(st) of the current school year. They shall be required to submit an Affidavit of Undertaking, signed by the parent/guardian in order to be temporarily enrolled. For temporarily enrolled students, RC shall issue a Temporary Progress Report Card signed by the Homeroom Adviser for the parents/guardians to monitor the progress of his/her child. This form is inadmissible for transfer and enrollment purposes and is only issued for progress monitoring. Upon complete submission of the documentary requirements, the student shall be tagged as officially enrolled in the LIS. Otherwise, the student retains the status of temporarily enrolled; the student cannot be officially promoted to a higher grade level, and the student cannot officially graduate from the school. The student will not be recognized should he/she attain the qualifying average and other criteria for academic honors, and RC shall not release official documents such as the SF 10, Certificate of Completion, Diploma, etc.

VII. Provisional Enrolment (DepEd Order No. 88 s. 2010) In meritorious cases as may be determined by the private school concerned, a student without any appropriate admission or transfer credentials may be provisionally enrolled, allowed to attend classes and to earn credits for the subject or subjects he/she is enrolled in during the school year. The provisional enrolment of the student shall be conditioned on the submission of his/her valid admission or transfer credentials on or before the last day of the school year. A provisionally-enrolled student shall not be enrolled for the next higher grade, course or level for the next succeeding school term, if he/she cannot submit his/her valid admission of transfer credentials on or before the period specified herein, and whatever credits for the subject or subjects he/she may have passed shall not be recognized. VIII. Late Enrolment (DepEd Order No. 3, s. 2018) RC may accept late enrollees provided that the student will be able to meet 80% of the prescribed number of school days for each school year and the quarterly requirement to pass the grade level as governed by the latest existing applicable DepEd issuances.

If the student cannot meet the required number of school days and the quarterly requirement, the Principal may exercise his/her discretion to accept the enrollee and implement make-up activities or interventions under acceptable circumstances. IX. Students Moving In/Out (DepEd Order No. 3, s 2018) Students from other schools who enrolled in RC in the middle of the school year shall be tagged in the system as “moved in”, while students who were previously enrolled in the school but enrolled in other schools in the middle of the school year shall be tagged in the system as “moved out”. Students may move in/out from one school to another school anytime during the school year for valid reasons such as, but not limited to, family migration and disaster, among others. Students who fail to submit the necessary requirements upon moving in shall be considered temporarily enrolled. The guidelines on temporary enrolment shall apply. X. Invalid Enrolment (DepEd No. 3 s. 2018) Unless otherwise specifically authorized by the Secretary of Education, the enrollment of any student who is under a term of suspension or expulsion, of the enrollment of any student from a school or course without government authority shall not be valid.

2. Based on Attendance A student who incurs absences of more than twenty (20%) percent of the prescribed number of class or laboratory periods during the school year or term should be given a failing grade and given no credit for the course or subject,

section_title: GUIDELINES AND CONDITIONS ON MONITORING/PROBATION STATUS
content: RC education is for all students who can maintain its standards of academic excellence and exemplary conduct. It requires a high degree of achievement from its students. Thus, a student who does not meet the standards set by the school is put on a probationary status. Probation is a period of time designed to ascertain the ability of a student to abide by the academic and conduct standards of the school. I. Academic Probation Status Academic Probation status is a formal warning or reminder that carries with it a condition that improvement in terms of academic achievement is necessary for readmission and/or promotion. This is given to a student so that he will show improvement during the school year. 1.1. Academic Probation is given to a student who has shown below average academic performance in the previous school year. It is a status imposed on a student whose final general average is below 82%. 1.2. The student on Academic Probation is required to maintain good grades (no failing marks in any subject) and to have a final general average of at least 82% in order for his/her status to change to that of a regular student the following school year.

section_title: GUIDELINES AND CONDITIONS ON MONITORING/PROBATION STATUS
content: 1.3. Failure on the part of the student to show definite improvement or abide by the academic standards of the school within the school year would mean non-readmission for the following school year. 1.4. A student placed on Academic Probation for an incoming school year shall not be eligible for any higher elective and/or appointive position in any varsity team, club or organization subject to the discretion of the Rector. II. Conduct Monitoring Status 1. A student is placed on Conduct Monitoring after incurring a series of minor offenses during a school year. 2. If a student commits other minor offenses or a major offense during the monitoring period, his/her status will be elevated to conduct probation for the current school year. 3. The Conduct Monitoring status may be lifted the following school year if the student shows satisfactory improvement in his/her behavior. III. Conduct Probation Status 1. A student is placed on Conduct Probation after committing a major offense. 2. A student placed on Conduct Probation for an incoming school year shall not be eligible for any elective and/or appointive position in any varsity team, club or organization subject to the discretion of the Rector.

section_title: GUIDELINES AND CONDITIONS ON MONITORING/PROBATION STATUS
content: 3. If a student placed on Conduct Probation commits a series of minor offenses or a major offense, he/she may be dismissed in the following school year or he/she may be dismissed immediately. 4. The Conduct Probation status may be lifted after a school year if the student shows remarkable improvement in his/her behavior.

An RC student on his/her last year in the Junior High School Department should have satisfactorily completed all academic and other requirements prescribed by the school in order to qualify as a candidate for the Completion Rites.

1. A grade 10 student will not be permitted to participate in the Completion Rites for any of the following reasons: 1.1. He/She fails in one or more subjects. 1.2. He/She lacks units or subjects required for graduation under the Rogationist College High School curriculum. 1.3. He/She has incurred absences of more than 20% of the prescribed number of school days during the school year. 1.4. He/She has committed an offense meriting the penalty of non-participation in the Completion Rites. 1.5. He/She did not pass the assessment given by the institution and/or TESDA after completion of the chosen TLE training program 2. All Grade 10 in the Junior high school department are required to attend the rehearsals for the Baccalaureate Mass and Completion Rites. These are the regulations set by the school in relation to the attendance of completers to rehearsals: 2.1. A grade 10 participating in the Completion Rites rehearsals should be in complete uniform or should follow the required dress code. Failure to do so shall be considered an unexcused absence. 2.2. A grade 10 shall be allowed a maximum of 2 unexcused

absences. Exceeding this allowable number of absences shall automatically ban the student from participating in the Completion Rites. 2.3. Honors, awards and/or diplomas may be withheld unless the Principal is informed in advance about the reasons for the student’s inability to attend the rehearsals. For those with unexcused absence, release of the above mentioned documents will be after a make up for the number of days of absence.

Scholarships granted by the school are percentage discounts which apply only to the tuition fee. 1. Scholarship for Incoming Grade 7 students This is a 100% tuition fee scholarship grant given by the Rogationist College Junior High School Department to an incoming Grade 7 student who graduated with first honors, or who received the highest academic award in an elementary school with at least 200 graduates. 2. Highest Scholastic Achievement Scholarship This is a tuition fee discount granted to the three students with the highest general academic average in each grade level after one year stay. 2.1. Rank 1 – 75% 2.2. Rank 2 – 50% 2.3. Rank 3 – 25% 3. Employee’s Legal Dependents’ Discount All full-time employees who have rendered at least 1 year of service to the SABV and RC are entitled to 50% tuition fee discount in Rogationist College for all their legal dependents/beneficiaries. Legal dependents/beneficiaries would mean the employee’s brothers, sisters and children 18 years and below, subject to the following conditions: a. Dependent’s age upon their enrolment should be 18 years and below. b. Tuition fee discounts shall only be granted for a period no longer than the duration of the course/program in which the beneficiary has originally enrolled.

4. Family Discount For brothers and sisters enrolled at the same time within a school year, the 2^(nd) child and each of the succeeding children enrolling will receive a 5% discount. This discount does not apply to employees of SABV and RC. 5. St. Anthony’s Boys Village Grantees’ and Interns’ Discount This is granted to less-privileged youths chosen by the SABV community. According to the by-laws of SABV-RC, the interns are considered children or beneficiaries of the Institution who are entitled to receive the benefit of 50% discount in the tuition fee. N.B. In case a student qualifies for two or more scholarships, grants or aids, the one with the highest benefit applies. No monetary refund will be allowed.

I. Academic Programs 1. Enrichment and Enhancement Program Each subject area organizes activities that provide opportunities for the students to show and develop their talents and potentials. These may be in the form of theatrical plays, song compositions, debates, quiz bee and other competitions. The activity program with its co-curricular activities likewise gives the students a chance to be more creative, resourceful and progressive in their field of interest. 2. Remedial and Tutorial Program The school offers remedial program for students in all subjects. A special program for Filipino and AralingPanlipunan is designed for foreign students or students returning from abroad. The tutorial program is offered to students to help them improve their academic performance. The tutorial sessions and remedial classes shall be conducted at the Rogationist College on the agreed dates and time schedules within the actual school year. Arrangement can be done with the Vice- Principal and specific guidelines will be given to the students and their parents. 3. Technology and Livelihood Education (TLE) Program TLE subjects are offered to high school students to equip them with basic technical skills in the different trade areas. Grade 7 students have exploratory subjects in TLE such as, Automotive, Electrical and Dressmaking. For Grade 8 students, the TLE offerings are Caregiving, Cookery. Automotive Servicing, and Technical Drafting SMAW (Shielded Metal Arc Welding), Electronics, Caregiving and Drafting. Grade 9 students are given the chance to choose their TLE subject specialization, which they will continue until Grade 10. The following are the Offerings for TLE specialization:

3.1. Automotive 3.2. Caregiving 3.3. Cookery 3.4. Computer Servicing 3.5. Technical Drafting 3.6. Electrical 3.7. Electronics Grade 10 students must pass the assessment given by TESDA after completion of the training program, which is a requirement for inclusion of the students in the Junior High School’s Completion Rite. 4. Christian Enhancement Program The school offers Christian Living Education subject in all year levels. It is required as an academic subject for spiritual and moral formation. This is handled by CLE subject teachers in collaboration with the Campus Ministry under the Office of Spiritual Affairs. This program includes First Friday Masses, monthly confessions, confirmation, retreats recollections and seminars. II. Academic Policies 1. Types of Assessment (DepEd Order # 8 s. 2015: Policy Guidelines on Classroom Assessment of the Basic Education Program) 1.1. Formative Assessment - is given at any time during the teaching and learning process. Also known as ‘Assessment for Learning”, it can be used by the teacher to make adjustments in their instruction while it can also be used by students as ‘assessment as learning’ so that they can reflect on their own progress.

1.2. Summative Assessment – also known as assessment of learning is given at the end of a particular unit “… measures whether learners have met the content and performance standards. There are three components that teachers should use in this type of assessment: Written Work, Performance Tasks and Quarterly Assessments/Examinations. Distribution of these components varies depending on the subject. However, Rogationist College includes Mini-Tasks as scaffolds for the Performance tasks. Likewise, the Cognitive Process Dimensions by Anderson and Kratwohl (2001) such as remembering, understanding, applying, analyzing, evaluating and creating are also being used in this assessment especially in the quarterly assessments/examinations. 1.2.1. For the Mini-tasks and Performance tasks, students are informed at the start of the quarter and provided time for performance task making/presentation. Teachers also give the following guides to students to ensure that they correctly make these mini-tasks and performance tasks; - Title of the Assessment Activity - Date of Submission/Presentation - Guidelines/Mechanics of the Activity - Criteria/Rubric - Documentation/ Evaluation & Sample evidences of the Performance Task/Assessment Activity Weight of the Components for Grades 7 to 10:

Interventions based on Assessment Results per DepEd Order # 8 s. 2015, V. Item C. “ When the learner’s raw scores are consistently below expectations in Written Work and Performance tasks, the learner’s parents or guardians must be informed not later than the fifth week of the quarter.” In RC JHS Department, parents are updated of their child’s performance through a letter. Parents are required to sign all written quizzes, seat works, exercises, long tests and quarterly exams of their child. Should the student fail or get a low mark in the assessments, or did not fully understand the lessons, he/she must attend remediation.

Parents are encouraged to confer with teachers, through the Office of the Vice Principal, to discuss the child’s performance and come to an agreement on how both parties can help the learner improve his/her performance. For School Year 2020 -2021, parents are given access codes in Schoology for them to keep track of their child’s attendance, performance and activities. Likewise, constant communication by the Homeroom Adviser, Guidance Counselor/Facilitator, Discipline Officer and Vice-Principal is observed within the quarter. 3. Grading System RC uses a standards- and competency-based grading system as mandated in the K to 12 Basic Education Program (DepEd Order No. 8, s. 2015). A student’s grade is based on the weighted raw score of his/her summative assessments. The minimum grade needed to pass a specific learning area is 60, which is transmuted to 75 in the report card. The lowest mark that can appear on the report card is 65 for Quarterly Grades and Final grades. At the end of the school year, students’ grades are computed by getting the average of the Quarterly Grades (QG) and this is considered as the Final Grade.

Benefits of Students Who Join Academic Competitions outside the School Due recognition and benefits are given to students who are sent to various off-campus academic competitions as representatives of the school.

General Rule: 1. Students who undergo training for a day or more will be exempted from the seatwork/quizzes and assignments during training and competition days. 2. However, they still need to do their performance tasks, and take their summative tests for them to prepare for their quarterly exams. They can avail remedial classes if needed.

1. If the student competed in the 1^(st) quarter, the benefit will take effect in the 2^(nd) quarter. (If it’s within the time frame, it can still be considered). 2. A student who reaches the second level (of the competition) or higher will be given recognition during the Honor’s Assembly. 5. Report Card (School Form 9 or SF 9) The report card is an official document of the school that shows the student’s performance per quarter. Report Cards are distributed every quarter. These are given to the parents during the 1^(st), 3^(rd) and 4^(th) quarters and to the students every 2^(nd) quarter. Parent-Teacher Conference (PTC) usually happens during report Card Distribution except for the 2^(nd) quarter which happens on a Saturday after the distribution or if the family has been scheduled for Home Visitation. Parents are encouraged to confer with teachers and/or other school authorities during the regular Parent-Teacher Conference. 6. Loss of Report Card Any student who loses his/her report card can request for a replacement at the Registrar’s Office. The cost shall be charged to the student. 7. On Examinations

7.1. Quarterly (periodic) examinations in all subjects are administered within a span of 3 half-days such that a maximum of three subjects are given in each half-day, one hour for each subject. 7.2. Schedule of quarterly examination is posted on the bulletin of information as well as written in the student diary. Students must strictly follow these schedules. 7.3. Examination Room Assignment is posted in all classrooms a day before the examination period. 7.4. Examination permits are required during all quarterly examinations and submitted to the homeroom adviser within one week before the examination days. 7.5. Students must be in the examination room five minutes before the scheduled examination. They should bring only necessary things for the exam. Other school materials should be at the lockers. 7.6. Students should observe absolute silence in the examination room and adjoining corridors. 7.7. Students are expected to observe all examination rules enforced by the Room Examiners such as: 7.7.1. Be seated on their assigned seats 7.7.2 No borrowing of materials 7.7.3. No talking to seat mate or Room Examiner as soon as the examination starts

7.7.4. No eating 7.7.5. No loitering along the corridors or 15 meters around the examination rooms 7.7.6. No one is allowed to leave the examination room once the examination has started 7.7.7. Bags, notes and other materials not to be used during the examinations must be placed on the platform upon entering the examination room. 7.7.8. Questions to proctors are not allowed except for corrections in the test questions and missing pages of the test papers 7.7.9. Clarifications may be directed only to Room Examiners/Room Supervisors assigned in different examination areas. Note: Failure to observe any one of items 7.7.1 to 7.7.9 is considered an offense and therefore subjects the student to disciplinary action. 7.8. Special Examinations A student who fails to take the scheduled quarterly examination must secure a special examination permit from the Principal upon submission of an excuse letter from the parent/ guardian. If the reason for failure to take the examination is illness, a medical certificate must be attached to the excuse letter. A minimal fee per subject will be charged. Upon payment of this fee, the Principal approves the permit. Special examinations are facilitated in the Guidance Testing Room.

8. Moratorium on Student Co-curricular Activities All co-curricular activities are suspended one (1) week before the examinations so that the students can concentrate on their preparation for the examinations. 9. Guidelines in Technology Integration and Use of Gadgets Rationale The use of Technology in classroom instruction has proved to be very helpful in the teaching-learning process. Several studies have proven that integration of technology has made the student performance higher. However, another study shows that integration of technology will reach its optimal effect only if the teachers are trained to utilize such and will maximize its use in the classroom. Likewise, another study shows that too much use of technology may hamper student’s learning as this may also be detrimental to their health especially if not regulated. It is in this premise, that Rogationist College Junior High School Department has established guidelines in Technology Integration and Use of gadgets not only in the school but also in the classroom. Nature

Several technological instructional aids (projectors and televisions) and even the internet (Wifi connection)are provided in the school and are installed in the classrooms/hallways, hence, maximum utilization of such is encouraged. However, other gadgets/devices may also be utilized inside and outside the classroom both for teachers and students provided that they are used solely for documentation and teaching- learning process. Generally, students are not allowed to bring and use gadgets in school except if there is a valid reason or at times when the activity organizers, upon the approval of the administration, allow its use. However, sense of responsibility on both parties is encouraged. The school will not be liable for any damage or loss of a gadget not reported/surrendered in proper authorities. Proper sanction/administrative action will also be served for student/teacher who does not subscribe to this rule. The use of Facebook, Messenger, games and other applications are blocked in school premises so that students and personnel may not be distracted from their work and study. Guidelines for Students Generally, students are not allowed to bring and use gadgets in school However, this will not apply if such will be used in activities related to academics. The following guidelines should be followed:

1. Students may be allowed to bring and use the said gadgets provided that parents are informed of its use and the students will present a written permission by the parents (with specified purposes/subjects) to be signed by the subject teacher. 2. Students who brought the required gadgets should surrender the gadgets to their subject teacher concerned before the morning assembly or after the 1^(st) period if the class involved will be in the first period. 3. He/She should log-in/out in the Gadget Depository Log and secure the Permitted Gadget Form from the teacher. The gadget Depository Log should be place on a visible/accessible place if in case the teacher is not available when the student deposits or retrieves his/her gadget. 4. Should the gadget be used in multiple subjects in different schedule, he should let the subject teacher sign before and after each use of the gadget during their class. He/She should deposit it to the last teacher from which the student used the gadget. (for editing, need suggestion from the Department) 10. Student Clearance Clearance should be accomplished by all students every end of the school year. A Grade 10 student should be cleared from all financial obligations and administrative accountabilities from the different offices before a transcript of records, Certificate of Completion, and other similar documents are issued to him/her.For Grades 7, 8 and 9 students, the completed clearance form is needed in order for them to get their final grades and to enroll.

11. Withholding of Credentials (DepEd Order No. 88 s. 2010) The release of the transfer credentials of any student may be withheld for reasons of suspension, expulsion or nonpayment of financial obligations or property responsibility of the student to the school. The credentials shall be released as soon as his/her obligation shall have been settled or the penalty of suspension or expulsion lifted. VIII. Guidelines in Giving Student Awards Rogationist College gives quarterly and annual awards to outstanding students who have distinguished themselves in Academics, Diligence, Conduct, and Leadership. Special Awards related to co-curricular activities are also given. These awards are given to promote the educational development and personal growth of students in the fields of intellectual, behavioral and affective formation. The highest award given by the institution is the Rogate Award. The following criteria shall be used in determining the awards:
Academic Award will be given to the following:

All students who obtained a general average of 90% & above, have a satisfactory mark in conduct and not have a grade lower than 85% in any of the learning areas will be given a certificate of academic excellence at the end of the quarter with the following specifications: 98-100 – With Highest Honors 95-97 – With High Honors 90-94 – With Honors

All students who obtained a general average of 90% & above, have a satisfactory mark in conduct and not have a grade lower than 85% in any of the learning area in any quarter will be given medals at the end of the school year with the following specifications: 98-100 – With Highest Honors (Gold Medal) 95-97 – With High Honors (Silver Medal) 94. – With Honors (Bronze Medal)

This award shall be given to students who manifest remarkable and positive attitude towards education and the learning process. They must possess a natural desire and willingness to learn and to be educated and must have the personal initiative to improve their understanding and comprehension of the lessons. 2.1. Quarterly Awardees are determined by the following procedure: 2.1.1. In the first quarter, advisers and teachers nominate and rank the candidates per class for the award. The nominees should have satisfactory performance with Approaching Proficiency (AP) as the lowest rating in any learning area. Out of the nominees per class, only the top three student awardees will receive certificates. 2.1.2. In the succeeding quarters (second and third), nominees’ quarterly averages should have improved and they must not have a rating lower than Approaching Proficiency (AP). Standard deviation is applied to the difference between quarterly marks. The top three ranking students per class per quarter will receive the certificates. 2.2. Annual Quarterly awardees will automatically become candidates for the annual awards. Other candidates can be nominated as long as their averages have improved remarkably and consistently until the finals. The top three ranking student awardees per year level will receive the medals. However, the number of awardees may vary depending on how many among the candidates have met the set criteria.

This award shall be given to students who manifest exemplary human behavior and who meet the highest standards of good character and discipline set by the school. They must have conducted themselves in conformity with the school rules and regulations. The rating for conduct shall be based on the four core values (,Integrity-25%, Excellence-25%, Love of God and Neighbor-25%, Patriotism-25%). Awardees shall be determined from the computed averages of conduct marks given by the subject teachers. The core values should be manifested by each of the awardees through the following:

He/She influences his/her fellow students to visit and pray in the chapel, lead his/her fellow students in prayers, show positive attitude in dealings with fellow students, exercise charity throughout the department, and refrains from anger when faced by difficult circumstances.

He/She shows pride and honor in being a true Filipino. He/She also actively involveshimself/herself in school’s flag ceremony and other school programs which promote nationalism. He/Shealso abides by the rules and regulations sets in the school and his/hercommunity. He/She also upholds Filipino virtues such as respect for the elderly, righteousness and pakikisama.

He/She gives healthy opinions and sound views during class or group discussions. He/She also exercises responsibility over tasks performed in and outside the classroom.He/She also demonstrates honesty at all times and acts as a good role model to fellow students. He/She also hold on to his/her moral beliefs.

He/She uses his/her free time to help other students understand difficult lessons. He/She also complies with all the school requirements on time. He/She also shows outstanding performance in academics and behavioral concerns. He/She is also respected by fellow students and highly regarded by teachers and school personnel. 4. Leadership Award This annual award is given to any graduating student who has exemplified outstanding leadership qualities during his/her four years of stay in Rogationist College. The awardee shall be chosen from the nominees presented by the teachers. The following are the criteria set in choosing a nominee for the award: 4.1. An elected school, club or class officer 4.2. Has manifested the following traits during his/her term of office: - Honesty - Decisiveness - Responsibility - Obedience - Promptness - Affability/Friendliness - Community-orientedness 4.3. has no failing grades in any of the learning areas 4.4. has not committed any major offense 5. Rogate Award This is the highest honor Rogationist College bestows on any of its graduating students. The award goes to whoever best exemplifies the spirit and ideals of Saint Hannibal Mary Di Francia. The awardee should meet the following requirements:

5.1. Belongs to the graduating class. 5.2. Must have stayed for four years in Rogationist College. 5.3. Prays for and promotes vocation. 5.4. Cares for the poor. 5.5. Must have an academic average of Very Satisfactory or better in every grade level (no grade lower than 85% in all grade levels, in all quarters as reflected in the report card (excellence) 5.6. Must have conducted himself/herself in conformity with the school rules and regulations (no conduct grade below 85% in al quarters, in all grade levels as reflected in the report card). Thus, those with Satisfactory (S) or lower conduct grades in any of the quarters of their stay in the school are automatically disqualified. In selecting the Rogate Awardee, the following are observed; 3. The short list of candidates is to be passed by the Honor’s Committee to the School Board. 4. Candidates shall submit an essay to the School Board (specific topic to be determined by the School Board) 5. The School Board shall conduct an individual or panel interview with the candidates before determining the student to be awarded.

N.B. Without a qualified candidate, no award will be given. Guidelines on the Selection of Honor Students In giving due recognition to students who have shown exemplary performance, the following guidelines shall be observed: 1. Any member of the non-graduating/graduating classes shall be a candidate for honors if he/she meets the criteria specified in the Annual Award/s. 2. An honor selection committee shall be created and chaired by the Principal to screen and select honor students. The committee shall be composed of: teacher-representative from each year level, the Vice-Principal and the Prefect of Discipline. The final deliberations of the selection committee shall be approved by the Director for Academic Affairs. 3. The presence of the principal, parents of the candidates for honors, candidates for honors, and the members of the honors committee is required during the deliberation. 4. The Principal shall make the final announcement of honor students after the approval of the Director for Academic Affairs and information to the Rector. 5. Any clarifications are entertained only during or right after the deliberation and before the final announcement of the results.

The Student Activity Program is based on the school’s objectives of developing the students’ cultural competence and social responsibility. Student activities provide experiences and opportunities for skills and values development of students in support of the academic program. They help in maximizing their potentialities by promoting self-actualization and fostering holistic growth and development. Rogationist College encourages students to join these school activities. I. Guidelines on Student Activity Program 1. All teachers, homeroom advisers and club moderators are required to submit a work plan of their activities before the start of each school year. Major activities, especially those which will entail monetary collections require written approval from the Principal, Director for Finance and Administration and the Rector. 2. Students are required to belong to a club or organization provided they pass the criteria for membership. 3. Organization of any activity prejudicial to the welfare of the students and the interest of the school is not allowed. Any group that wishes to start a new club/organization should submit a letter addressed to the Rector through the Principal and recommended by the DSS. The letter must contain the goals and the structure of the proposed new club/organization.

4. Holding of homeroom, academic and club activities must be properly coordinated with the SAC, Principal, Prefect of Discipline and the DSS/DAA/OGS. Reservations of venues, equipment and other materials needed for the activities should be facilitated by the adviser or moderator at least two weeks before their schedule. 5. Student Activities are usually done outside class hours. Extra-ordinary sessions which require calling students from their classes must have the permission of the Principal. 6. At the end of each school year, all clubs and organizations are required to submit a year-end report which includes the minutes of the meetings, attendance, updated list of members and officers, financial statement, documentation, evaluation tools, results of evaluations conducted and work plans. 7. Acquired funds of the clubs must be turned over to the Finance and Administration Office at the end of the school year. These will be transferred to the next moderator with the approval of the DFA. 8. Students are encouraged to participate in worthwhile activities outside of the school. Invitation to such kind of activities is endorsed by the club moderators to the SAC who shall seek the approval of the Principal, DSS, DFA and Rector.

9. Off-campus, overnight, after class hours and weekend activities require parents’ permission. Hence, students have to accomplish the activity permit a week before the activity. II.
