Written referrals concerning students are received and processed in this office.

12. Learning Resource Centers (LRC) Pope Paul VI LRC is located on the 2^(nd) floor of Fr. Vitale Building and Pope John XXIII LRC is found on the 3^(rd) floor of Fr. Palma Building. The LRC supports the information needs of all the members of the institution. It helps the school personnel and students to transform information into knowledge and practice by providing quality and updated library information and learning services. 13. Avignone Clinic The clinic is adjacent to the St. Francis Sports Center. It promotes the well-being of the school community. It is administered by qualified health practitioners to address the health needs of the education community. 13.1. Medical Services: - first-aid treatment - health monitoring - personal care - health education program - referrals 13.2. Dental Services: - dental consultation and referrals - dental health education program - emergency dental treatment 14. Office for Student Affairs The Office for Student Affairs is located on the ground floor of Fr. Palma Building for college and technical education departments. The high school’s OSA is located on the 2^(nd) floor of HS Building A, Fr. Vitale Building. It supervises, evaluates and oversees the co-curricular activities and programs through the club moderators/advisers in coordination with the department heads and related offices.

15. Office for the School Publications The Office for the School Publications (The Plectrum) is located on the ground floor of Fr. Palma Building. It facilitates the organization and printing of the school papers. It promotes campus journalism in order to strengthen ethical values, character and critical thinking among students and school personnel. 16. Office of the Finance and Administration Director The Office of the Finance and Administration Director is located in Fr. Vitale Building. It is responsible for the internal administration of financial and material resources of the institution. 17. Office for Finance and Accounting The Office for Finance and Accounting is located in Fr. Vitale Building. It handles the financial transactions of the school. It ensures accuracy and completeness of accounting data, adherence to policies and safeguarding of assets. It also accepts payment for tuition and other school fees. 18. Office for Marketing and External Relations The Office for Marketing and External Relations is located on the ground floor of Fr. Palma Building. It facilitates the on-the-job trainings of students, job placements, school promotion, tie ups with industries, and coordination with the alumni associations and other external agencies.

19. Office for School Physical Plant and General Services The Office for School Physical Plant and General Services is located in Fr. Vitale Building. It is responsible for ensuring the integrity of the school physical plant and general services. 20. Office for Scholarship The Office for Scholarship is located in Fr. Vitale Building. It handles the processing of academic scholarship applications of the high school, college and technical education departments. It coordinates with agencies such as DepEd, CHED and TESDA and other government and non-government organizations to assist students in availing of scholarships.

1. St. Anthony’s Chapel The St. Anthony’s Chapel is located in HS Building B, Fr. Vitale Building and is considered the heart of the school. It is a House of God and therefore a place for prayer. Students are encouraged to spend some moments with Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. The following shall be observed in the Chapel: 1.1. Silence should be maintained at all times. 1.2. Proper attire should be worn. 1.3. Cleanliness and orderliness of the chapel should be maintained. 2. Canteen and Food Services RC has two canteens to accommodate all the students and personnel. The college canteen is located near the entrance gate while the high school canteen is located near the St. Francis Sports Center. 3. St. Francis Sports Center The sports center is equipped with the following facilities: 3 indoor basketball courts, 2 volleyball courts, a soccer field, sound system, digital score board, shower rooms, dance hall, fitness room and other indoor games facilities. This is where most of the Physical Education classes are held. Students, after seeking permission from concerned school authorities, may use the gymnasium for playing basketball, volleyball, badminton, and table tennis, and for dancing and other physical fitness activities provided they are in proper sports attire.

4. Conference Rooms and Multi-media Rooms 4.1. John Paul II Conference Room - located on the 3^(rd) floor of Fr. Palma Building. It can accommodate 100 persons. 4.2. Fr. Gaspare Gallitto Conference Room – located on the ground floor of Fr. Palma Building. It can accommodate 15 persons. 4.3. Fr. Joseph Aveni Conference Room – located in Fr. Vitale Building. It is usually used for School Board and School Council meetings. It can accommodate 20 persons. 4.4. St. Therese Multimedia Room – located on the 2^(nd) floor of HS Building A, Fr. Vitale Building. It can accommodate 40 persons. 4.5. St. Bernadette Multi-media Room – located on the ground floor of Fr. Levi Building. It can accommodate 40 persons. 4.6. St. Claire Multi-media Room – located in Fr. Levi Building. It can accommodate 40 persons. Reservation of the conference rooms should be made with the Property Custodian three (3) days before their use. The Multi-media rooms may be reserved through the faculty in-charge. Students’ request for the use of conference rooms and multi-media rooms is honored only if noted by the teachers/instructors in-charge of the subject.

I. Audio-Visual Materials and Equipment 1. The faculty and students can borrow any of the audio-visual materials. 2. All audio-visual materials are for school, library, and classroom use only. 3. Request and reservation of the audio-visual materials should be forwarded to the Librarian at least three (3) days before their use. 4. Request of students for audio-visual materials is honored only if noted by the teachers/instructors in charge of the subject. 5. For teachers/instructors, audio-visual materials can be taken out only for an overnight use. Penalty for overdue materials will be imposed. II. Di Francia Auditorium and Audio-Visual Room (AVR) 1. The reservation/request slip for the use of the Di Francia Auditorium or Audio-Visual Room must be accomplished and submitted to the Property Custodian at least one week before the proposed activity (program, film viewing, etc.) 2. The program of activities and list of audio-visual materials needed must be given to the Property Custodian before the activity. 3. Facilities and other materials and equipment should be cleaned and properly arranged after their use. 4. Lights and air conditioning units should be turned off after the activity.

5. The “NO EATING, NO DRINKING” policy shall be strictly implemented. 6. Any problem encountered during the activity, especially equipment which is not functioning properly, should be immediately brought to the attention of the control room technician/library staff. 7. Students and teachers shall be held accountable for any damage done to any of the equipment used. III. Learning Resource Centers (LRC) 1. LRC schedule: Monday to Friday (7:30 am - 6:00 pm); Saturday (8:00 am- 12:00 noon) 2. Students may avail of the following services: 2.1. Library Orientation 2.2. Library Instruction 2.3. Library Exhibits 2.4. Library Guides 2.5. Reference and Information Services 2.6. Current Events Awareness 2.7. Reader Advisory Guidance 2.8. Searching, Reserving and Stack Service 2.9. Inter-Library Loan 2.10. Compiling Bibliographies upon request 2.11. Reader Word Power Corner 2.12. Film Viewing 3. The following non-print materials/services are available at the Instructional Media Center (IMC): 3.1. Overhead Projectors 3.2. Multimedia Materials 3.3. Visual Aids 4. A photocopying machine is also available at the LRC. 5. Rules Governing the Use of the Internet Access Room: 5.1. To access information from the internet access room, faculty and students should present their validated school ID at the circulation counter before using the internet terminals.

5.2. The Internet is used strictly for researches. 5.3. Use of computer is limited to one hour per session. (Repetition is possible but not in immediate succession.) 5.4. Preparing/typing of projects such as reaction and term papers, thesis or drawing in the computer is not allowed. 5.5. Printing and downloading of researched data or information may be requested at the circulation counter. 5.6. The “NO EATING, NO DRINKING” policy shall be strictly implemented. 5.7. CD-ROM formats and other multi-media software are available upon request at the circulation counter. 5.8. Students who violate these rules shall be subjected to disciplinary action. 6. Rules and Regulations in the LRC 6.1. All students of Rogationist College may borrow any learning resource material from the LRC by presenting a valid school ID. 6.2. SILENCE must be strictly observed. 6.3. The following are strictly prohibited inside the LRC: a. sleeping b. littering c. using electronic gadgets (cellphones, camera, MP3 players, Ipod, etc.) 6.4. Group study or group research may be done in the Discussion Room with reservation. 6.5. The library implements the Open Shelves Control System and uses the Online Public Access Catalogue (OPAC).

6.6. General references, pamphlets, newspapers, magazines or other periodical materials (loose or bound) and rare collections are read only inside the LRC. 6.7. Students are not allowed to bring camera or cellphone with camera inside the Thesis Collections Area. 6.8. Students are held responsible for the loss or damage of any learning material borrowed from the LRC. 6.9. No student is allowed to use the LRC and any of its resources unless all due accounts are settled. 6.10. Chairs and tables should be arranged properly after use. 6.11. Any problem encountered in the LRC should be reported to the Librarian or any of his staff for assistance. 6.12. No photograph may be taken in the reading areas without authorized permission from the Librarian. 6.13. Students must deposit their belongings at the baggage area. 6.14. Any student found violating any of the above-stated policies shall be referred to the Office of Student Discipline. 7. Rule on Circulation Books may be borrowed for three (3) days and may be renewed for another three (3) days provided they are not in demand. 8. Rules on “Reserved” Books

8.1. Due to limited copies, “Reserved” books may be used only for a certain time (1 hour) in the LRC. 8.2. “Reserved” books may be borrowed only during the last period in the afternoon. These should be returned not later than 9:00 a.m. the following day. 9. Materials for “Library Use Only” 9.1. General Reference Materials 9.1.1. Encyclopedia 9.1.2. Dictionaries 9.1.3. Atlases 9.1.4. Almanac 9.1.5. Periodicals 9.2. Non-Print Materials

9.2.2. Audio CD/DVD 9.2.3. Multimedia CDs 9.2.4. Audio cassettes tapes 9.2.5. Transparencies 9.2.6. Slides 9.2.7. VHS tapes 10. Fines and Other Penalties 10.1. For overdue regular, fiction and reference books, a fine of P5.00/day including Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays will be charged. 10.2. For overdue reserved books, a fine of P5.00/hour including Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays will be charged. 10.3. Unauthorized taking out of LRC materials is punishable by suspension of LRC privileges. In addition, the case will be reported to the Office of Student Discipline. 11. Lost Books Lost books should be reported immediately to the Librarian. Otherwise, the lost book will be considered as overdue and the borrower will have to pay the overdue fine. Aside from the cost of the lost book (or replacement with the same book), a processing fee of P200.00 shall also be charged. 12. Disfiguring of Library Materials Students who disfigure (mutilate and/or mark) any library materials, whether book or periodical, shall be suspended from borrowing books for one month and will be fined P100.00 per page or replacement of the same material. In addition, the case will be referred to the Office for Student Discipline.
All penalties and fines should be settled and paid at the Cashier’s Office.

1. Computer Laboratories There are six computer laboratories: two computer laboratories for the high school department, three for the college and technical education departments and one for speech classes. The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the Computer Laboratories: 1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their computer class. 2. The following are prohibited inside the computer rooms: 1.2.1. Food and drinks 1.2.2. Laptops and other electronic gadgets 1.2.3. Using of computer for games 1.2.4. Playing with computer peripherals/accessories 1.2.5. Copying (uploading/downloading) any program from the computer 1.2.6. Opening and attempting to repair any computer 1.2.7. Use of computer hardware and accessories outside the laboratory 1.3.Students should use only their designated computer units. 1.4. Care must be observed while using the equipment in the laboratory. Everything must be returned to its proper place after use. 2. Science Laboratories There are two science laboratories for the College Department, the Chemistry and Physics Laboratories. For the High School Department, there are four science laboratories: General Science, Biology, Chemistry and Physics Laboratories. These are provided with the necessary equipment, instruments, gadgets, utensils, tools, supplies and materials. These laboratories enable the students to gain adequate learning experiences on the theories and principles taught in the classroom through laboratory exercises and experiments.

The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the Science Laboratories: 2.1. Unauthorized persons are not allowed to enter the laboratories. 2.2. Vandalism and littering as well as eating and drinking are prohibited in the laboratories. 2.3. Laboratory seats should be arranged at all times. 2.4. Bags, books and the like should be placed in designated areas. Working tables should be reserved for laboratory materials/equipment needed in the experiment. 2.5. Cabinets in the laboratories can only be used as storage for laboratory paraphernalia. 2.6. Laboratory gowns and/or protective gear such as masks, goggles and gloves should be worn whenever necessary during experimentation. 2.7. After each laboratory activity, the subject teacher/students should check that: 2.7.1. All borrowed laboratory equipment/materials are returned clean, dry and in good working condition. 2.7.2. Working tables are clean and dry. 2.7.3. Sinks are free from lumps. Faucets, gas outlets, lights and ceiling fans are turned off. 2.7.4. Chairs are properly arranged. 2.7.5. Writing on the boards is erased. 2.7.6. Laboratory wastes, chemicals and plant and animal specimens are disposed of at designated areas of the laboratory.

2.8. Any untoward incident related to laboratory activities shall be reported by the students to the subject teacher/instructor or laboratory assistant in charge. 2.9. A subject teacher/instructor/laboratory assistant who has knowledge of any untoward incident should prepare a concise incident report which contains the exact date, time and persons involved. 2.10. Any subject teacher/instructor/laboratory assistant who fails to submit the incident report within 48 hours shall be held accountable for the cost of the damage. 2.11. The incident report shall be submitted in 3 copies to the Property Custodian, Science Subject Area Coordinator and Principal or Cluster Coordinator/TED Head for appropriate action. 2.12. In cases of breakage of materials or damage to equipment/facilities, policies in the Students Manual shall be applied. 2.13. Students who fail to return borrowed material/equipment will not be allowed to borrow again without first settling their responsibility. 2.14. For loss/breakage/damage of laboratory material/equipment, the student should pay through the Cashier’s Office the exact amount as determined by the Property Custodian/Purchasing Officer. The official receipt (O.R.) should then be presented to the Laboratory Assistant/Subject Teacher/Instructor for clearance signing.

3. Technical Laboratories There are six technical laboratories. The Automotive, Mechanical, Welding, and Pneumatics Laboratories are located in Fr. Levi Building. The Electronics and Electrical Laboratories are found in Fr. Palma Building. These are equipped with industry standard facilities and training materials to ensure transfer of learning and skills to students. These laboratories are also made available to High School students for their Technology and Livelihood Education subjects. The following are the rules and regulations inside the Technical Laboratories: 3.1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their technical and practical classes.All scientific and technical works or projects must be performed in the respective laboratories. 3.2. Procedures prescribed by the subject teacher or instructor must be strictly followed. 3.3. Equipment, tools or materials may be borrowed from the stockroom only after accomplishing a borrower’s slip. 3.4. Utmost care must be observed when using any of the equipment, tools or chemicals in the laboratories. The students shall be held responsible for any damage done to any of the equipment, instruments or tools used. 3.5. Students are not allowed to use or take any of the equipment, tools or materials outside the laboratories.

3.6. Students should deposit their personal belongings in the lockers provided outside the laboratories. 4. Technology and Livelihood Education (TLE) Laboratory The TLE Laboratory is located in Fr. Bonarrigo Building. It is equipped with sewing, housekeeping, baking, and cooking equipment. The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the TLE Laboratory: 4.1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their TLE class. 4.2. Students should wear proper attire while doing the activities in the laboratory. 4.3. Moving from one working area to another without the permission of the subject teacher, and playing or running are strictly prohibited. 4.4. Care must be observed while using any of the utensils and equipment in the laboratory. In case a student or a group of students accidentally or intentionally breaks an equipment or utensil, the said student or group is required to replace it. 4.5. Students should use equipment in the laboratory under the supervision of the subject teacher. 4.6. Students should provide their own cleaning materials (i.e. dishwashing liquid, dishwashing foam/pad, cleaning rags and garbage bag). 4.7. Order and cleanliness must be observed in the laboratory. Trash must be properly disposed.

4.8. Unauthorized taking out of any utensil or equipment is considered a major offense with corresponding disciplinary action. 5. Drawing Rooms There are two drawing rooms located on the second floor of Fr. Palma Building. Each room contains sixteen drawing tables and is provided with necessary drawing tools. Rules and Regulations on the Use of the Drawing Room: 5.1. Only students with drawing subjects are allowed to use the room and borrow drawing instruments. 5.2. Borrowed instruments should be used only inside the drawing room. 5.3. Students must maintain the orderliness and cleanliness of the drawing room. 5.4. Students are responsible for any damage or loss of the instruments and tables assigned to them. 6. Cassetti Mini-Hotel The mini-hotel is one of the laboratories for THRM students. It has a front office, a reception area, a tourism office, two standard bedrooms with comfort rooms, a suite complete with a receiving area, a kitchen, comfort room, porch and household appliances and furnishings. Rules and Regulations on the Use of the Cassetti Mini-Hotel: 6.1. The management is not responsible for any loss of personal properties.

6.2. Guests and students should not move furnishings or interfere with the electrical network or any other installations in the hotel. 6.3. Equipment and appliances should be turned off before leaving. 6.4. Order and cleanliness must be observed in the mini-hotel. Trash must be properly disposed. 6.5. Students are responsible for any damage or loss in the mini-hotel. 7. Hotel and Restaurant Management Laboratory Together with the Mini-Hotel, the HRM laboratory is used to facilitate the learning of skills associated with restaurant management. It is adjacent to the Munch Canteen and is provided with the necessary equipment for restaurant operations. The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the HRM Laboratory: 7.1. Students must wear the prescribed laboratory uniform during working sessions. 7.2. Students are required to stay in their assigned working areas. 7.3. Cleanliness and orderliness must be maintained in the laboratory. 8. Caregiving Laboratory This is located adjacent to Avignone Clinic and is equipped with training facilities for Caregiving and Health Care services. The following rules and regulations must be observed in the Caregiving Laboratory: 8.1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their Caregiving class.

8.2. Students should wear proper attire while doing the activities in the laboratory. 8.3. Care must be observed while using the equipment in the laboratory. In case a student or a group of students accidentally or intentionally breaks a piece of equipment, the said student or group is required to replace it. 8.4. Order and cleanliness must be observed in the laboratory. Trash must be properly disposed.

The home shall fully support the school in the implementation of the total school program - curricular and co-curricular - toward the proper physical, social, intellectual and moral development of the child. -Article76. The Child and Youth Welfare Code (Presidential Decree No. 603, s. 1974)

1. The rules and regulations of RC as stated in this Handbook are intended to enhance the life in school of an RC student as he relates and interacts with the members of the school community. As such, it is understood that they are mutual good role models of each other. 2. It is the duty and responsibility of the parents and/or guardians to keep track of the progress of their children/wards in school. The parents and/or guardians are encouraged to confer with the school authorities at their own volition or whenever calls for conference are issued to them. This is to enhance the harmonious working relationship between the school and the home for the welfare of the student. 3. The enrollment of a student in RC is taken as an expressed willingness on his/her part, and consequently of his/her parents and/or guardians, to abide by all rules and regulations of the school. Thus, the student and his/her parents and/or guardians are committed to the strict observance of the same. 4. RC reserves the right to admit, readmit, refuse admission or exclude a student or drop the name of an erring student from the school rolls on the basis of his/her academic performance, conduct or attendance.

5. RC acknowledges its obligations to exercise reasonable supervision over the conduct of the student and to cultivate the best potentialities of the heart and mind of the student. Its role in “loco parentis” is the exercise of substitute parental authority over students in the school and in school-related activities (Civil Code, Art. 349). 6. RC, as a Catholic school, strongly respects and adheres to the practice of holy sacrament (matrimony) and does not tolerate sexual indiscretions. Violation of this policy would merit the student appropriate disciplinary action, including but not limited to, requiring the student to go on leave or will be excluded or dropped from the school rolls. 7. RC expects its students to uphold the standards of responsibility and dignity. When a student of RC does not measure up to these standards, he/she will be excluded or dropped from the school rolls after due process. 8. Students, either as individuals or as a group, must not use the name and seal of the school without official authorization. 9. Students who are using the social media in their respective homes are not to make inappropriate comments (including in private messages) about the school personnel or other students.

10. Parents or guardians may consult or confer with teachers and instructors provided they secure appointments with the Department Head (Principal, Dean or TED Head) two days before the actual date of appointment. Concerns and/or complaints must be written and directly addressed to proper school authority rather than posting them on social media – whether on their own pages, in closed groups (e.g. groups set up for school parents to communicate with each other) or on the school's pages. Complaint posted on social media will not be entertained by the school. 11. Parents, guardians or visitors are not allowed to go to the classrooms. Messages and allowance for the students must be coursed through the Guidance Office. 12. Students may be called out of the classrooms provided an approved written permission/call slip is issued by either of the following: 12.1. Rector/Vice-Rector 12.2. Director for Academic Affairs (DAA) 12.3. Director for Student Services (DSS) 12.4. Director for Spiritual Affairs (DSA) 12.4. Principal/Dean/Technical Education Department Head (TED Head) 12.5. Vice Principal/Vice Dean 12.6. Guidance Counselor/Facilitator 12.7. Prefect of Discipline/Discipline Officer 12.8. Health Services Coordinator/Nurse

13. As a Catholic School, with Rogationist Formation as the core of the curriculum, RC requires all students to attend and pass all the requirements of Christian Living Education or Religious Education subjects. Students also need to attend masses and/or similar activities and complete spiritual recollections and retreats scheduled by the institution. In addition, parents of High School students are required to follow the agreement (to attend/participate in parents’ formation programs, PTA assemblies, etc.) signed during the enrolment of their children. 14. The “No ID, no entry” policy is strictly implemented. The school ID is required for the admittance of students and personnel to the school premises. For parents or other visitors, a visitor’s ID is issued by the guard in exchange for a valid identification card, which is returned after a legitimate business transaction or visit inside the campus. Visitors will be charged for lost visitor’s ID. 15. High School students will stay inside the campus from the moment of their arrival in the morning until their dismissal time in the afternoon. They cannot leave the school premises unless they have written permission from their parents and/or they have secured a gate pass from the Discipline Office duly noted by the Homeroom Adviser and approved by the Principal. In the absence of both, the Prefect of Discipline signs the gate pass. In case of sickness/medical concern, the School Nurse will issue the gate pass.

16. The privacy of certain areas in the campus should be respected by the students. The areas where students are not allowed to stay or loiter are: 16.1. Religious community’s residence and interns’ dormitories 16.2. Refectory, kitchen, lavatory, and carpentry shop 16.3. All laboratories except during scheduled classes and/or when permitted by the Principal/Dean/TED Head 16.4. Fr. Vitale Administration Building, except for official business 16.5. Faculty rooms 16.6. High School classrooms and corridors during recess, lunch and after dismissal time, unless under the supervision of a teacher or with specific permission from the Prefect of Discipline/Discipline Officer. 17. Everyone is enjoined to keep the campus clean at all times. Thus, littering is strictly prohibited. There are waste bins around the campus for proper waste disposal. 18. Everybody should respect, maintain and safeguard the school physical plant. Any damages must be reported immediately to the Office of the General Services. 19. Students are obliged to use English as a medium of communication. 20. Everyone is expected to be courteous and respectful at all times especially to visitors and treat others in a positive and considerate manner.

21. Students must exhibit proper behavior at all times in all places. When the behavior of a student adversely affects the integrity and objectives of the school, he will be subjected to disciplinary action. 22. Using the school website, official Facebook page or RC ID System, announcements are made from time to time to keep the students abreast of school concerns and procedures. Students should relay to their parents all announcements which concern them. Likewise, the school gives out regular and/or timely communications or correspondence to parents. The parents are earnestly requested to acknowledge every communication by filling-up the reply/return slips/parental consents and returning them to the school through their children. 23. Parents/Students are discouraged to post photos or videos that include other children at the school on their personal social media account. 24. In case of misunderstanding between or among the students, parents of the concerned students should not do any drastic action or in any way harass the other concerned students. Such occurrences will be settled according to the policies and guidelines stipulated in this handbook. In addition to this, cooperation of all stakeholders is needed to maintain and promote trust, respect, and dignity of all students, parents/guardians, teachers, and administrators of the school.

25. An activity permit signed by the teacher-in-charge, noted by the Student Affairs Coordinator, and approved by the Principal/Dean/TED Head must be secured by students at least two days before any school activity/practice during non-class days. This form which can be obtained from the Student Affairs Coordinator should be signed by their parents and returned to the teacher-in-charge a day before the approved activity/practice. In this way, parents are properly informed and could monitor their children’s activities. 26. Students who wish to participate in any outside activity as representatives of the school should secure approval from the school administration. 27. In cases of emergency, or for valid reasons, high school students may bring cellular phones or other gadgets provided there is a letter of permission from the parents. These gadgets will be surrendered to the subject teacher, adviser or discipline officer right after the morning assembly and will be retrieved after classes in the afternoon. College students however, may bring their cellular phones but they should refrain from using these inside the classrooms, library or during school hours and liturgical celebrations.

28. High School students permitted to bring cellphone, laptop, netbook, camera or any gadget/device must deposit the gadget/device to the Office for Student Discipline or to the subject teacher during the first period. The gadget/device must be used only during the class activity and only by its owner. Unauthorized/improper use of a gadget/device may result in disciplinary action and confiscation of the gadget/device. A confiscated item shall be released only to the student’s parent/legal guardian 29. Taking into consideration the educational system of RC and the promotion of an environment that is conducive to learning, the Discipline Officer, together with the subject teacher or adviser, may conduct inspection as the need arises. 30. Parents or students who wish to request for school forms or documents such as ESC Certificates, Form 137/ SF10, Certificate of Enrolment, Certificate of Grades, Certification of Good Moral Character and/or Rank, and Recommendation Letter, must apply for these at least a week before actual claim to give ample time for the preparation of such forms or documents. Formal request letter must be submitted to the concerned offices and attach proof of requirements. Online (e-mail) or phone call request may be accommodated provided that proof of requirement is presented upon claiming. A minimal amount will be charged.

31. In order to be allowed to enter the school premises, students’ vehicles/school service vehicles must have the official school sticker which may be secured at the Accounting Office. 32. The Office for Student Discipline will inform parents/guardians in writing about a student’s case and may require the parents to come personally for proper disposition of the said case. 33. Parents visiting the school are required to wear modest/proper clothes. 34. No students or visitors, including parents or guardians, shall be allowed inside the school building and the premises after the last class period has ended. (DepEd Order No. 11 s. 2011) 35. A student shall be responsible for informing his parents/guardians of the following: 35.1. School policies and guidelines stated in this handbook. 35.2. Student’s academic standing and the possible consequences of his excessive absences, dropping, failures or gross misbehavior.

Classes are suspended in the following situations: 1. Typhoon warning signal is raised by PAGASA in the area of Cavite. Signal no. 2 automatically suspends classes in the secondary level while signal no. 3 automatically suspends classes in the tertiary level. Depending on signal numbers declared at 10:00 pm and 4:30 am of the following day, classes in appropriate levels for the whole day are deemed automatically cancelled/suspended. (DepEd Order No. 43 series 2012). 2. Natural calamities or disturbances compromising the safety of the students; 3. Rector’s announcement; 4. Cancellation of classes by DepEd, TESDA or CHED; 5. National, Provincial, and Municipal proclamations N.B. Afternoon classes in the appropriate levels in areas with signal numbers declared at 11:00 am that day will be cancelled or suspended at 2:00 pm to ensure the safety of the students and to provide ample time for the school authorities to contact school service providers and/or the parents. In addition to this, during heavy rains affecting the health or safety of their children, parents have the discretion not to send their children to school;

1. Tuition fees and other charges are prescribed by the school authorities. These charges are posted in the Bulletin of Information. 2. Parents and students enter into agreement with the school regarding the mode of payment of tuition and other fees. 3. It is the obligation of the parents and students to update themselves with regard to the status of their accounts by consulting the Finance and Administration Department. 4. Examination permit for the JHS & SHS and by the Cashier for the College/TED students. This should be signed by the Cashier two weeks before each major examination. It is recommended that accounts be settled at least two weeks before the scheduled examination period to avoid inconvenience and delay. 5. Tuition fees and other charges for transferring or withdrawing students shall be governed by the following provisions:

When a student registers in a school, it is understood that he/she is enrolling for the entire school year for secondary courses. (DepEd Order No. 88 series 2010: Revised Manual of Regulations for Private Schools. Section 119. Rules for Registration) thus, a student who transfers or otherwise withdraws, in writing, within two weeks after the beginning of classes and who has already paid the pertinent tuition and other fees in full or for any length of time longer than one month may be charged 10% of the total amount due for the term if he withdraws within the 1^(st) week of classes, or 20% if within the 2^(nd) week of classes, regardless of whether or not he has actually attended classes. The student may be charged in full if he withdraws any time after the 2^(nd) week of classes. However, if the transfer or withdrawal is due to justifiable reason, the student shall be charged the pertinent fees only up to and including the last month of attendance.

For College students: Manual of Regulations for Private Higher Education Section 100. Tuition Charges – A student who transfers or otherwise withdraws, in writing, within two weeks after the beginning of classes and who has already paid the pertinent tuition and other fees in full or for any length of time longer than one month may be charged 25% of the total amount due for the term if he withdraws within the 1^(st) week of classes, or 50% if within the 2^(nd) week of classes, regardless of whether or not he has actually attended classes. The student may be charged all the school fees in full if he withdraws any time after the 2^(nd) week of classes.

The Senior High School Department is an excellent provider of integrated human formation leading towards learners’ tertiary, work and entrepreneurial preparedness aligning its thrust to the Catholic education and the ideals of St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia.

1. Design curricular program offerings for the students that shall equip them with the 21^(st) century skills like learning and innovation, life and career, communication and information media and technology; 2. Instill a Culture of Life and Prayer through the development of relevant programs and activities that lead to heightened spiritual, social and moral responsibilities; and 3. Develop programs that shall strongly encourage participative involvement among students and stakeholders for a more meaningful and effective learning experience.
To become an innovative center of learning that forms productive and responsible students equipped with the essential competencies and values for both life-long skills and lucrative employment.

Admission for incoming Grade 11 students is open to all Grade 10 completers with very satisfactory academic qualification (a final average of at least 85% in the Grade 9 and Grade 10 report card and no line of 7 grade in any subject), intellectual ability (average I.Q.), normal personality and good conduct (conduct grade of Satisfactory/Good/B/85). Prior to the admission, the school may require a list of documents or clearances for evaluation with regard to character or medical history of a student. Only until the student has completed all admission requirements shall he/she be considered officially enrolled. I. Admission Procedure for Grade 11 Applicants coming from Other Junior High Schools 1. Application for Entrance Test 1.1. Secure an application form from the Registrar’s Office. This form is free of charge and can be photocopied. 1.2. Fill-out the form completely and attach: 1.2.1. A clear photocopy of the applicant’s Grade 9 and latest Grade 10 report cards 1.2.2. A clear photocopy of the applicant’s National Career Assessment Examination (NCAE) certificate 1.2.3. Two (2) pieces of 2x2 colored I.D. pictures (with white background and name tag)

1.3. Pay the testing fee to the Cashier. 1.4. Submit the form with the above requirements and receipt to the Registrar’s Office. Thereafter, a test permit indicating the schedule of entrance test will be issued to the applicant. 1.5. Entrance examinations usually start on the 2^(nd) Saturday of January and every Saturday thereafter until April. 1.6. Applicants should report on their scheduled examination date at least 10 minutes earlier than their scheduled examination time. They should bring the test permit, pencil and eraser. 1.7. Applicants who were able to submit the completed documents should follow-up on the application two weeks after taking the examination. A list of qualifiers and other possible candidates will be posted on the bulletin boards. 1.8. Qualified Grade 11 applicants will be advised to report for interview and/or pre-enrolment. 2. Interview and Pre-enrolment Qualified incoming Grade 11 students and their parents who are interested to push through with their application have to report for interview on the indicated schedule. After passing the interview, the applicants can proceed with the pre-enrolment. They must follow the following procedure:

2.1. Attend the Batch Orientation; 2.2. Report to the Guidance Office for interpretation test results and intake interview; 2.3. Report to the Office for Student Discipline for Initial Orientation on conduct expectations; 2.4. Report to the school nurse for the medical interview; 2.5. Proceed to the Office of the Senior High School Principal for final interview 2.6. Submit to the Registrar’s Office the accomplished pre-enrolment form 2.7. Pay a non-refundable reservation fee, which is deductible from the total tuition fee upon enrolment. 2.8. Get the List of Requirements for Enrollment from the Registrar’s Office. II. Admission Procedure for Grade 11 Applicants coming from Rogationist College Junior High School Department Grade 10 students of RC Junior High School Department should follow these procedures to pre-enroll in the Senior High School Department; 1. Fill-out the Pre-enrolment Form 2. Report to the Guidance Office for Career Advising and Recommendation 3. Report to the Junior High School Principal for Interview and Endorsement 4. Proceed to the Senior High School Principal for Final Interview 1. Presence of student’s parent will be required for provisional applicants

5. Pay a non-refundable reservation fee, which is deductible from the total tuition fee upon enrolment. 6. Submit to the Registrar’s Office the accomplished pre-enrolment form 7. Get the List of Requirements for Enrollment from the Registrar’s Office. III. Admission Procedure for Grade 12 RC grade 11 students are required to submit School Form 9 (report card) duly signed by parents for grade 12 enrolment. RC is not accepting transferee students for grade 12. IV. Enrollment On the scheduled date of enrolment, students must present to the Registrar the following requirements: 1. Original Report Card, duly signed by the parents and the School Principal 2. A photocopy of PSA Birth Certificate 3. Four (4) pieces of 2”x2” colored I.D. pictures (with white background and name tag) 4. Medical Certificate/Immunization Record for those with health problems or special conditions 5. Full or partial payment of school fees V. Temporary Enrolment (DepEd Order No. 3 s. 2018) Students from public or private schools in the Philippines who failed to submit the SF9 (formerly Form 138) during early registration or upon enrolment shall only be temporarily enrolled until the submission of required documents on or before August 31^(st) of the current school year. They shall be required to submit an Affidavit of Undertaking, signed by the parent/guardian in order to be temporarily enrolled.

For temporarily enrolled students, RC shall issue a Temporary Progress Report Card signed by the Homeroom Adviser for the parents/guardians to monitor the progress of his/her child. This form is inadmissible for transfer and enrolment purposes and is only issued for progress monitoring. Upon complete submission of the documentary requirements, the student shall be tagged as officially enrolled in the LIS. Otherwise, the student retains the status of temporarily enrolled; the student cannot be officially promoted to a higher grade level, and the student cannot officially graduate from the school. The student will not be recognized should he/she attain the qualifying average ad other criteria for academic honors, and RC shall not release official documents such as the SF 10, Certificate of Completion, Diploma, etc. VI. (VIII). Invalid Enrolment (DepEd No. 3 s. 2018) Unless otherwise specifically authorized by the Secretary of Education, the enrollment of any student who is under a term of suspension or expulsion, or the enrollment of any student from a school or course without government authority shall not be valid.

section_title: GUIDELINES AND CONDITIONS ON MONITORING/PROBATION STATUS
content: RC education is for all students who can maintain its standards of academic excellence and exemplary conduct. It requires a high degree of achievement from its students. Thus, a student who does not meet the standards set by the school is put on a probationary status. Probation is a period of time designed to ascertain the ability of a student to abide by the academic and conduct standards of the school. I. Academic Probation Status Academic Probation status is a formal warning or reminder that carries with it a condition that improvement in terms of academic achievement is necessary for readmission and/or promotion. This is given to a student so that he will show improvement during the semester/school year. 1.1. Academic Probation is given to a student who has shown below average academic performance in the previous semester/school year. It is a status imposed on a student whose final general average is below 82%. 1.2. The student on Academic Probation is required to maintain good grades (no failing marks in any subject) and to have a final general average of at least 82% in order for his/her status to change to that of a regular student the following school year.

section_title: GUIDELINES AND CONDITIONS ON MONITORING/PROBATION STATUS
content: 1.3. Failure on the part of the student to show definite improvement or abide by the academic standards of the school within the school year would mean non-readmission for the following school year. 1.4. A student placed on Academic Probation for an incoming school year shall not be eligible for any higher elective and/or appointive position in any varsity team, club or organization subject to the discretion of the Rector. II. Conduct Monitoring Status 1. A student is placed on Conduct Monitoring after incurring a series of minor offenses during a semester/school year. 2. If a student commits other minor offenses or a major offense during the monitoring period, his/her status will be elevated to conduct probation for the current semester/school year. 3. The Conduct Monitoring status may be lifted the following semester/school year if the student shows satisfactory improvement in his/her behavior. III. Conduct Probation Status 1. A student is placed on Conduct Probation after committing a major offense. 2. A student placed on Conduct Probation for an incoming school year shall not be eligible for any elective and/or appointive position in any varsity team, club or organization subject to the discretion of the Rector.

section_title: GUIDELINES AND CONDITIONS ON MONITORING/PROBATION STATUS

If a student placed on Conduct Probation commits a series of minor offenses or a major offense, he/she may be dismissed in the following school year or he/she may be dismissed immediately. 4. The Conduct Probation status may be lifted after a semester/school year if the student shows remarkable improvement in his/her behavior.

A grade 12 RC student should have satisfactorily completed all academic and other requirements prescribed by the school in order to qualify as a candidate for the Commencement Exercises. The regulations for graduations are the following: 1. A graduating senior high school student will not be permitted to participate in the Commencement Exercises for any of the following reasons: 1.1. He/She fails in one or more subjects. 1.2. He/She lacks units or subjects required for graduation under the Rogationist College High School curriculum. 3. He/She has incurred absences of more than 20% of the prescribed number of school days during the school year (DepEd Order no. 11 s. 2011) 1.4. He/She has committed an offense meriting the penalty of non- participation in the Commencement Exercises. 2. All graduating students in the senior high school department are required to attend the rehearsals for the Thanksgiving Mass and Commencement Exercises. These are the regulations set by the school in relation to the attendance of graduating students to rehearsals: 2.1. A graduating student participating in the graduation rehearsals should be in complete uniform or should follow the required dress code. Failure to do so shall be considered a commission of an offense equivalent to 8 hours community service.

2.2. A graduating student shall be allowed one (1) absence but must render 8 hours community service. 2.3 For those with unexcused absence/community service, release of the school documents will be done after a make-up for the number of days of absence.

Scholarships granted by the school are percentage discounts which apply only to the tuition fee. 1. Employee’s Legal Dependents’ Discount All full-time employees who have rendered at least 1 year of service to the SABV and RC are entitled to 50% tuition fee discount in Rogationist College for all their legal dependents/beneficiaries. Legal dependents/beneficiaries would mean the employee’s brothers, sisters and children 18 years and below, subject to the following conditions: a. Dependent’s age upon their enrolment should be 18 years and below. b. Tuition fee discounts shall only be granted for a period no longer than the duration of the course/program in which the beneficiary has originally enrolled. 2. Family Discount For brothers and sisters enrolled at the same time within a school year, the 2^(nd) child and each of the succeeding children enrolling will receive a 5% discount. This discount does not apply to employees of SABV and RC and those under the SHS Socialized Program. 3. St. Anthony’s Boys Village Grantees’ and Interns’ Discount This is granted to less-privileged youths chosen by the SABV community. According to the by-laws of SABV-RC, the interns are considered children or beneficiaries of the Institution who are entitled to receive the benefit of 50% discount in the tuition fee.
N.B. In case a student qualifies for two or more scholarships, grants or aids, the one with the highest benefit applies. No monetary refund will be allowed.

I. Academic Programs 1. Enrichment Program Each subject area organizes activities that provide opportunities for the students to show and develop their talents and potentials. These may be in the form of theatrical plays, song compositions, debates, quiz bee and other competitions. The activity program with its co-curricular activities likewise gives the students a chance to be more creative, resourceful and progressive in their field of interest. 2. Remedial Program The school offers remedial program for students in all subjects to help them improve their academic performance. The remedial classes shall be conducted at the Rogationist College on the agreed dates and time schedules within the actual school year. Arrangement can be done with the Vice-Principal and specific guidelines will be given to the students and their parents. 3. Technical Vocational Program Elective subjects are offered to senior high school students to equip them with technical skills in the areas of Home Economics, Industrial Arts, and Information and Communication Technology. All Grade 11 students are given the chance to choose their elective subject and pass the assessment given by TESDA after completion of the training program, which is a requirement for inclusion of the students in the commencement exercises.

4. Christian Enhancement Program The school offers Religious Education subject in grades eleven and twelve. It is required as an academic core subject for spiritual and moral formation. This is handled by Religious Education subject teachers in collaboration with the Campus Ministry under the Directorate for Spiritual Affairs. This program includes First Friday Masses, monthly confessions, confirmation, retreats recollections and seminars. II. Academic Policies 1. Classroom Assessment Classroom Assessment is an integral part of curriculum implementation. It allows the teachers to track and measure learners’ progress and to adjust instruction accordingly. Classroom assessment informs the learners, as well as their parents and guardians, of their progress. It is also an ongoing process of identifying, gathering, organizing, and interpreting quantitative and qualitative information about what learners know and can do. The RC Senior High School Department utilizes two kinds of assessment of a student’s performance: the formative assessment and the summative assessment. 1.1. Formative Assessment (Assessment as Learning) This is conducted during and/or after every lesson. It is given by the teacher to check whether students are attaining the objectives of instructions. The results are recorded but not part of the grade except when the result is satisfactory. The teacher uses the results for improving learning by changing or modifying strategies of learning activities that have not been effective.

1.2. Summative Assessment (Assessment of Learning) This is conducted at the end of every phase of the lesson for the purpose of making a judgment on the level of proficiency the student has attained. The components of summative assessment are as follows: 1.2.1. Written Work component ensures that the students are able to express skills and concepts in written form. Written Work, which may include long quizzes, and unit or long tests, help strengthen test-taking skills among the learners. It is strongly recommended that items in long quizzes/ tests be distributed across the Cognitive Process Dimensions so that all are adequately covered. Through these, learners are able to practice and prepare for quarterly assessment and other standardized assessments. Other written report work may include essays, written reports, and other written output. 1.2.2. Performance Task component allows learners to show what they know and are able to do diverse ways. They may create or innovate products or do performance-based tasks. Performance-based tasks may include skills demonstration, group presentations, oral work, multimedia presentations, and research projects. It is important to note that written output may also be considered as performance tasks.

1.2.3. Quarterly Assessment measures student learning at the end of the quarter. These may be in the form of objective tests, performance-based assessment, or combination thereof. 1.3. Weight of the Components for SHS The grading system for Senior High School follows a different set of weights for each component. The weights for the core, applied, specialized and elective subjects are the following: 1.3.1. Core Subjects Written Works - 25% Performance Tasks - 50% Quarterly Assessment - 25% 1.3.2. Applied and Specialized Subjects (except subjects indicated in 1.3.3.) Written Works - 25% Performance Tasks - 45% Quarterly Assessment - 30% 1.3.3. Work Immersion/ Business Enterprise Simulation/ Capstone Project/ Culminating Activity Written Works - 35% Performance Tasks - 40% Quarterly Assessment - 25% 1.3.4. Elective Subjects Written Works - 20% Performance Tasks - 60% Quarterly Assessment - 20% *will be changed for G11 due to implementation of SSHS 2. Grading System RC uses a standards- and competency-based grading system as mandated in the K to 12 Basic Education Program. These are found in the curriculum guides and maps. A student’s grade is based on the weighted raw score of his/her summative assessments. The minimum grade need to pass a specific learning area is 60, which is transmuted to 75 in the report card. The lowest mark that can appear on the report card is 60 for Quarterly Grades and Final Grades.

At the end of each semester, students’ grades are computed by getting the average of the midterm grade and final grade and this is considered as the subject grade. --------------------------- --------------- --------- Descriptor Grading Scale Remarks Outstanding 90-100 Passed Very Satisfactory 85-89 Passed Satisfactory 80-84 Passed Fairly Satisfactory 75-79 Passed Did Not Meet Expectations Below 75 Failed --------------------------- --------------- --------- 3. Benefits of Students Who Join Academic Competitions outside the School Due recognition and benefits are given to students who are sent to various off-campus academic competitions as representatives of the school. 3.1. For the Related Subject 3.1.1. The student will be exempted from all the activities (seat works, quizzes, assignments, and laboratory activities) done in the related subject during the trainings and the competition proper except for the performance task and summative examinations. 3.1.2. The student’s grade for the affected term must not be lower than 82% and must not be below than the passing grade provided that he/she complies with the PT & summative examinations. 3.2. For Other Subjects 3.2.1. The student will not be exempted from all the activities (seat works, and quizzes). The student must take missed activities (seat works, quizzes, assignments, and laboratory activities) on the schedule set the subject teacher, provided that the student is given ample time to comply.

3.2.2. The student’s grade for the affected quarter must not be lower than his/her previous grade provided that he/she complies with all the requirements given by the subject teachers. 4. Report Card (School Form 9) The report card is an official document of the school that shows the student’s performance per quarter. This card is intended to show how students performed in a particular quarter or grading period. Report cards are distributed quarterly. During the first and third quarters, these are given to the parents coinciding with the Parent-Teacher Conference while on the second quarter, these are given to the students while Parent-Teacher Conference is done a day after issuance. Parents are encouraged to confer with teachers and/or other school authorities during the regular Parent-Teacher Conference. 5. Loss of Report Card Any student who loses his/her report card can request for a replacement with affidavit of loss as a requirement at the Registrar’s Office. The cost shall be charged to the student. 6. On Examinations 6.1. Quarterly (midterm and final) examinations in all subjects are administered within a span of four (4) 3 half-days such that a maximum of three subjects are given in each half-day, one hour for each subject.

6.2. Schedule of quarterly examination is posted on the bulletin of information as well as written in the student diary. 6.3. Examination room assignment is posted in all classrooms a day before the examination period. 6.4. Examination permits are required during all quarterly examinations and submitted to the Homeroom Adviser within one week before the examination days. 6.5. Students must be in the examination room five minutes before the scheduled examination. 6.6. Students should observe absolute silence in the examination room and adjoining corridors. 6.7. Students are expected to observe all examination rules enforced by the Room Examiners such as: 6.7.1. Be seated on their assigned seats 6.7.2 No borrowing of materials 6.7.3. No eating 6.7.4. No loitering along the corridors 6.7.5. No one is allowed to leave the examination room once the examination has started 6.7.6. Bags, notes, and other materials not to be used during the examinations must be placed on the platform upon entering the examination room. 6.7.7. Questions to room examiners are not allowed except for corrections in the test questions and missing pages of the test papers

6.7.8. Clarifications may be directed only to the Room Supervisors assigned in different examination areas. Note: Failure to observe any one of items 6.7.1 to 6.7.8 is considered an offense and therefore subjects the student to disciplinary action. 6.8. Special Examinations A student who fails to take the scheduled quarterly examination must secure a special examination permit from the Vice-Principal upon submission of an excuse letter from the parent/guardian. If the reason for failure to take the examination is illness, a medical certificate must be attached to the excuse letter. A required fee per subject will be charged. Upon payment of this fee, the Principal approves the permit. Special examinations are facilitated by the Office of the Vice-Principal. 7. Moratorium on Student Co-curricular Activities All co-curricular activities are suspended one (1) week before the examinations so that the students can concentrate on their preparation for the examinations. 8. Student Clearance Clearance should be accomplished by all students every end of the school year. A graduating student should be cleared from all financial obligations and administrative accountabilities from the different offices before a High School graduation certificate, transcript of record, certification and other similar documents are issued to him/her. For Grade 11 students, the completed clearance form is needed in order for them to get their final grades and to enroll.

9. Withholding of Credentials (DepEd Order No. 88 s. 2010) The release of the transfer credentials of any student may be withheld for reasons of suspension, expulsion or nonpayment of financial obligations or property responsibility of the student to the school. The credentials shall be released as soon as his/her obligation shall have been settled or the penalty of suspension or expulsion lifted. Guidelines in Giving Student Awards Rogationist College gives quarterly and annual awards to outstanding students who have distinguished themselves in Academics, Diligence, Conduct, and Leadership. Special Awards related to co-curricular activities are also given. These awards are given to promote the educational development and personal growth of students in the fields of intellectual, behavioral and affective formation. The highest award given by the institution is the Rogate Award. The following criteria shall be used in determining the awards:

1.1. Quarterly This award shall be given to students of a particular class who obtain the highest average of all learning areas. They must not have a grade lower than 85% in any of the learning areas. They must have conducted themselves in conformity with the school rules and regulations. The top three ranking students in a class per quarter will receive the certificates. This number may increase in case of a tie. 1.2. Annual The guidelines on awards and recognition for the K to 12 Basic Education Program DepEd Order No. 36, s. 2016 shall apply in determining the annual awardees. This annual award is given to students from Grade 11 to 12 who have attained a General Average of at least 90 and a passing Final Grade in all learning areas. --------------------------- ----------------- Academic Excellence Award General Average With Highest Honors 98 - 100 With High Honors 95 - 97 With Honors 90 - 94 --------------------------- -----------------

This award shall be given to students who manifest remarkable and positive attitude towards education and the learning process. They must possess a natural desire and willingness to learn and to be educated and must have the personal initiative to improve their understanding and comprehension of the lessons. 2.1. Quarterly Awardees are determined by the following procedure: 2.1.1. In the first quarter, advisers and teachers nominate and rank the candidates per class for the award. The nominees should have satisfactory performance with Approaching Proficiency (AP) as the lowest rating in any learning area. Out of the nominees per class, only the top three student awardees will receive certificates. Approaching proficiency grade must be defined. In SHS, 2.1.2 is applicable only for the second quarter/final term since the curriculum is semestral. Third quarter (2nd sem-midform) 2.1.1. Applies 2.1.2. In the succeeding quarters (second and third), nominees’ quarterly averages should have improved and they must not have a rating lower than Approaching Proficiency (AP). Standard deviation is applied to the difference between quarterly marks. The top three ranking students per class per quarter will receive the certificates.

2.2. Annual Quarterly awardees will automatically become candidates for the annual awards. Other candidates can be nominated as long as their averages have improved remarkably and consistently until the finals. The top three ranking student awardees per year level will receive the medals. However, the number of awardees may vary depending on how many among the candidates have met the set criteria.

This award shall be given to students who manifest exemplary human behavior and who meet the highest standards of good character and discipline set by the school. They must have conducted themselves in conformity with the school rules and regulations. The rating for conduct shall be based on the four core values (Integrity-25%, Excellence-25%, Love of God and Neighbor-25%, Patriotism-25%). Awardees shall be determined from the computed averages of conduct marks given by the subject teachers. The core values should be manifested by each of the awardees through the following:

He/She influences his/her fellow students to visit and pray in the chapel, lead his/her fellow students in prayers, show positive attitude in dealings with fellow students, exercise charity throughout the department, and refrains from anger when faced by difficult circumstances.

He/She shows pride and honor in being a true Filipino. He/She also actively involves himself/herself in school’s flag ceremony and other school programs which promote nationalism. He/She also abides by the rules and regulations sets in the school and his/her community. He/She also upholds Filipino virtues such as respect for the elderly, righteousness and pakikisama.

He/She gives healthy opinions and sound views during class or group discussions. He/She also exercises responsibility over tasks performed in and outside the classroom. He/She also demonstrates honesty at all times and acts as a good role model to fellow students. He/She also hold on to his/her moral beliefs.

He/She uses his/her free time to help other students understand difficult lessons. He/She also complies with all the school requirements on time. He/She also shows outstanding performance in academics and behavioral concerns. He/She is also respected by fellow students and highly regarded by teachers and school personnel. 4. Leadership Award This annual award is given to any graduating student who has exemplified outstanding leadership qualities during his/her four 2 years of stay in Rogationist College. The awardee shall be chosen from the nominees presented by the teachers. The following are the criteria set in choosing a nominee for the award: 4.1. An elected school, club or class officer 4.2. Has manifested the following traits during his/her term of office: - Honesty - Decisiveness - Responsibility - Obedience - Promptness - Affability/Friendliness - Community-orientedness 4.3. has no failing grades in any of the learning areas 4.4. has not committed any major offense 5. Rogate Award This is the highest honor Rogationist College bestows on any of its graduating students. The award goes to whoever best exemplifies the spirit and ideals of Saint Hannibal Mary Di Francia. The awardee should meet the following requirements:

5.1. Belongs to the graduating class. 5.2. Must have stayed for two years in Rogationist College. 5.3. Prays for and promotes vocation. 5.4. Cares for the poor. 5.5. Must have an academic average of Very Satisfactory or better in every grade level (no grade lower than 85% in all grade levels, in all quarters as reflected in the report card (excellence) 5.6. Must have conducted himself/herself in conformity with the school rules and regulations (no conduct grade below 85% in al quarters, in all grade levels as reflected in the report card). Thus, those with Satisfactory (S) or lower conduct grades in any of the quarters of their stay in the school are automatically disqualified. N.B. Without a qualified candidate, no award will be given. In selecting the Rogate Awardee, the following are observed; 1. There shall be nomination from students. 2. There shall be nomination and screening from teachers. 3. The short list of candidates is to be passed by the Honor’s Committee to the School Board. 4. Candidates shall submit an essay to the School Board (specific topic to be determined by the School Board)

5. The School Board shall conduct an individual or panel interview with the candidates before determining the student to be awarded. Guidelines on the Selection of Honor Students In giving due recognition to students who have shown exemplary performance, the following guidelines shall be observed: 1. Disciplinary actions are corrective and formative measures which are given to students who fail to comply with the policies and rules of the school. The primary objective of these disciplinary actions is to guide and accompany erring students to the right behavior which also takes into consideration the guidelines stated above (proper student decorum). Disciplinary actions range from verbal warning to exclusion depending on the gravity of the offense and its circumstances. The Discipline Officer is the one who directly monitors students’ conduct. All offenses incurred by the students shall be immediately reported to the Discipline Officers, who will do the necessary verification and processing of cases. Prompt reporting of incident of misbehavior of an RC student is encouraged. This covers incidents from the first day of classes of the current year until the final report card distribution of the following year. This is done in order to maximize the intervention, reformation and/or imposition of appropriate disciplinary action/s of the school. I. Disciplinary Actions 1. For Minor Offenses

2.2. Preventive Suspension – A student under investigation of a serious or grave case may be preventively suspended from entering the school premises especially if the evidence of guilt is strong and the Office for Student Discipline and the Principal is morally convinced that the continued stay of the student during the period of investigation constitutes a distraction to the normal operations of the school or poses a risk or danger to the life of persons and property in the school. This may also be imposed by the school to protect the student with pending cases from acts of vindictiveness and to maintain an atmosphere in the school that is conducive to learning. 2.3. Exclusion – The school reserves the right to exclude/dismiss, or drop from school during the year, any student who fails to give positive evidence of earnestness of purpose and active cooperation in all requirements of conduct or whose conduct makes the student a liability and nuisance to the school. N.B. In some major disciplinary offenses, erring students may not be allowed to attend/participate in a major school activity such as Acquaintance Party, Celestial Night, Christmas Party, Educational Tour, Sports Festival, Completion Rite, etc.

II. Monitoring and Probation 1. Conduct Monitoring – This is a period during which a student who has incurred a series of minor offenses during a semester/school year will be closely monitored by the Guidance Counselors/Facilitators and the Discipline Officers for one semester/school year. The monitoring may be lifted the following semester/school year if the student shows satisfactory improvement of behavior. However, if the student commits other minor offenses or a major offense during the monitoring period, his/her status will be elevated to conduct probation for the current semester/school year. Further, an erring student shall be placed under Conduct Monitoring if he/she is involved in a special case (neither a minor or major offense). 2. Conduct Probation – A student who has committed a major offense will fall under this status. The student will be closely followed-up by the Adviser, Guidance Counselor and the Discipline Officers for one school year. If he/she commits a series of minor offenses or a major offense, he/she may be excluded the following school year or he/she may be excluded immediately. The Conduct Probation status may be lifted the following school year if no offense has been made (minor or major) and the student has manifested the expected behavior.

III. Conference with Subject Teachers Conference with Subject Teacher is done if a student commits academic-related offense. After a series of conferences with a teacher and the student still commits an academic-related offense for the third time, inside or outside the classroom, the case may referred to the Office for Student Discipline IV. Due Process The school recognizes the students’ right to due process through conference and dialogue before implementing a disciplinary action. Thus, the school conducts due inquiry or verification of students’ cases, wherein parties involved are given the chance to present their sides. The Discipline Officer is authorized by the school to call students involved. Students will be asked to write his/her narrative account of the incident. Considering that high school students are of minor age, parents or legal guardians of students involved are invited to the Office for Student Discipline to be informed of the case and to promptly answer charges against them, if they so desire. The basic principles of due process shall be in place. In some major offenses, the discipline committee may be convened by the Director for Student Services in order to carefully assess the case and reach a decision. This committee is composed of the DSS, Director for Spiritual Affairs, Principal, Prefect of Discipline/Discipline Officer, and Guidance Counselor.

After the discipline committee has reached a decision, a final conference facilitated by the Director for Student Services, Principal and Prefect of Discipline will be made with the student and his/her parents. A student who has committed an offense may also be referred to the Guidance Office if after due verification and consideration, counseling is deemed to be more appropriate than disciplinary action. A student who transfers or otherwise withdraws, in writing, within two weeks after the beginning of classes and who has already paid the pertinent tuition and other fees in full or for any length of time longer than one month may be charged ten (10%) percent of the total amount due for the term if he withdraws within the first week of classes, or twenty percent if within the second week of classes, regardless of whether or not he has actually attended classes. The student may be charged all the school fees in full if he withdraws any time after the second week of classes. However, if the transfer or withdrawal is due to a justifiable reason, the student shall be charged the pertinent fees only up to and including the last month of attendance. The foregoing tuition fee schedules are based on the premise that a student who enrolls in a school stays enrolled for the entire school year or semester, regardless of his subsequent transfer or withdrawal. Section 66, MRPS and Section 104, TVET Manual protect schools which accept tuition fee payments on installment – i.e., where a down payment is given upon enrollment and the balance is paid before examinations–– by requiring students who transfer or withdraw from the course to first settle their accounts before the school issues them transfer credentials.

It must be stressed that according to the stipulations of Section 62(e) of the MRPS and section 124(e), TVET Manual, a school can legally collect outstanding tuition fees from a student who has transferred or withdrawn only if he was officially enrolled. This means that the student must have at least made an initial payment of his school fees and that the school must have accepted that payment and authorized him to participate in his classes. Without these attending circumstances, there is no legal basis for the collection of tuition fee charges, since no contractual relationship between student and school was established. A student who has paid in full or for any length longer than one month and transfers or withdraws in the first week after classes begin shall be charged 10% of the total amount due for the term (i.e. one semester for the collegiate level and TVET courses, one year for elementary and secondary levels); if he withdraws in the second week he will be charged 20%; if he withdraws any time after the second week, he may be fully charged for all fees applicable for the entire term. These charges hold whether or not he actually participated in his classes, because attendance is not the issue; what matters is that the school actually authorized him to attend them.

For purposes of determination, the day of the student’s submission of his written notice of withdrawal shall be considered the date of withdrawal. Verbal notice is not enough. If the tuition fees, registration, library and laboratory fees already paid equal the amount still to be paid for the first month (or less) in a monthly installment scheme, no refund shall be given to the student when he withdraws after the registration period. However, if the transfer or withdrawal is due to justifiable cause, the student shall only be charged the pertinent fees up to the last month of attendance. An existing DepEd ruling states that any promissory note signed in favor of a school by a student below 18 years old is null and void. It does not constitute the “payment of some kind” needed to establish enrollment unless a responsible relative or legal guardian acts as surety. The reason for this is that in law, a person below 18 years old is still a minor and is not legally competent to contract such a financial obligation. Yet even if the student were of majority age but still dependent on the parents or a guardian for support, the DepEd would not consider him competent to sign a promissory note. Therefore, such a note would likewise be considered null and void unless a responsible relative or guardian appears as surety.

Although the MRPS and the TVET Manual no longer provide for this, it is submitted that students are entitled to a full refund of fees for any course or subject that has been discontinued by the school, or which was not credited by the DepEd, CHED or TESDA.

Values – patience, self-confidence, appreciation and respect for others 2.5. Sportsmanship – right spirit of competitiveness, grace and composure before defeat and victory III. Requirements for Outside Competitions 1. original and photocopy of Birth Certificate 2. 2 x 2 pictures (4 pcs.) 3. Medical Certification from the family doctor and the School Physician IV. Benefits 1. Grades-98 in PE subject during the quarter(s) that they have competition. If the competition happens outside during school days, their grades in other subjects must not be lower than that of the previous grading period provided that they comply with all the requirements given by the subject teachers.
2. Allowance - meal allowance during competition 3. Sports uniform 4. Special Awards - for selected players only

Preamble We, the students of Rogationist College - High School, with the help of God, and believing in the need for a better organized student organization, and in the development of the youth as future leaders of the nation, hereby form a unified student organization that shall embody the ideals and principles of democracy, in collective efforts to promote the welfare of all students and the academic standards of our Alma Mater, do hereby promulgate and adopt this constitution and by-laws that will promote, implement, and maintain our goals and aspirations.

General Provisions Sec. 1 This Constitution and By-Laws shall be known as the Constitution of the Student Body Organization of Rogationist College – High School Department. Sec. 2 For purposes of this Constitution and By-Laws, SBO refers to the Student Body Organization of Rogationist College – High School Department.
