Gaspare Gallitto Conference Room – located on the ground floor of Fr. Palma Building. It can accommodate 15 persons. 4.3. Fr. Joseph Aveni Conference Room – located in Fr. Vitale Building. It is usually used for School Board and School Council meetings. It can accommodate 20 persons. 4.4. St. Therese Multimedia Room – located on the 2^(nd) floor of HS Building A, Fr. Vitale Building. It can accommodate 40 persons. 4.5. St. Bernadette Multi-media Room – located on the ground floor of Fr. Levi Building. It can accommodate 40 persons. 4.6. St. Claire Multi-media Room – located in Fr. Levi Building. It can accommodate 40 persons. Reservation of the conference rooms should be made with the Property Custodian three (3) days before their use. The HS Multi-media rooms may be reserved through the faculty in-charge. Students’ request for the use of conference rooms and multi-media rooms is honored only if noted by the teachers/instructors in-charge of the subject.

I. Audio-Visual Materials and Equipment 1. The faculty and students can borrow any of the audio-visual materials. 2. All audio-visual materials are for school, library, and classroom use only. 3. Request and reservation of the audio-visual materials should be forwarded to the Librarian at least three (3) days before their use. 4. Request of students for audio-visual materials is honored only if noted by the teachers/instructors in charge of the subject. 5. For teachers/instructors, audio-visual materials can be taken out only for an overnight use. Penalty for overdue materials will be imposed. II. Di Francia Auditorium and Audio-Visual Room (AVR) 1. The reservation/request slip for the use of the Di Francia Auditorium or Audio-Visual Room must be accomplished and submitted to the Property Custodian at least one week before the proposed activity (program, film viewing, etc.) 2. The program of activities and list of audio-visual materials needed must be given to the Property Custodian before the activity. 3. Facilities and other materials and equipment should be cleaned and properly arranged after their use. 4. Lights and air conditioning units should be turned off after the activity.

5. The “NO EATING, NO DRINKING” policy shall be strictly implemented. 6. Any problem encountered during the activity, especially equipment which is not functioning properly, should be immediately brought to the attention of the control room technician/library staff. 7. Students and teachers shall be held accountable for any damage done to any of the equipment used. III. Learning Resource Centers (LRC) 1. LRC schedule: Monday to Friday (7:30 am - 6:00 pm); Saturday (8:00 am- 12:00 noon) 2. Students may avail of the following services: 2.1. Library Orientation 2.2. Library Instruction 2.3. Library Exhibits 2.4. Library Guides 2.5. Reference and Information Services 2.6. Current Events Awareness 2.7. Reader Advisory Guidance 2.8. Searching, Reserving and Stack Service 2.9. Inter-Library Loan 2.10. Compiling Bibliographies upon request 2.11. Reader Word Power Corner 2.12. Film Viewing 3. The following non-print materials/services are available at the Instructional Media Center (IMC): 3.1. Overhead Projectors 3.2. Multimedia Materials 3.3. Visual Aids 4. A photocopying machine is also available at the LRC. 5. Rules Governing the Use of the Internet Access Room: 5.1. To access information from the internet access room, faculty and students should present their validated school ID at the circulation counter before using the internet terminals.

5.2. The Internet is used strictly for researches. 5.3. Use of computer is limited to one hour per session. (Repetition is possible but not in immediate succession.) 5.4. Preparing/typing of projects such as reaction and term papers, thesis or drawing in the computer is not allowed. 5.5. Printing and downloading of researched data or information may be requested at the circulation counter. 5.6. The “NO EATING, NO DRINKING” policy shall be strictly implemented. 5.7. CD-ROM formats and other multi-media software are available upon request at the circulation counter. 5.8. Students who violate these rules shall be subjected to disciplinary action. 6. Rules and Regulations in the LRC 6.1. All students of Rogationist College may borrow any learning resource material from the LRC by presenting a valid school ID. 6.2. SILENCE must be strictly observed. 6.3. The following are strictly prohibited inside the LRC: a. sleeping b. littering c. using electronic gadgets (cellphones, camera, MP3 players, Ipod, etc.) 6.4. Group study or group research may be done in the Discussion Room with reservation. 6.5. The library implements the Open Shelves Control System and uses the Online Public Access Catalogue (OPAC).

6.6. General references, pamphlets, newspapers, magazines or other periodical materials (loose or bound) and rare collections are read only inside the LRC. 6.7. Students are not allowed to bring camera or cellphone with camera inside the Thesis Collections Area. 6.8. Students are held responsible for the loss or damage of any learning material borrowed from the LRC. 6.9. No student is allowed to use the LRC and any of its resources unless all due accounts are settled. 6.10. Chairs and tables should be arranged properly after use. 6.11. Any problem encountered in the LRC should be reported to the Librarian or any of his staff for assistance. 6.12. No photograph may be taken in the reading areas without authorized permission from the Librarian. 6.13. Students must deposit their belongings at the baggage area. 6.14. Any student found violating any of the above-stated policies shall be referred to the Office of Student Discipline. 7. Rule on Circulation Books may be borrowed for three (3) days and may be renewed for another three (3) days provided they are not in demand. 8. Rules on “Reserved” Books

8.1. Due to limited copies, “Reserved” books may be used only for a certain time (1 hour) in the LRC. 8.2. “Reserved” books may be borrowed only during the last period in the afternoon. These should be returned not later than 9:00 a.m. the following day. 9. Materials for “Library Use Only” 9.1. General Reference Materials 9.1.1. Encyclopedia 9.1.2. Dictionaries 9.1.3. Atlases 9.1.4. Almanac 9.1.5. Periodicals 9.2. Non-Print Materials

9.2.2. Audio CD/DVD 9.2.3. Multimedia CDs 9.2.4. Audio cassettes tapes 9.2.5. Transparencies 9.2.6. Slides 9.2.7. VHS tapes 10. Fines and Other Penalties 10.1. For overdue regular, fiction and reference books, a fine of P5.00/day including Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays will be charged. 10.2. For overdue reserved books, a fine of P5.00/hour including Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays will be charged. 10.3. Unauthorized taking out of LRC materials is punishable by suspension of LRC privileges. In addition, the case will be reported to the Office of Student Discipline. 11. Lost Books Lost books should be reported immediately to the Librarian. Otherwise, the lost book will be considered as overdue and the borrower will have to pay the overdue fine. Aside from the cost of the lost book (or replacement with the same book), a processing fee of P200.00 shall also be charged. 12. Disfiguring of Library Materials Students who disfigure (mutilate and/or mark) any library materials, whether book or periodical, shall be suspended from borrowing books for one month and will be fined P100.00 per page or replacement of the same material. In addition, the case will be referred to the Office for Student Discipline.
All penalties and fines should be settled and paid at the Cashier’s Office.

1. Computer Laboratories There are six computer laboratories: two computer laboratories for the high school department, three for the college and technical education departments and one for speech classes. The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the Computer Laboratories: 1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their computer class. 2. The following are prohibited inside the computer rooms: 1.2.1. Food and drinks 1.2.2. Laptops and other electronic gadgets 1.2.3. Using of computer for games 1.2.4. Playing with computer peripherals/accessories 1.2.5. Copying (uploading/downloading) any program from the computer 1.2.6. Opening and attempting to repair any computer 1.2.7. Use of computer hardware and accessories outside the laboratory 1.3.Students should use only their designated computer units. 1.4. Care must be observed while using the equipment in the laboratory. Everything must be returned to its proper place after use. 2. Science Laboratories There are two science laboratories for the College Department, the Chemistry and Physics Laboratories. For the High School Department, there are four science laboratories: General Science, Biology, Chemistry and Physics Laboratories. These are provided with the necessary equipment, instruments, gadgets, utensils, tools, supplies and materials. These laboratories enable the students to gain adequate learning experiences on the theories and principles taught in the classroom through laboratory exercises and experiments.

The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the Science Laboratories: 2.1. Unauthorized persons are not allowed to enter the laboratories. 2.2. Vandalism and littering as well as eating and drinking are prohibited in the laboratories. 2.3. Laboratory seats should be arranged at all times. 2.4. Bags, books and the like should be placed on designated areas. Working tables should be reserved for laboratory materials/equipment needed in the experiment. 2.5. Cabinets in the laboratories can only be used as storage for laboratory paraphernalia. 2.6. Laboratory gowns and/or protective gear such as masks, goggles and gloves should be worn whenever necessary during experimentation. 2.7. After each laboratory activity, the subject teacher/students should check that: 2.7.1. All borrowed laboratory equipment/materials are returned clean, dry and in good working condition. 2.7.2. Working tables are clean and dry. 2.7.3. Sinks are free from lumps. Faucets, gas outlets, lights and ceiling fans are turned off. 2.7.4. Chairs are properly arranged. 2.7.5. Writing on the boards is erased. 2.7.6. Laboratory wastes, chemicals and plant and animal specimens are disposed at designated areas of the laboratory.

2.8. Any untoward incident related to laboratory activities shall be reported by the students to the subject teacher/instructor or laboratory assistant in charge. 2.9. A subject teacher/instructor/laboratory assistant who has knowledge of any untoward incident should prepare a concise incident report which contains the exact date, time and persons involved. 2.10. Any subject teacher/instructor/laboratory assistant who fails to submit the incident report within 48 hours shall be held accountable for the cost of the damage. 2.11. The incident report shall be submitted in 3 copies to the Property Custodian, Science Subject Area Coordinator and Principal or Cluster Coordinator/TED Head for appropriate action. 2.12. In cases of breakage of materials or damage to equipment/facilities, policies stipulate in the Students Manual shall be applied. 2.13. Students who fail to return borrowed material/equipment will not be allowed to borrow again without first settling their responsibility. 2.14. For loss/breakage/damage of laboratory material/equipment, the student should pay through the Cashier’s Office the exact amount as determined by the Property Custodian/Purchasing Officer. The official receipt (O.R.) should then be presented to the Laboratory Assistant/Subject Teacher/Instructor for clearance signing.

3. Technical Laboratories There are six technical laboratories. The Automotive, Mechanical, Welding, and Pneumatics Laboratories are located in Fr. Levi Building. The Electronics and Electrical Laboratories are found in Fr. Palma Building. These are equipped with industry standard facilities and training materials to ensure transfer of learning and skills to students. These laboratories are also made available to High School students for their Technology and Livelihood Education subjects. The following are the rules and regulations inside the Technical Laboratories: 3.1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their technical and practical classes.All scientific and technical works or projects must be performed in the respective laboratories. 3.2. Procedures prescribed by the subject teacher or instructor must be strictly followed. 3.3. Equipment, tools or materials may be borrowed from the stockroom only after accomplishing a borrower’s slip. 3.4. Utmost care must be observed when using any of the equipment, tools or chemicals in the laboratories. The students shall be held responsible for any damage done to any of the equipment, instruments or tools used. 3.5. Students are not allowed to use or take any of the equipment, tools or materials outside the laboratories.

3.6. Students should deposit their personal belongings in the lockers provided outside the laboratories. 4. Technology and Livelihood Education (TLE) Laboratory The TLE Laboratory is located in Fr. Bonarrigo Building. It is equipped with sewing, housekeeping, baking, and cooking equipment. The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the TLE Laboratory: 4.1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their TLE class. 4.2. Students should wear proper attire while doing the activities in the laboratory. 4.3. Moving from one working area to another without the permission of the subject teacher, and playing or running are strictly prohibited. 4.4. Care must be observed while using any of the utensils and equipment in the laboratory. In case a student or a group of students accidentally or intentionally breaks an equipment or utensil, the said student or group is required to replace it. 4.5. Students should use equipment in the laboratory under the supervision of the subject teacher. 4.6. Students should provide their own cleaning materials (i.e. dishwashing liquid, dishwashing foam/pad, cleaning rags and garbage bag). 4.7. Order and cleanliness must be observed in the laboratory. Trash must be properly disposed.

4.8. Unauthorized taking out of any utensil or equipment is considered a major offense with corresponding disciplinary action. 5. Drawing Rooms There are two drawing rooms located on the second floor of Fr. Palma Building. Each room contains sixteen drawing tables and is provided with necessary drawing tools. Rules and Regulations on the Use of the Drawing Room: 5.1. Only students with drawing subjects are allowed to use the room and borrow drawing instruments. 5.2. Borrowed instruments should be used only inside the drawing room. 5.3. Students must maintain the orderliness and cleanliness of the drawing room. 5.4. Students are responsible for any damage or loss of the instruments and tables assigned to them. 6. Cassetti Mini-Hotel The mini-hotel is one of the laboratories for THRM students. It has a front office, a reception area, a tourism office, two standard bedrooms with comfort rooms, a suite complete with a receiving area, a kitchen, comfort room, porch and household appliances and furnishings. Rules and Regulations on the Use of the Cassetti Mini-Hotel: 6.1. The management is not responsible for any loss of personal properties.

6.2. Guests and students should not move furnishings or interfere with the electrical network or any other installations in the hotel. 6.3. Equipment and appliances should be turned off before leaving. 6.4. Order and cleanliness must be observed in the mini-hotel. Trash must be properly disposed. 6.5. Students are responsible for any damage or loss in the mini-hotel. 7. Hotel and Restaurant Management Laboratory Together with the Mini-Hotel, the HRM laboratory is used to facilitate the learning of skills associated with restaurant management. It is adjacent to the Munch Canteen and is provided with the necessary equipment for restaurant operations. The following rules and regulations must be observed inside the HRM Laboratory: 7.1. Students must wear the prescribed laboratory uniform during working sessions. 7.2. Students are required to stay in their assigned working areas. 7.3. Cleanliness and orderliness must be maintained in the laboratory. 8. Caregiving Laboratory This is located adjacent to Avignone Clinic and is equipped with training facilities for Caregiving and Health Care services. The following rules and regulations must be observed in the Caregiving Laboratory: 8.1. Students are allowed inside the laboratory only during their Caregiving class.

8.2. Students should wear proper attire while doing the activities in the laboratory. 8.3. Care must be observed while using the equipment in the laboratory. In case a student or a group of students accidentally or intentionally breaks a piece of equipment, the said student or group is required to replace it. 8.4. Order and cleanliness must be observed in the laboratory. Trash must be properly disposed.

The home shall fully support the school in the implementation of the total school program - curricular and co-curricular - toward the proper physical, social, intellectual and moral development of the child. -Article76. The Child and Youth Welfare Code (Presidential Decree No. 603, s. 1974)

1. The rules and regulations of RC as stated in this Handbook are intended to enhance the life in school of an RC student as he relates and interacts with the members of the school community. As such, it is understood that they are mutual good role models of each other. 2. It is the duty and responsibility of the parents and/or guardians to keep track of the progress of their children/wards in school. The parents and/or guardians are encouraged to confer with the school authorities at their own volition or whenever calls for conference are issued to them. This is to enhance the harmonious working relationship between the school and the home for the welfare of the student. 3. The enrollment of a student in RC is taken as an expressed willingness on his/her part, and consequently of his/her parents and/or guardians, to abide by all rules and regulations of the school. Thus, the student and his/her parents and/or guardians are committed to the strict observance of the same. 4. RC reserves the right to admit, readmit, refuse admission or exclude a student or drop the name of an erring student from the school rolls on the basis of his/her academic performance, conduct or attendance.

5. RC acknowledges its obligations to exercise reasonable supervision over the conduct of the student and to cultivate the best potentialities of the heart and mind of the student. Its role in “loco parentis” is the exercise of substitute parental authority over students in the school and in school-related activities (Civil Code, Art. 349). 6. RC, as a Catholic school, strongly respects and adheres to the practice of holy sacrament (matrimony) and does not tolerate sexual indiscretions. Violation of this policy would merit the student appropriate disciplinary action, including but not limited to, requiring the student to go on leave or will be excluded or dropped from the school rolls. 7. RC expects its students to uphold the standards of responsibility and dignity. When a student of RC does not measure up to these standards, he/she will be excluded or dropped from the school rolls after due process. 8. Students, either as individuals or as a group, must not use the name and seal of the school without official authorization. 9. Students who are using the social media in their respective homes are not to make inappropriate comments (including in private messages) about the school personnel or other students.

10. Parents or guardians may consult or confer with teachers and instructors provided they secure appointments with the Department Head (Principal, Dean or TED Head) two days before the actual date of appointment. Concerns and/or complaints must be written and directly addressed to proper school authority rather than posting them on social media – whether on their own pages, in closed groups (e.g. groups set up for school parents to communicate with each other) or on the school's pages. Complaint posted on social media will not be entertained by the school. 11. Parents, guardians or visitors are not allowed to go to the classrooms. Messages and allowance for the students must be coursed through the Guidance Office. 12. Students may be called out of the classrooms provided an approved written permission/call slip is issued by either of the following: 12.1. Rector/Vice-Rector 12.2. Director for Academic Affairs (DAA) 12.3. Director for Student Services (DSS) 12.4. Director for Spiritual Affairs (DSA) 12.4. Principal/Dean/Technical Education Department Head (TED Head) 12.5. Vice Principal/Vice Dean 12.6. Guidance Counselor/Facilitator 12.7. Prefect of Discipline/Discipline Officer 12.8. Health Services Coordinator/Nurse

13. As a Catholic School, with Rogationist Formation as the core of the curriculum, RC requires all students to attend and pass all the requirements of Christian Living Education or Religious Education subjects. Students also need to attend masses and/or similar activities and complete spiritual recollections and retreats scheduled by the institution. In addition, parents of High School students are required to follow the agreement (to attend/participate in parents’ formation programs, PTA assemblies, etc.) signed during the enrolment of their children. 14. The “No ID, no entry” policy is strictly implemented. The school ID is required for the admittance of students and personnel to the school premises. For parents or other visitors, a visitor’s ID is issued by the guard in exchange for a valid identification card, which is returned after a legitimate business transaction or visit inside the campus. Visitors will be charged for lost visitor’s ID. 15. High School students will stay inside the campus from the moment of their arrival in the morning until their dismissal time in the afternoon. They cannot leave the school premises unless they have written permission from their parents and/or they have secured a gate pass from the Discipline Office duly noted by the Homeroom Adviser and approved by the Principal. In the absence of the Principal, the Prefect of Discipline signs the gate pass. In case of sickness/medical concern, the School Nurse will issue the gate pass.

16. The privacy of certain areas in the campus should be respected by the students. The areas where students are not allowed to stay or loiter are: 16.1. Religious community’s residence and interns’ dormitories 16.2. Refectory, kitchen, lavatory, and carpentry shop 16.3. All laboratories except during scheduled classes and/or when permitted by the Principal/Dean/TED Head 16.4. Fr. Vitale Administration Building, except for official business 16.5. Faculty rooms 16.6. High School classrooms and corridors during recess, lunch and after dismissal time, unless under the supervision of a teacher or with specific permission from the Prefect of Discipline/Discipline Officer. 17. Everyone is enjoined to keep the campus clean at all times. Thus, littering is strictly prohibited. There are waste bins around the campus for proper waste disposal. 18. Everybody should respect, maintain and safeguard the school physical plant. Any damages must be reported immediately to the Office of the General Services. 19. Students are obliged to use English as a medium of communication. 20. Everyone is expected to be courteous and respectful at all times especially to visitors and treat others in a

positive and considerate manner. 21. Students must exhibit proper behavior at all times in all places. When the behavior of a student adversely affects the integrity and objectives of the school, he/she will be subjected to disciplinary action. 22. Using the school website, official Facebook page or RC ID System, announcements are made from time to time to keep the students abreast of school issues and procedures. Students should relay to their parents all announcements which concern them. Likewise, the school gives out regular and/or timely communications or correspondence to parents. The parents are earnestly requested to acknowledge every communication by filling-up out the reply/return slips/parental consents and returning them to the school through their children. 23. Parents/Students are discouraged to post photos or videos that include other children at the school on their personal social media account. 24. In case of misunderstanding between or among the students, parents of the concerned students should not do any drastic action or in any way harass the other concerned students. Such occurrences will be settled according to the policies and guidelines stipulated in this handbook. In addition to this, cooperation of all stakeholders is needed to maintain and promote trust, respect, and dignity of all students, parents/guardians, teachers, and administrators of the school.

25. An activity permit signed by the teacher-in-charge, noted by the Student Affairs Coordinator, and approved by the Principal/Dean/TED Head must be secured by students at least two days before any school activity/practice during non-class days. This form which can be obtained from the Student Affairs Coordinator should be signed by their parents and returned to the teacher-in-charge a day before the approved activity/practice. In this way, parents are properly informed and could monitor their children’s activities. 26. Students who wish to participate in any outside activity as representatives of the school should secure approval from the school administration. 27. In cases of emergency, or for valid reasons, high school students may bring cellular phones or other gadgets provided there is a letter of permission from the parents. These gadgets will be surrendered to the subject teacher, adviser or discipline officer right after the morning assembly and will be retrieved after classes in the afternoon. College students however, may bring their cellular phones but they should refrain from using these inside the classrooms, library or during school hours and liturgical celebrations.

28. High School students tasked to bring cellphone, laptop, netbook, camera or any gadget/device must deposit the gadget/device to the Office for Student Discipline or to the subject teacher during the first period. The gadget/device must be used only during the class activity and only by its owner. Unauthorized use of a gadget/device may result in disciplinary action and confiscation of the gadget/device. A confiscated item shall be released only to the student’s parent/legal guardian. 29. Taking into consideration the educational system of RC and the promotion of an environment that is conducive to learning, the Discipline Officer, together with the subject teacher or adviser, may conduct inspection as the need arises. 30. Parents or students who wish to request for school forms or documents such as ESC Certificates, Form 137/ SF10, Certificate of Enrolment, Certificate of Grades, Certification of Good Moral Character and/or Rank, and Recommendation Letter, must apply for these at least a week before actual claim to give ample time for the preparation of such forms or documents. Formal request letter must be submitted to the concerned offices and attach proof of requirements. Online (e-mail) or phone call request may be accommodated provided that proof of requirement is presented upon claiming. A minimal amount will be charged.

31. In order to be allowed to enter the school premises, students’ vehicles/school service vehicles must have the official school sticker which may be secured at the Accounting Office. 32. The Office for Student Discipline will inform parents/guardians in writing about a student’s case and may require the parents to come personally for proper disposition of the said case. 33. Parents visiting the school are required to wear modest/proper clothes. 34. No students or visitors, including parents or guardians, shall be allowed inside the school building and the premises after the last class period has ended. (DepEd Order No. 11 s. 2011) 35. A student shall be responsible for informing his parents/guardians of the following: 35.1. School policies and guidelines stated in this handbook. 35.2. Student’s academic standing and the possible consequences of his excessive absences, dropping, failures or gross misbehavior.

Classes are suspended in the following situations: 1. Typhoon warning signal is raised by PAGASA in the area of Cavite. Signal no. 2 automatically suspends classes in the secondary level while signal no. 3 automatically suspends classes in the tertiary level. Depending on signal numbers declared at 10:00 pm and 4:30 am of the following day, classes in appropriate levels for the whole day are deemed automatically cancelled/suspended. (DepEd Order No. 43 series 2012). 2. Natural calamities or disturbances compromising the safety of the students; 3. Rector’s announcement; 4. Cancellation of classes by DepEd, TESDA or CHED; 5. National, Provincial, and Municipal proclamations N.B. Afternoon classes in the appropriate levels in areas with signal numbers declared at 11:00 am that day will be cancelled or suspended at 2:00 pm to ensure the safety of the students and to provide ample time for the school authorities to contact school service providers and/or the parents. In addition to this, during heavy rains affecting the health or safety of their children, parents have the discretion not to send their children to school;

1. Tuition fees and other charges are prescribed by the school authorities. These charges are posted in the Bulletin of Information. 2. Parents and students enter into agreement with the school regarding the mode of payment of tuition and other fees. 3. It is the obligation of the parents and students to update themselves with regard to the status of their accounts by consulting the Finance and Administration Department 4. Examination permit for the JHS & SHS and by the Cashier for the College/TED students. This should be signed by the Cashier two weeks before each major examination. It is recommended that accounts be settled at least two weeks before the scheduled examination period to avoid inconvenience and delay. 5. Tuition fees and other charges for transferring or withdrawing students shall be governed by the following provisions:

When a student registers in a school, it is understood that he/she is enrolling for the entire school year for secondary courses. (DepEd Order No. 88 series 2010: Revised Manual of Regulations for Private Schools. Section 119. Rules for Registration) thus, a student who transfers or otherwise withdraws, in writing, within two weeks after the beginning of classes and who has already paid the pertinent tuition and other fees in full or for any length of time longer than one month may be charged 10% of the total amount due for the term if he/she withdraws within the 1^(st) week of classes, or 20% if within the 2^(nd) week of classes, regardless of whether or not he has actually attended classes. The student may be charged all the school fees in full if he/she withdraws any time after the 2^(nd) week of classes. However, if the transfer or withdrawal is due to justifiable reason, the student shall be charged the pertinent fees only up to and including the last month of attendance.

For College students: Manual of Regulations for Private Higher Education Section 100. Tuition Charges – A student who transfers or otherwise withdraws, in writing, within two weeks after the beginning of classes and who has already paid the pertinent tuition and other fees in full or for any length of time longer than one month may be charged 25% of the total amount due for the term if he/she withdraws within the 1^(st) week of classes, or 50% if within the 2^(nd) week of classes, regardless of whether or not he has actually attended classes. The student may be charged all the school fees in full if he withdraws any time after the 2^(nd) week of classes.

Mission The College Department commits itself to: - Form members who will uphold the core values of Rogationist College; - Offer a dynamic curriculum, quality instruction, conducive environment and up-to-date facilities that address the needs of the community; - Produce professionals who are globally competitive and internationally recognized; - Promote social responsibility and preferential option for the poor, especially the children

I. Pre-enrollment Procedure: 1. Secure an Application Form from the Registrar’s Office. 2. Fill out the Application Form for the entrance examination. 3. Present the Application Form to the Cashier’s Office and pay the required entrance examination fee. 4. Present the proof of payment and Application Form to the Registrar who shall then inform the student of the date of the entrance examination. 5. Present the test permit to the Guidance Office on the scheduled entrance examination date. Examination results will be released and posted in the bulletin board and on the school’s website (www.rog.edu.ph) and on the school’s official Facebook account one week after the examination. Applicants may visit or call the Guidance Office for verification. II. Enrollment Procedure: 1. Report to the Registrar’s Office for the evaluation of requirements. 2. Report to the Course Coordinator for academic advising (both freshmen and transferees). 2.1. Report to the Scholarship Coordinator. (For scholarship grantees only) 3. Report to the Guidance Office for interview. 4. Report to the School Nurse for medical interview. 5. Proceed to the Registrar’s Office for registration and assessment of tuition and other fees.
6. Proceed to the Cashier’s Office for payment. 7. Submit Registration Form to the Registrar’s Office for validation and ID application.

I. Types of Scholarship Grants/Aids Percentage discounts on all scholarships grants shall apply only to the tuition fee. 1. Honor Students 1.1. Valedictorian – 100% 1.2. Salutatorian – 50% 1.3. With Honors (First, Second, Third) – 25% 2. Academic Scholarship This tuition fee discount is granted on a per semester basis and in accordance with the conditions/guidelines set by the Dean/TED Head. As general guideline, student applicants’ must have at least 1.50 GWA and Dean’s List for two (2) consecutive semesters. 3. Employees’ Legal Dependents’ Discount All full-time employees who have rendered at least 1 year of service to the SABV, RC are entitled to 50% tuition fee discount in Rogationist College for all their legal dependents/beneficiaries. Legal dependents/beneficiaries refer to the employees’ brothers, sisters and children. Tuition fee discounts shall only be granted for a period no longer than the duration of the course/program in which the beneficiary has originally enrolled. 4. Family Discount For brothers and sisters enrolled at the same time within a school year, the 2^(nd) child and each of the succeeding children will receive a 5% discount in the tuition fee.

This discount does not apply to employees of SABV, RC. 5. St. Anthony’s Boys Village Grantees’ and Interns’ Discount This is granted to less-privileged youths chosen by the SABV community. According to the by-laws of SABV-RC, the Village interns are considered children or beneficiaries of the Institution who are entitled to the benefit of 50% discount in the tuition fee. 6. Student Assistantship Tuition fee discount/assistance is granted to students (incoming freshmen from low-income families) who pass the screening standards/guidelines for student assistantship set by the school authorities. Grantees shall be assigned to assist/render service in the different offices/departments/laboratories. 7. Government Administered Scholarships These are scholarships granted by the following government agencies, subject to the guidelines as stipulated in the contracts:

7.3. LGU/District/Provincial/National 8. Private Companies and Organizations N.B. In case a student qualifies for two or more scholarship grants or aids, the one with the highest benefit applies. No monetary refund will be allowed. II. General Qualifications for Scholarship Grants/Aids 1. The grantee must enroll the regular load as specified in his/her curriculum. 2. He must have passed all the subjects enrolled in the previous semester or term. 3. He must pass the selection process of the concerned scholarship program or grantee group. III. Privileges Full and/or discounted tuition and laboratory fees depend on the number of units enrolled for the current semester or term. These privileges also depend on the scholarship availed of.

I. Academic Year The academic year for semester-based subjects is divided into two (2) terms of 18 weeks each, inclusive of examination periods and class days lost due to natural or man-made calamities. A summer session of six (6) weeks follows the second semester. For non-semester-based programs, the academic year is based on the number of modules or blocks offered per program. The school calendar shall serve as the guide for the schedule of all academic and non-academic activities, unless a change is made by the school officials. II. Study Load Students’ academic loads are prescribed for all regular and irregular students. 1. Term Load 1.1. For regular students, the term load is as prescribed in the curriculum 1.2. For irregular students, the term load must not exceed the corresponding number of units prescribed for the year level based on the curriculum. 2. Summer Load The summer load should not exceed three (3) subjects. 3. Underload 3.1. Underload is any load below the number of units prescribed in the curriculum. 3.2. Students may be allowed to have underload on the following conditions:

3.2.1. Employed either in or out of school 3.2.2. Probationary or warning status 3.2.3. Health reasons 3.2.4. Unavailability of subjects needed in the curriculum to complete the full load 4. Overload Overload is any load beyond the number of units prescribed in the curriculum. A student may be allowed to have overload on the following conditions: 4.1. Graduating student in his/her last term of attendance 4.2 Irregular Student/Transferee Student that needs to cope-up with missed subjects from his/her existing program. A maximum overload of 6 units may be allowed, subject to the endorsement of the Program Chair and the approval of the Dean/TED Head. III. Change of Matriculation Each type of change requires a different set of documentation and authorization. 1. Change of Subject and Load Students are allowed to change subjects or schedules within two (2) weeks after the start of classes. Subjects cancelled during this period will not appear in the student’s transcript of records. Steps necessary to effect the change are as follows: 1.1. Accomplishment of the Change of Matriculation Form 1.2. Program Chair/TED Head’s endorsement 1.3. Re-assessment of fees and approval from the Registrar’s Office

1.4. Payment to the Cashier’s Office 1.5. Submission of completed form to the Office of the Registrar 1.6. Official “stamping” of the student’s copy by the Registrar’s Office 2. Dropping of Subjects Students are allowed to drop a subject without being given a failing grade in the subject before the midterm examination. The transcript will contain a grade of Dropped or “DRP” for the subject, earning for the students zero credits. Steps for dropping of subject/s are as follows: 2.1. Accomplishment of the Student’s Dropping Form 2.2. Instructor’s approval of the subject to be dropped 2.3. Endorsement of the Program Chair 2.4. Approval of the Dean /TED Head 2.5. Notation of the Registrar 2.6. Payment of processing fee at the Cashier’s Office 2.7. Submission of completed form to the Office of the Registrar 2.8. Official “stamping” of the student’s Dropping Form. 3. Shifting of Academic Programs Students are allowed to shift their academic program as long as they satisfy the admission requirements of the particular program. Program “shifted” takes effect on the semester indicated in the form. Steps necessary to effect the change are as follows:

3.1. Accomplishment of the application for program change 3.2. Consent from the parent or guardian 3.3. Program Chair’s endorsement 3.4. Validation and approval from the Dean’s/TED’s Office 3.5. Official “stamping” of the student’s copy by the Registrar’s Office 4. Refund of Fees (for verification with DFA) A refund of fees shall be made only in accordance with the following rules: 4.1. A duly enrolled student who wishes to drop one or more subjects or his entire load, or to withdraw from the school and obtain a refund, must give an accomplished Dropping Form to the DFA, copy furnished the Dean/TED Head and the Registrar. This must be done within three weeks from the first day of classes during the regular semester and within the first week of classes during summer term. Beyond this period, no refund will be allowed. 4.2. If the student files the required dropping notice within the first week after the opening of classes during the regular semester and within the first three days of the summer term, the student shall be entitled to a refund of 90% of the tuition fee paid for the subject/s dropped.

4.3. If the student files the required dropping notice within the second and third week after the opening of classes during the regular semester or after the third day up to the sixth day of summer classes, the student shall be entitled to a refund of 80% of the tuition fee paid for the subject/s dropped. 5. Refund without deduction Full refund or credit adjustments shall be made when the class is dissolved or discontinued. 6. Official Dropping Without Refund Official dropping forms shall be accomplished and filed with the Registrar any time before the start of the midterm examinations, provided the student has not incurred more than the allowable absences. 7. Consequences of Load Withdrawal/ Dropping without Notice A student who drops one or more subjects without filing the required dropping form shall receive a grade of 5.0 (failed) and shall be charged the total assessment or the corresponding assessment for the subject/s dropped. IV. Attendance 1. General Guidelines 1.1. All students are required to attend classes regularly and punctually. If and when the student is tardy or absent, he/she is expected to assume full responsibility for the subject matter taught, discussed and assigned.

To illustrate: A student is not allowed to exceed 7 class hours of unexcused absences in a 2-unit lecture subject or 22 laboratory hours in a 2-unit laboratory subject. For a 4-unit class with 3 units of lecture and 1 unit of laboratory, a student must not incur unexcused absences of more than 11 lecture hours nor more than 11 laboratory hours. 2.3. Three (3) instances of tardiness are equivalent to one (1) absence. 2.4. Time lost due to late enrolment is considered time lost by absence unless these steps are accomplished: 2.4.1. The student applies for his absence to be excused 2.4.2. The faculty considers the absence excused 3. Excused Absences 3.1. Excused absences are limited to the following cases: 3.1.1. Indisposed due to sickness, certified by an attending physician 3.1.2. Death of next of kin (grandparent, parent, brother, sister, spouse, or guardian) subject to verification by the Discipline Officer. 3.1.3. Other special cases deemed meritorious by the Dean/TED Head and approved by the DAA. 3.2. Claims for excused absences must be filed within the term. 4. Waiting Period

4.1. An instructor is considered absent only after the fifteen-minute grace period has elapsed. 4.2. A student who leaves the classroom before the waiting period has elapsed will be considered absent if the instructor arrives within the stipulated waiting period. V. Leave of Absence (LOA) A student is expected to enroll each semester until he/she completes the course or is dropped from the rolls. When a student cannot enroll in the succeeding semester, he/she must file in writing for an official leave of absence with the Registrar’s Office before the end of the currently enrolled term wherein the leave starts. The maximum leave period that may be applied for in a single application is one (1) academic year. However, the total duration of all leaves taken must not exceed the length of the program. 1. Conditions for LOA 1.1. Leaves are officially granted for the following reasons: 1.1.1. Death of an immediate member of the family (spouse, children, parents, brothers, sisters or guardians) as certified by a copy of the death certificate 1.1.2. Attendance in approved seminars sponsored or recognized by CHED or TESDA

1.1.3. Poor health as certified by the school physician or any duly registered physician. 1.1.4. Any other reason deemed acceptable by the Dean/TED Head. 2. Students applying for LOA must accomplish the Leave of Absence Form from the Registrar’s Office. Necessary supporting documents (e.g. medical certificate) must be attached to this form. 1.3. Extension of Leave Any extension of an official leave is considered as another leave application. As such, the leave extension must be formally applied for in writing. For the purpose of computing the maximum residency status, the duration of official LOA is not counted as residency. 1.4. Return to School A student shall be classified as a Returnee upon his return from an approved leave and he shall enroll with this status. 2. AWOL Status A student who takes an unofficial or disapproved leave is placed on AWOL (Absence without Official Leave) status. Any AWOL period is included in the reckoning of a student’s maximum residency. The school reserves the right to refuse automatic admission of a student upon his/her return. A student who is refused automatic admission is required to officially apply for readmission.

The following are the requirements for readmission: a. Letter from the student (noted by the parent/guardian, if the student is of minor age) b. Interview by the Program Chair c. Approval of the Dean/TED Head VI. Residency There are prescribed minimum and maximum periods of residency in order to acquire a degree at Rogationist College. 1. Minimum Residency 1.1. A student may graduate from any CHED academic program if he/she has completed at Rogationist College the major and core subjects of the last two (2) years of the program prior to graduation. 1.2. For TESDA-governed courses, the student must have completed at Rogationist College at least a year of the academic units excluding PE and NSTP. 2. Maximum Residency 2.1. A student must finish the requirements of a course within a period of actual residence equivalent to the length of the course plus an additional half (50%) of the total number of years of the course. 2.1.1. one-year course – not to exceed 1-¹/₂ years 2.1.2. two-year course – not to exceed 3 years 2.1.3. four-year course – not to exceed 6 years

2.2. In meritorious cases, as in the case of graduating students, the Dean/TED Head may extend the allowable period of maximum residency. VII. On-the-Job Training (OJT) Program A student who has completed all unit prerequisite to the program will be allowed to enroll in the OJT. The Program Chair shall recommend the enrollment of the student for approval of the Registrar and the Dean. 1. Purposes of the OJT: 1.1. provide the OJT student the opportunity to gain practical/hands-on experience in the field; 1.2. enhance the personality, confidence, human relations/communication and critical thinking skills of the OJT student; 1.3. inculcate in the OJT student the attitude of a responsible professional; and, 1.4. provide opportunities for the OJT student to integrate and synthesize the various theories of his/her course. 2. General Guidelines 2.1. Duration and Time: The student must complete the required minimum number of OJT hours as stated in the student’s curriculum. 2.2. Leave of Absence or Deferment of OJT: As a general rule, no deferment shall be allowed once a student has been deployed for OJT. However, for justifiable reasons and after due consultation with the Program Chair and the Partner Institution, the OJT Coordinator may allow a student a maximum period of six (6) months of deferment. The student should file the request for such deferment in written form.

The student trainees are not allowed to transfer or move to another company without notifying the OJT Supervisor, / External Relations Officer, and OJT Adviser. Violation of this provision will mean non-credit of the enrolled practicum subject. 2.3. Uniform: It is the prerogative of the Rogationist College to prescribe the necessary uniform for the OJT students provided that it is not identical with the uniform of the personnel of the Partner Institution. Such uniform shall bear a name patch on the upper left side bearing clearly the student’s surname and initials of the first and middle names together with the name of the related course. 2.4. Safety and Protection: Rogationist College (according to the provisions of the insurance coverage and other appropriate safety nets) and the Partner Institution shall ensure the safety and protection to life of the OJT students at all times during the OJT. 2.5. OJT tuition fee: Rogationist College collects tuition fee from the students who shall undertake the OJT, in conformity with the existing CHED/TESDA rules and regulations. 2.6. Venue: The venue for the OJT shall be near or within the vicinity of the School. However, other venues may be recommended by the OJT Coordinator with the advice of the Cluster Coordinator and approval of the Dean/TED Head.

3. School’s Responsibility: As a general rule, Rogationist College is responsible for: 3.1. making OJT arrangements with the Partner Institution through the External Relations Officer; 3.2. providing and ensuring the safety and protection of the OJT students; 3.3. setting and prescribing of institutional requirements and necessary forms to be accomplished by the OJT students; and 3.4. conducting periodic visits and dialogue with OJT students and regularly coordinating with the Partner Institution regarding the implementation of the OJT. 4. Grading System The OJT grade is derived from 75% of the grades earned from the periodic evaluation of the student’s on-the-job training by the OJT Supervisor and 25% of the grade given by the OJT Adviser. Grade = 0.60 (Grade from OJT Supervisor) + 0.40 (Grade from OJT Adviser) The evaluation shall adopt the following grading system: ---------- ------------ Grade Equivalent 98-100 1 95-97 1.25 92-94 1.5 89-91 1.75 86-88 2.00 83-85 2.25 80-82 2.5 77-79 2.75 75-76 3.00 below 75 5 ---------- ------------ A failing grade (5) shall mean the repetition of the OJT in another host company. The following conditions shall result to a failing grade in OJT:

4.1. Failure to submit requirements for OJT placement within the term as scheduled by the OJT Coordinator. 4.2. Failure to report on time on three separate occasions for interview or examination without justifiable reasons. 4.3. Failure to submit time sheets and evaluations for two consecutive evaluation periods. 4.4. Failing grades in two (2) consecutive evaluations from the partner institution. 4.5. Dropping of the student by the partner institution due to any of the following: dishonest/illegal acts, misconduct, tardiness/absences. These offenses will also constitute sanctions for major offense as provided in this Handbook. VIII. Examinations 1. Major Examinations For term-based subjects, there are three (3) major periodic examinations in a semester. These are: Prelims, Midterms and Finals. 2. Schedules The examination schedules are announced through the Office of the Dean at least one week before the actual examinations. Examination permits are issued two (2) weeks before the of the schedule of examinations. 3. Examination Permit Examination permits are required during major examinations. The “No permit, no examination” policy is strictly implemented. If account due for the term is not settled fully, the student can be given the examination permit provided a promissory note approved by DFA is presented to the Cashier.

4. Special Examinations Special examinations, due to conflict schedules, will be scheduled on the day of the examination from 3:00-5:00 pm. Special examinations, due to other valid reasons, will be scheduled a week after a major examination and must present special examination permit which may be secured from the Registrar’s Office. IX. Grading System and Earned Credits Grades are determined by averaging a student’s performance over the term for both lecture and laboratory. A failing grade may be given to a student who does not meet attendance requirements. 1. Grading System Grade Equivalent Description 98 - 100% 1.00 Excellent 95 - 97% 1.25 Very Good 92 - 94% 1.50 Very Good 89 - 91% 1.75 Good 86 - 88% 2.00 Good 83 - 85% 2.25 Satisfactory 80 - 82% 2.5 Satisfactory 77 - 79% 2.75 Fair 75 - 76% 3.00 Fair Below 75% 5.00 Failed DRP DRP Officially Dropped INC INC Incomplete 2. Subject Grade The subject grade is based on the percentage distribution for each periodical grade to be expressed in percentage form rounded to the nearest unit. Grade = Prelim (0.3) + Midterm (0.3)+ Final (0.3) + Final Output (0.1)

In subjects with a combination of lecture and laboratory, the subject grade is based on the proportion of lecture to laboratory units. Hence, the subject grade for a three (3) unit subject with two (2) units lecture and one (1) unit of laboratory shall be a ratio of 2:1, lecture : laboratory, and rounded off to the nearest numeric grade. 3. Periodical Grade Recommended periodical grade components: Major Examinations: 40% Class Standing: 60% 100% 4. General Weighted Average (GWA) Grades for all subjects prescribed in the curriculum are included in the computation of the GWA. Religious Education and National Service Training Programs subjects are assigned 1.5 units only for purposes of computing the GWA. The following are not included in the GWA computation: 4.1. non-numeric grade such as “INC” (Incomplete) and “DRP” (Dropped) 4.2. grades earned outside Rogationist College 5. Computation of the GWA Multiply the Final Grade (FG) by the Number of Units (Un) of each subject prescribed in the curriculum to get the Credit Points per Subject (CPS). Add all of the CPS and divide the sum by the Total Number of Units (TNU).

5.1. Add the credit points of all the subjects to get the total credit points (TCP) 5.2. Divide the total credit points by the total number of units of all the subjects, and round off to two (2) decimal places. CPS = Un x FG

6. Release of Subject Grades Report of subject grades will be released on the dates specified in the school calendar to students and parents without any pending accountability. 7. Completion of Incomplete Ratings Incomplete grades incurred in a subject must be completed within one (1) semester (45 days) from the time the grade was given or within the set period, by the office of the dean, for grade completion. Failure to remove an incomplete mark within the stipulated period or before the student transfers to another school will automatically result to a failing grade of 5.0 which shall be indicated in the Transcript of Records. Students forfeit the right to complete an incomplete grade even within the stipulated period once a Certificate of Transfer is issued to them. 7.1. Steps for Completion of Grades The steps to be followed for the completion of grades are as follows: 7.1.1. The student gets the application for completion from the Registrar’s Office. 7.1.2. The student fills out the form and confers with the faculty member concerned regarding the means of grade completion. In the absence of the faculty member, the student may confer with the Program Chair.

7.1.3. The student pays the completion fee to the Cashier. 7.1.4. The student presents the Official Receipt to the Registrar’s Office for stamping of “paid” and to log the date of application. 7.1.5. The faculty member indicates the completion grade on the form and submits it to the Program Chair. The Registrar will prepare two (2) reports at the end of the term for submission to CHED/TESDA and the Dean/TED Head’s Office: 1) a list of students with completed INC Grades and 2) a list of students with automatic failure due to non-completion of INC grades. 8. Minimum Standard of Good Academic Standing Minimum standard for good academic standing is passing all the subjects officially enrolled in. It also means completing an “INC” rating within the prescribed grace period. Students who fail to meet such standard are placed on Academic Probation. X. Bridging Program 1. Bridging Program An incoming freshman whose SHS tracks are different in his/her chosen college program are required to undergo bridging program. 2. Make-up Classes During the term, the faculty member or Program Chair may request authority from the Dean/TED Head to conduct make up classes for sections which do not meet the minimum requirement for student contact hours due to the following reasons: 2.1. Faculty absences 2.2. Student’s learning ability 2.3. Disruption of classes XI. Transferring to another School A student transferring to another school shall be required to process the clearance form and accomplish the Record Application Form for Transfer. XII. Student Clearance and Request for Documents Clearance should be accomplished by all students every end of the semester. A graduating student should be cleared from all financial obligations and administrative accountabilities from the different offices before a diploma, transcript of records, certification, and other similar documents are issued to him. For non-graduating students, the completed clearance form is needed in order for them to get their final grades and to enroll. 1. Related Documents Released to Students

1.1. Certificate of Transfer Credential A student who wishes to transfer to another school before the completion of his/her degree will be given a Certificate of Transfer Credential. 1.2. Certification of Good Moral Character A student may request for a Certification of Good Moral Character from the Guidance Counselor/Facilitator. In case of commission of a major offense, a student is issued a Certificate of Attendance instead of the Certification of Good Moral Character. 1.3. True Copy of Grades A student may request for a true copy of his grades any time upon payment of the required fees. This copy is attested to by the Registrar and marked as “For Evaluation Purposes Only”. The student may hand carry the True Copy of Grades. 1.4. Official Transcript of Records. 1.4.1. For graduates: an official TOR is issued only to a graduate of RC. 1.4.2. For undergraduates: the official TOR of the transferring student will be issued upon request of the Registrar of the new school. XIII. Graduation Requirements 1. Qualifications of an Applicant for Graduation Only a bona fide Rogationist College student with the following qualifications may be allowed to apply for graduation from a CHED or TESDA program.

1.1. Sufficient Residency The minimum residency equivalent to at least 50% of the total units required in the curriculum should have been taken at Rogationist College. 1.2. Academic Status - For CHED programs, the student must be at least in his last two (2) terms of attendance prior to graduation 1.3. Completion of entrance credentials 1.4. Completion of OJT 1.5. For CHED programs, passing the written or oral comprehensive examinations. For TESDA programs, passing the National Competency Assessment. 1.6. Successfully passed the defense for the undergraduate thesis (for students under CHED Programs) and submission of three (3) hard-bound copies of the thesis to the Dean’s on the scheduled date. A graduating student who failed on his 3^(rd) final defense is not eligible for graduation. 2. Steps in Processing Application for Graduation 2.1. The graduating student accomplishes the application for Graduation Form in the Registrar’s Office on the last month of the term prior to the last term of attendance. Students with INC rating should secure a copy of the application for completion from the Registrar’s Office. 2.2. The Registrar evaluates the applicant’s Entrance Credentials, Subject Grades and Residency Status and informs the Cluster Coordinators of the student’s deficiencies.

2.3. The Program Chair informs the student of the academic deficiencies and the required study load for the last term, copy furnished the Registrar. 2.4. The list of candidates for graduation is submitted by the Registrar to the School Graduation Committee (composed of the DAA, Dean/TED Head, Registrar and Program Chairs). 2.5. The School Graduation Committee assesses and releases the official list after receiving the final grades from the faculty on the last term. 2.6. The graduating student pays the graduation fees at the Cashier’s office not later than one (1) week after the release of the official graduation list. 2.7. The graduating student presents the official receipt to the Registrar’s Office to get a copy of Record Application together with the accomplished clearance. N.B. The Transcript of Records and Diploma will be issued by the Registrar as soon as the Special Order is received from CHED/TESDA. XIV. Graduation Honors 1. Academic Honors These are awarded to students who finish their courses with a GWA and other qualifications that are within the set criteria/guidelines in the selection of honor students. The following academic honors shall be awarded to deserving graduating students:

GWA CHED Programs TESDA Programs 1.00 – 1.25 Summa Cum Laude With Highest Honors 1.26 – 1.50 Magna Cum Laude With High Honors 1.51 – 1.75 Cum Laude With Honors 1.1. Criteria/Guidelines: 1.1.1. Grades in all subjects as prescribed in the curriculum are included in the computation of the General Weighted Average (GWA). The GWA is rounded off to two decimal places. The units as prescribed in the curricular program are used in the computation of the GWA, except for the following subjects which are assigned the following units for purposes of computation of the GWA: NSTP 1.5 units Religious Education 1.5 units 1.1.2. Completion of at least seventy five percent (75%) of the total number of academic units/hours at Rogationist College 1.1.3. Regular load per semester, unless the lighter load is due to justifiable causes such as health reasons, unavailability of subjects required in the curriculum to complete the full load, or the candidate is a student assistant 1.1.4. No final grade below 2.25 in any subject in any academic year 1.1.5. Course is finished within the prescribed academic period i.e. two years for 2-year TESDA programs, four or five years for 4-year CHED programs

1.1.6. Non-commission of a major offense 2. Special Award for Academic This award is given to a student who completes his/her course with a GWA of at least 1.75 but does not meet the requirements for load and residency. 3. Rogate Award This is the highest honor Rogationist College bestows on any of its graduating students. The award goes to whoever best exemplifies the spirit and ideals of Saint Hannibal Mary Di Francia. The awardee should meet the following criteria: 3.1. Belongs to the graduating class. 3.2. Must have stayed for four years in Rogationist College. 3.3. Prays for and promotes vocation. 3.4. Cares for the poor. 3.5. Must have a computed General Weighted Average of 1.75 and no grade below 2.25 in any of the enrolled subjects for his or her four-year stay in the college. 3.7. Must have conducted himself/herself in conformity with the school rules and regulations. XV. Recognition Honors and Special Awards 1. Dean’s List Outstanding academic performance is recognized through the publication of the Dean’s List during the succeeding term. Students who qualify for the Dean’s List receive a certificate of recognition at the end of the term.

1. Criteria/Guidelines: 1. Grades in all subjects as prescribed in the curriculum are included in the computation of the General Weighted Average (GWA). The GWA is rounded off to two decimal places. The units as prescribed in the curricular program are used in the computation of the GWA except for the following subjects, which are assigned the following units for purposes of computation of the GWA: NSTP 1.5 units Religious Education 1.5 units 1.1.2. With a GWA of at least 1.50 1.1.3. No final grade lower than 2.25 or INC/DRP in any subject for two consecutive semesters 1.1.4. A regular load of at least 18 units per semester 1.1.5. Non-commission of any major offense in school 2. Diligence Award This award shall be given to a student who manifests a remarkable, positive attitude towards education and the learning process. He must possess the desire and willingness to learn and to be educated and must have the personal initiative in improving his understanding and comprehension of the lessons. He should have conducted himself in conformity with the school rules, polices and regulations.

3. Leadership Award This annual award is given to any graduating student who exemplifies outstanding leadership qualities during his four years of stay in Rogationist College. The instructors nominate candidates for the award, deliberate and choose the most deserving from among the candidates. 4. Conduct Award This award is given to any student who manifests exemplary human behavior and meets the highest standard of good character and discipline set by the Rogationist College. 5. Achievement Award This is awarded to a student who best manifests the skills acquired in his curricular program or trade area in any of the different CHED or TESDA programs.

The Student Activity Program is based on the school’s objectives of developing the students’ cultural competence and social responsibilities. Student activities provide experiences and opportunities for skills and values development of students in support of the academic program. They help in maximizing the students’ potentialities by promoting self-actualization and fostering holistic growth and development. Rogationist College encourages students to join these school activities. I. Guidelines on Student Activity Program 1. All instructors, program chairs and club/organization moderators and advisers are required to submit a work plan of their activities before the start of each school year. Major activities, especially those which will entail monetary collections, require written approval from the Dean/TED Head, the Director of Finance and Administration and the Rector. 2. Students can belong to a maximum of three clubs or organizations provided they pass the criteria for membership. 3. Organization of any activity prejudicial to the welfare of the students and the interest of the school is not allowed. Any group that wishes to start a new club/organization should submit a letter addressed to the Rector through the Dean/TED Head and recommended by the DSS. The letter must contain the goals and the structure of the proposed new club/organization.

4. Holding of classroom, academic and club activities must be properly coordinated with the SAC, Dean/TED Head, Prefect of Discipline and the DSS/DAA/OGS. Reservations of venues, equipment and other materials needed for the activities should be facilitated by the adviser or moderator at least three (3) days before their schedule. 5. Student activities are usually done outside class hours. Extra-ordinary sessions which require calling students from their classes must have the permission of the Program Chair /Dean/TED Head. 5. At the end of each semester, all clubs/organizations are required to submit a semestral report which includes the minutes of the meetings, attendance, updated list of members and officers, financial statement, documentation, evaluation tools, results of evaluations conducted and work plans. 6. Acquired club/organization funds must be turned over to the Finance and Administration Office at the end of the school year. They will be transferred to the next moderator/adviser with the approval of the DFA. 7. Students are encouraged to participate in worthwhile activities outside of the school. Invitation to these activities is endorsed by the club moderators to the SAC who shall seek the approval of the Dean/TED Head, DSS,DFA and Rector.

9. Off-campus, overnight, after class hour and weekend activities require parents’ permission. The students have to accomplish the activity permit a week before such activities. II. Community Extension Program The Community Extension Program of Rogationist College is designed to instill in every member of the education community the values and goals of the school according to the ideals of St. Hannibal Mary Di Francia in helping the poor especially the children. This program extends the teaching learning activity of RC beyond its campus. The DAA and DSS shall evaluate and recommend the proposed activities pertaining to the community extension program for the approval of the Rector. III. Varsity Players Varsity players are students who are members of the official team representing Rogationist College in different sports activities. (cf. Guidelines on the Selection of Varsity players in Appendix) IV. Organizations and Clubs 1. Supreme Student Council (SSC) - The highest students’ organization whose officers are elected by the entire student body. It coordinates with the administration regarding departmental activities of the students. 2. RCians - The official school organ of the College Department published every semester. The editorial board is selected by a screening committee composed of the Adviser, English Professors, Dean/TED Head and Rector.

MERCX – Marketing Enthusiasts for Rogationist College eXcellence 4. Cultural and Sports Clubs 4.1. Artists Club 4.2. Teatro Rogasyonista 4.3. Hard Court Movers 4.4. Glee Club 4.5. Varsity 5.
