Students of RC are expected to behave as worthy members of the Christian society and of the Rogationist family. An RC student exemplifies the ideals and virtues of Saint Hannibal Mary Di Francia, whether inside or outside the school campus. Thus, the administration considers each student as a guardian of school rules and regulations and holds each one responsible for their observance. I. Objectives of the Student Discipline Program 1. To develop in the students the freedom, social conscience and the commitment to be well-mannered persons. 2. To consolidate the Filipino values of respect and cooperation for the purpose of fostering family-oriented behavior and self-discipline. 3. To foster in the students a deep respect for persons, in obedience to authority, and appreciation of rules. 4. To provide for the development of young people who are confident, disciplined, and self-reliant. 5. To develop in the students the value of productive work, cooperation, and responsible leadership. II. Behavioral Expectation from Students “He who fears the Lord will accept his discipline and those who rise early to seek Him will find favor” (Sirach 2:14).

The exercise of good behavior shows that the students have internalized the philosophy of the school, that they understand the Christian objectives of the Rogationist College, and that they care for their participation in making the school respectable. These indicate that the students have achieved growth as Christians and worthy members of society. III. Proper Student Decorum Rogationist College, as a Catholic education community, sees the importance of character formation. Thus, every student is expected to be refined in thoughts, words and actions. 1. Every student aspiring for integrity and excellence should abide by the rules and regulations governing academic responsibilities. 2. A student should help maintain the cleanliness and order in their classrooms. 3. A student should refrain from boisterous conduct which may distract others. 4. A student should exhibit proper behavior when in malls, parks, resorts and other public places. 5. The school suggests that participation of students in activities such as modeling, product endorsing, beauty pageant, singing and stage performances be in accordance with its vision-mission. Therefore, any participation in such activities requires consultation with the Dean and DSSS.

IV. School Uniform The manner of dressing and grooming is also an expression and a measure of one’s personality. Therefore, the school imposes a dress code to train the students in proper dressing and proper grooming as a preparation for their future professional life. Simplicity, modesty and neatness are emphasized. A student must come to school in complete and proper uniform during school days. Proper uniform means that the uniform is properly ironed; the polo or blouse is buttoned properly; the ID card is worn properly; and the shoes are clean. All students must maintain a neat and decent hair cut/hairstyle. For male students, accessories like earrings, headbands, or hairclips are not allowed. Wearing of caps or any kind of hat is not allowed inside the campus unless necessary. The description of the College uniform is as follows: Uniform for Males: (cf. Appendix) a. Powder blue plain polo barong (with RC logo) and plain white T-shirt / “sando” b. Navy blue pants as prescribed by the school c. Black leather shoes with socks Uniform for Females: (cf. Appendix) a. Plain white short-sleeved blouse (with Navy Blue RC logo), dark blue belt and pants as prescribed by the school

b. Black ladies closed shoes. c. White ladies camisole/“sando” PE Uniform: a. Dark blue jogging pants (with the school name and logo) b. White T-shirt with blue round neckline and school logo c. Rubber shoes of any kind d. Sport socks of any kind TED Uniform (during Laboratory): a. Black shirt (with RC & TED logo) b. Dark-colored pants / jeans c. Rubber shoes Caregiving Program: a. Light Blue Scrub Suit c. White rubber shoes Corporate Attire The attire’s design/style is prescribed by respective program/cluster and worn on a particular day per week. FRIDAY UNIFORM (Blue Day) Students are required to wear the following during RC’s Blue Day: a. RC blue shirt b. Jeans/denim pants c. Closed shoes V. Dress Code A student may come to school in appropriate civilian attire/organization’s shirt only during Saturdays, Sundays or school holidays as long as he/she is wearing his/her ID. The attire should not be revealing. Leggings, “tokong”, cargo pants, low-waist/hip-hop pants, flip flops, and the likes are not allowed. Only closed-shoes are acceptable. VI. Personal Appearance and Grooming 1. Students shall always be in clean and presentable manner.

a. Personal hygiene and grooming –Students are advised not to wear excessive jewelry, have body tattoo or body piercing. Male students are not allowed to wear headbands or earrings of any kind. b. Haircut and hairstyle-Students’ hair must be neatly combed and presentable. Hair color is not allowed. VII. Attendance Monitoring Students with five (5) consecutive absences in class shall be referred by the instructor to the Office for Guidance and Counseling for processing. Cases of excessive absences in a class or in the departmental/institutional activities (i.e. 20% of the allowable absences) shall be reported by the instructor to the Program Chair who in turn will update the Dean/TED Head. Attendance in every activity will be checked and has a corresponding mark/grade for the subject/s of the students. If the student/s incurred more than 20% of the allowable absences, he/she will get a DROPPED REMARKS OR FAILED GRADES. Non-attendance will have a corresponding paper work.

All offenses are subject to imposition of penalties ranging from warning to separation from the school, depending on the gravity and attendant circumstances, whether mitigating or aggravating, as each case may warrant. Every bona fide student of the Rogationist College is obliged to observe all disciplinary policies of the school. Any violation of such policies shall compel the school to take the necessary disciplinary measures. All offenses shall be attended to by Office for Student Discipline. Offenses shall be counted on a semestral basis. Prompt reporting of incident of misbehavior of an RC student is encouraged. This covers the period when said student is officially enrolled in the college/Technical Education department. This is done in order to maximize the intervention, reformation and/or imposition of appropriate disciplinary action/s of the school. I. Disciplinary Actions 1. For Minor Offenses

1. The name of the student against whom the complaint is filed; and 2. A narration of the pertinent facts and circumstances of the act/s complained of. 2. The Office for Student Discipline through the Discipline Officer conducts its own preliminary inquiry through other concerned persons. 3. A written report shall be forwarded by the Discipline Officer to the Prefect of Discipline, attaching pertinent documents related to the case. Cases falling under Category A of Major Offenses will be decided by the Prefect of Discipline. 4. Cases falling under Categories B & C are to be deliberated by the Discipline Committee headed by the DSS and composed of the Discipline Officer, Guidance Counselor, and Program Chair. The DSS shall initiate the hearing/deliberation the cases for Non-admission / Dismissal. The following items are to be observed in student disciplinary hearings (Sarmiento, “Students’ Rights and Wrongs”, 2006. pp.65-66) 1. The student shall be informed in writing of the nature and cause of the accusation against him; 2. He shall have the right to answer the charges against him within 3 school days. The basic principles of due process shall be in place.

3. He shall be informed of the evidence against him; 4. He shall have the right to adduce evidence in his own behalf, and 5. The evidence must be considered by the investigating committee or official designated by the school authorities to hear and decide the case. 5. The result of the deliberation shall be submitted by the Prefect of Discipline to the DSS, who will in turn forward this to the Rector for his final decision. 6. The DSS shall conduct conference with the erring student and his parents/guardian concerning the final decision. II. Probation and Dismissal In accordance with the provision in the Manual of Regulations for Private Schools, 9^(th) edition, the categories of disciplinary administrative sanctions for serious offenses or violation of school rules and regulations, which may be applied upon an erring student, are: 1. Disciplinary Probation This means that the student has forfeited the confidence and high esteem of the school authorities and he is required to restore these by definite and manifest acts of attention to duty. Habitual misbehavior and unsatisfactory conduct may lead the Discipline Committee to recommend a student to be placed under disciplinary probation for a specific period of time (i.e. for one semester). If the student is placed on probation for 1 semester, his compliance with the school rules will be evaluated at the end of the semester. His failure to show remarkable improvement forfeits his chance to re-enroll the following semester.

2. Dismissal The school reserves the right to dismiss, or drop from the school, at any time during the year/semester, any student who fails to give positive evidence of earnestness of purpose and active cooperation in all the requirements of conduct and academic work, or whose conduct makes the student a liability and nuisance to the school authority, and a bad influence to his fellow students. His credentials are readily given to facilitate transfer to another school. Some specific cases for dismissal from school: a. organizing, recruiting for, or membership in, a fraternity or sorority which does not promote the vision-mission of the college b. hazing c. carrying a deadly weapon d. sex-related offenses such as sexual violence e. selling and/or possession of prohibited drugs f. drug dependency g. drunkenness h. hooliganism i. vandalism j. assaulting a student or school personnel k. instigating or leading illegal strikes or similar concerted activities resulting in the stoppage of classes l. preventing or threatening any student or school personnel from entering the school premises or attending classes or discharging their duties m. forging or tampering with school forms or records,

n. securing or using forged school records, forms and documents o. other gross misbehavior judged as such by the Discipline Committee. III. Offenses 1. Minor Offenses 1.1. Violation of the rules on prescribed uniform and attire 1.2. Non-wearing of school ID or refusal to display school Id prominently and placing stickers and other objects on school ID 1.3. Using another student’s ID/lending personal ID to another student 1.4. Improper haircut, hair color or hairstyle 1.5. Elaborate body accessories and/or improper personal appearance or hygiene, dangling belts, chains, body piercing, excessive jewelry, too much use of gel/wax, colored nail polish 1.6. Littering 1.7. Loitering 1.8. Playing ballgames in the gymnasium not in sports attire or P.E. uniform and/or playing outside the scheduled P.E class without the coordinated permission from the Office for Student Affairs and the OSD 1. 9. Deliberate disruption of class (creating too much unnecessary noise) 1.10 Uncooperative behavior during emergency drills 2. Major Offenses Major offenses are acts that cause damage to a student’s honor and dignity as a person as well as to the property, name and honor of the College. Imposition of disciplinary action cited in this handbook shall not in any way prejudice the filing of cases and in the implementation of penalties prescribed by a court of law. No exception is made whether the offense is made the first, second, or the third time.

Category A: 1. Irreverence like disruptive noise, talking, laughing, eating and chewing gum while observing Midday Prayer, Angelus and Holy Mass 2. Reading or carrying any pornographic material or visiting/uploading/sharing pornographic websites 7. Bullying (physical, verbal or cyber) 8. 3. Exchanging examination papers/calculators with another student to enable the latter to copy it 4. Glancing at seatmate’s examination paper in disregard of an earlier warning or admonition 5. Commission of action/s resulting to a crime or violation of the law 21. Conviction by court in a criminal case
