A student who transfers or otherwise withdraws, in writing, within two weeks after the beginning of classes and who has already paid the pertinent tuition and other fees in full or for any length of time longer than one month may be charged ten (10%) percent of the total amount due for the term if he withdraws within the first week of classes, or twenty percent if within the second week of classes, regardless of whether or not he has actually attended classes. The student may be charged all the school fees in full if he withdraws any time after the second week of classes. However, if the transfer or withdrawal is due to a justifiable reason, the student shall be charged the pertinent fees only up to and including the last month of attendance. The foregoing tuition fee schedules are based on the premise that a student who enrolls in a school stays enrolled for the entire school year or semester, regardless of his subsequent transfer or withdrawal. Section 66, MRPS and Section 104, TVET Manual protect schools which accept tuition fee payments on installment – i.e., where a down payment is given upon enrollment and the balance is paid before examinations–– by requiring students who transfer or withdraw from the course to first settle their accounts before the school issues them transfer credentials.

It must be stressed that according to the stipulations of Section 62(e) of the MRPS and section 124(e), TVET Manual, a school can legally collect outstanding tuition fees from a student who has transferred or withdrawn only if he was officially enrolled. This means that the student must have at least made an initial payment of his school fees and that the school must have accepted that payment and authorized him to participate in his classes. Without these attending circumstances, there is no legal basis for the collection of tuition fee charges, since no contractual relationship between student and school was established. A student who has paid in full or for any length longer than one month and transfers or withdraws in the first week after classes begin shall be charged 10% of the total amount due for the term (i.e. one semester for the collegiate level and TVET courses, one year for elementary and secondary levels); if he withdraws in the second week he will be charged 20%; if he withdraws any time after the second week, he may be fully charged for all fees applicable for the entire term. These charges hold whether or not he actually participated in his classes, because attendance is not the issue; what matters is that the school actually authorized him to attend them.

For purposes of determination, the day of the student’s submission of his written notice of withdrawal shall be considered the date of withdrawal. Verbal notice is not enough. If the tuition fees, registration, library and laboratory fees already paid equal the amount still to be paid for the first month (or less) in a monthly installment scheme, no refund shall be given to the student when he withdraws after the registration period. However, if the transfer or withdrawal is due to justifiable cause, the student shall only be charged the pertinent fees up to the last month of attendance. An existing DepEd ruling states that any promissory note signed in favor of a school by a student below 18 years old is null and void. It does not constitute the “payment of some kind” needed to establish enrollment unless a responsible relative or legal guardian acts as surety. The reason for this is that in law, a person below 18 years old is still a minor and is not legally competent to contract such a financial obligation. Yet even if the student were of majority age but still dependent on the parents or a guardian for support, the DepEd would not consider him competent to sign a promissory note. Therefore, such a note would likewise be considered null and void unless a responsible relative or guardian appears as surety.

Although the MRPS and the TVET Manual no longer provide for this, it is submitted that students are entitled to a full refund of fees for any course or subject that has been discontinued by the school, or which was not credited by the DepEd, CHED or TESDA.

Rationale: The Student Assistantship Program has been developed in order to: 1. add manpower to assist instructors in laboratory exercises/activities or those in the offices in addressing clerical and legworks 2. provide opportunities to less privileged youths who could not afford to continue with their schooling due to lack of financial resources Privilege: 100% tuition fee grant to be applied at the end of the semester or the summer term Terms and Conditions: A qualified Student Assistant should: 1. Enroll a maximum of 24 units (or 21 lecture and laboratory units for CHED/TESDA courses) per semester and 9 lecture units (or 6 lecture and laboratory units) during summer. 2. Render 12 work hours per week during the examination periods and 15 work hours per week during regular classes for 18 weeks per semester and 13 work hours per week for 6 weeks during summer classes. 3. Submit schedule of classes per semester/summer after enrolment to supervisor for the proper scheduling of work hours per week. 4. Comply with the work schedule agreed upon by him/her and his/her supervisor. 5. Pay the miscellaneous and laboratory fees in four equal installments upon enrollment and before each major examination.

6. Maintain good academic standing of at least an average of 2.50 without incurring any failing or incomplete grade in any subject. 7. Maintain good conduct records by not committing any major offense or displaying untoward behavior to anyone in school. Mechanics: Application, Selection and Deployment of Student Assistants 1. Offices or school personnel requesting for services of a Student Assistant shall prepare a request letter recommended by the Immediate Head and approved by the Rector every semester. This letter shall be forwarded to the HRD and Scholarship Coordinator. 2. Students who wish to avail of/apply for the SA Program should approach the Scholarship Coordinator to fill out the application form and for pre-evaluation. 3. SAs can be selected from any of the following: 1. High school graduates who have not enrolled yet as of the second week of classes due to lack of financial resources 2. College students who have stopped schooling due to lack of financial resources 3. Students whose family monthly gross income is not more than 15,000.00 4. If the SA applicant is a new student, he/she should have a GWA of at least 85% or its equivalent and should take and pass the College entrance examinations.

5. The SA applicant shall be interviewed by the Guidance Counselor, Scholarship Coordinator, and DSPS. The DSPS shall recommend the applicant to the Rector for approval. 6. Once qualified, the SA shall enroll the allowable units per semester or summer and shall be given orientation by the HRD and the supervisor to whom he/she shall be assigned. 7. Towards the end of every semester, the supervisor shall conduct a performance evaluation and submit the result to the HRD. Both this and the SA’s grades shall be bases for the continued availing of the program. SA Supervisor Responsibilities: 1. Approved letter of request for a student assistant submitted to the HRD and Scholarship Coordinator 2. Orientation with the qualified SA 3. Work load and schedule for the SA; close supervision on assigned tasks. 4. Monthly attendance sheet and SA accomplishment report for output monitoring submitted to the HRD 5. Coordination with the Registrar’s Office regarding release of examination permit and signing of SA clearance 6. Conduct of performance evaluation on SA to be submitted to the HRD

Rationale: The community service refers to an activity being done in Rogationist College to help its students realize the importance of self-discipline and to motivate students to see the significance of compliance and responsibility over their actions, taking into consideration the policies of the school and the formation of the entire educational community. Rogationist College upholds this principle of service to promote among its members the core values stated in its vision-mission. According to the Rogationist system of education, students should be responsible in following all school discipline rules and regulations. Community service is therefore required to students who habitually violate school rules and regulations, particularly the disciplinary rules of the college department. Procedure in Rendering Community Service: 1. The student reports to the Discipline Officer for the schedule of his/her community service. The student may perform any of the tasks such as cleaning in the canteen, classroom, campus ground, or laboratory. 1. clerical work in offices such as filing, recording, etc, 2. cleaning in the canteen, classroom, campus ground, or library 2. After completing the task, the student submits the Community Service Form to the Discipline Officer signed by the Supervising Personnel and the Program Chair.
Rogationist College – Supreme Student Council

Preamble We, the bona fide students of Rogationist College, imploring the aid and guidance of the Almighty, in order to establish and promote an autonomous, democratic and representative student leadership, to protect our rights and welfare and foster relationship among the students and the other sectors of the institution and in order to instill national consciousness for the advancement of our educational, social and cultural well-being through collective efforts in the spirit of service through justice and peace, do hereby ordain and promulgate this constitution.
Section I. The organization shall be called the Rogationist College – Supreme Student Council, hereinafter referred to as the RC-SSC.

section_title: Section II. The RC-SSC official seal is as follows:
content: RC – SSC Official Seal The RC – SSC Official Seal represents man’s total human and Christian formation. The cross symbolizes Christ, the living foundation of the whole Rogationist educational community. The four vertical columns sustaining the cross signify the four core values (Love of God and Neighbor, Patriotism, Integrity and Excellence) anchored on the Rogationist educational philosophy. The gavel and the book signify that the council shall be ruled by the tenets of the institution under the guidance of the Divine Providence, represented by the feathers. The human symbols at the bottom stand for the student leaders committed to support and serve the student body.

Section I. The RC-SSC shall be the highest legitimate student organization of the college. All the organizations listed below shall be under the Supreme Student Council. a. Junior Philippine Institute of Accountants (JPIA) b. Marketing Enthusiasts for Rogationist College eXcellence (MERCX) c. Rogationist College League of Industrial Technology and Engineering Students (RCLites) d. Young Educators Club (YEC) e. Rogationist Computer Society (ROCS) f. Tourism, Hotel and Restaurant Management Society (THRM Society) g. Hard Court Movers h. Dance Pro i. Theater Club j. Glee Club k. Artists Club Section II. The RC-SSC shall be the sole representative of the students to the school administration and in activities that will be held outside the school as part of promoting the institution within and outside the community.

section_title: Section III. The RC-SSC aims to:
content: a. Foster unity and harmony among the students and personnel for better coordination and understanding and for the common good of the students and of the school; b. Promote equal rights of all the students, regardless of their course, common group or organization; c. Establish alliance and solidarity with other organizations whose purposes are not contrary to law; d. Protect and uplift the welfare of the whole student body through dialogues and by raising the students’ concerns to the school administration, thus bridging the gap between the student body and the school administration; e. Serve as a forum for the expression of students’ ideas and sentiments of general significance; f. Train and develop student leaders; and g. Develop a strong sense of responsibility and consciousness with the positive view of contributing to the establishment of a just and humane society.

section_title: Section IV. The RC-SSC is an advocate of the following premises:
content: a. Education is a right, thus, it must be affordable to everyone; b. Education should develop critical thinking and creative growth; c. Education should instill national consciousness, social awareness and sense of responsibility; and d. Education should be mass-oriented and systematic. Section V. The RC-SSC believes in the principles of collective leadership that paves the way for effective governance. Section VI. The RC-SSC shall serve as the mediator between the students and any sector of the community and shall function as the voice of the entire student body.

section_title: Section VII. The decision of the majority shall always be respected.
content: Section IX. The RC-SSC shall always abide by the Constitution of the Philippines and the school’s policies and rules. Section X. Membership in the RC-SSC must be for the general welfare and collective interests of the student body.

section_title: Section I. It is the duty and obligation of every student to:
content: 1. Observe the law of the land and the school’s rules and regulations at all times; 2. Help bring forth an academic atmosphere that will create unity and harmony among the various sectors of the institution; 3. Support the institution in maintaining its high standards and in promoting the values of love of God and neighbor, excellence, patriotism and integrity; 4. Exercise his/her rights and privileges as well as responsibilities to family, community, school and country; 5. Directly and actively participate and support the activities, programs and projects of the RC-SSC; 6. Promote and enhance the good name of the institution; 7. Uphold the principles and objectives of the RC-SSC.

section_title: Section I. The RC-SSC Executive Committee shall be composed of the following officers:
content: a. President b. Vice President b.1. External Affairs b.2. Internal Affairs c. Secretary d. Finance Officers d.1. Treasurer d.2. Auditor e. Public Relations Officer g. Business Manager h. Representatives of each cluster Section II. Bona fide students of the Rogationist College shall elect the RC-SSC Executive Committee members (council officers). Section III. The term of office of all officers shall be one school year and shall commence after the induction.

section_title: Section IV. Candidates for the RC-SSC offices:
content: 1. Should be bona fide students of Rogationist College; 2. Must not have been found guilty of any major offense; 3. Must meet the other qualifications required for each position.

section_title: Section V. Vacancies within the RC-SSC may occur in the following situations:
content: 1. Impeachment 1. Grounds for Impeachment 1. Gross misconduct 2. Negligence and disloyalty to the cause of the RC-SSC and the school 3. Abuse of authority 4. Culpable violations of the constitution 2. Illness 3. Incapacity to fulfill duties in the office 4. Resignation Section VI. In case of vacancy in any position in the council, the remaining officers shall declare through a resolution that a vacancy exists. A notice thereof shall be given to the Office for Student Affairs. Section VII. If the office of the President is vacated, the Vice President for Internal Affairs shall take over. In case of permanent vacancy in the office; the council officers shall elect a new Vice President among its remaining officers and representatives. Section VIII. If both the offices of the President and the Vice President for Internal Affairs are vacated, the remaining officers within the council shall elect an acting President and Vice President from among them.

1. Enforce the Constitution as well as the other rules and regulations of the council; 2. Act as presiding officer in all meetings of the council; 3. Represent the council on occasions or events where representation is sought; 4. Sign all resolutions, communications and papers of the council; 5. Countersign, after approval of the adviser, all disbursements to be made by the treasurer; 6. Review and approve cash vouchers; and 7. Create committees and appoint the chairman and members of the said committees necessary to the noble objectives of the RC-SSC.

section_title: Section II. The Vice-President for Internal Affairs shall:
content: 2.1. Assist the President in the discharge of his/her duties; 2.2. Assume the function of the President in case of his incapacity or absence; 2.3. Link the academic and non-academic organizations inside the school; 2.4. Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the President; and 2.5. Succeed the President only for the unexpired term.

section_title: Section III. The Vice President for External Affairs shall:
content: 3.1. Link the school to other schools; 3.2. Represent the Student Council in occasions when representation is being sought in the absence of the President; and 3.3. Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the President.

4.1 Prepare the minutes of the meetings and do the safekeeping of records and documents of the council; 2. Prepare communication and file documents belonging to the council; 3. Send all necessary notices to the officers and the adviser; 4. Give advanced information of the scheduled meeting/s or engagement to the members of the council; 5. Disseminate information to other officers concerning meetings, updates and other important matters; and 6. Perform all other functions as may be assigned by the President.

1. Be the finance officer of the organization; 2. Act as the custodian of all the properties, funds and accounts of the council; 3. Keep and maintain true and detailed statements of receipt and disbursement/ expenses of the council; 4. Receive and deposit the funds of the organization; 5. Prepare and sign all documents regarding the funds of the organization as countersigned by the President and the adviser; 6. Perform all other duties with respect to finances; 7. Supervise all payment, requisition and liquidation of transactions; and 8. Prepare a financial report to the council after every activity.

6.1. Audit the financial statements provided by the treasurer; 6.2. Assist the treasurer in facilitating transactions of the council; 6.3. Monitor fund allocation in every activity; and 6.4. Perform all other functions as may be assigned by the President.

section_title: Section VII. The Public Relations Officer shall:
content: 7.1. Be the spokesperson of the organization; 7.2. Be in-charge in giving proper and due publicity to all activities of the council; and 7.3. Perform all other functions as may be assigned by the President.

section_title: Section VIII. The Business Manager shall:
content: 8.1. Manage the businesses and projects of the organization; 8.2. Take the lead in the fund-raising activities organized by the council; and 8.3 Perform all other functions as may be assigned by the President.

section_title: Section IX. The Cluster Representatives shall:
content: 9.1. Report to the council regarding their cluster activities; 9.2. Disseminate necessary information to their clusters; 8.3 Perform all other functions as may be assigned by the President.

section_title: Section III. The Council adviser shall perform the following functions:
content: 1. Serve as the liaison between the RC-SSC officers and the Administration; 2. Give advice to the council officers on matters related to the projects/programs and activities of the RC-SSC Section IV. The Council adviser shall have no voiding power in the meetings and deliberations of the council.
1. The presence of majority (50% plus one) of the members of the council shall constitute a quorum. 2. No business shall be done in the absence of a quorum.
2.1. The Executive Committee shall meet once a month. 2.2. In case the Executive Committee could not meet on the fixed date, the President may determine the schedule of meetings.
1. Whenever necessary, the executive committee may call for a special meeting of their own to attend to matters that need immediate action.

Section I. The funds of the RC-SSC can be generated from the membership fees of the students, fund raising activities, sponsorships, donations, grants and other contributions. Section II. The payment of the membership fee shall be P150.00 every semester and shall be included in the miscellaneous fees of the students. Section III. Any contributions, donations and grants shall be received and kept by the Accounting Officer of the institution. Section IV. All expenses of the RC-SSC shall be paid from the fund. The incumbent officers and members and the successors must use this fund for the benefit of the students in general.

Section I. The Rogationist College-Supreme Student Council Constitution may be amended only by an affirmative vote of two-thirds of all council members, provided that the proposed amendment is presented in writing at the previous meeting of the council and the copies thereof are sent to all council members at least two weeks prior to its consideration. Section II. Any amendment to or revision of this constitution shall be valid when approved by the Rogationist College Administrators and ratified in the same manner as the adoption of this constitution. Section III. The constitution shall take effect upon the approval of the Rogationist College Administrators and one week after its ratification by a majority vote of the students in an RC-wide plebiscite called for this purpose.

Selection of College Varsity Players Students interested to in trying out for the varsity team must secure an application form from the OSA and should meet the following requirements: 1.1. a bonafide college student (1^(st) – 2^(nd) year for the College Department; 1^(st) year for TED) 1.2. 19-20 years old 1.3. must have passed the College Admission Test 1.4. with good academic and conduct standing (not under academic probation and without disciplinary record) 1.5. must have passed the physical and medical examination conducted by the school physician 1. Drafting of Players 1. First Draft Thirty (30) players will be selected on the first day of try-out for the Team Sports. The number of players for individual games will depend on the decision of the coach/moderator. 2. Second Draft All selected players will undergo at most 5 days of training sessions. 3. Final Draft The official list of players will be deliberated upon by the coach, varsity club moderator, and SAC. The result of this deliberation will be submitted to the DSPS and the Rector for approval. 2. Number of Official Varsity Players per Event:

a. Basketball – 15 players b. Volleyball – 15 players c. Badminton – 5 players d. Chess – 5 players e. Table Tennis – 5 players II. Terms and Conditions The varsity player must meet the following requirements: 1. Enroll a minimum of 18 units per semester 2. Maintain good academic standing with an average of at least 2.50 without incurring any failing grade in any subject 3. Maintain good conduct records by not committing any major offense or a series of minor offenses. 4. Regularly attend classes and school/departmental activities. Absence in classes without valid reason can be a ground for removal from the team. 5. Follow the code of conduct and discipline and promote camaraderie and sportsmanship at all times. Any player who commits a major offense will be automatically disqualified from the varsity team. A player with series of minor offenses is to be referred to the OSD for appropriate action. III. Training 1. The schedule of practices shall be determined by the head coach. He will make a proposal through the OSA for approval by the Rector.

2. Practices should be held late in the afternoon three times a week. Saturday practices may be scheduled with prior approval from the DSPS. For practices on declared holidays, approval must be sought from the Rector. 3. Academic-related activities should be prioritized if they are in conflict with the scheduled practices. IV. Competitions The varsity teams shall participate in the following: 1. Inter-school competitions 2. Southern Cavite Athletic Association 3. Other events, subject to the approval of the Rector V. Benefits 1. Grades -1.0 in PE subject during the semester(s) that they have competitions 2. Allowance – meal allowance during competitions 3. Sports Accessories – complete uniform 4. Special Awards – for selected players only

section_title: KNOW ALL MEN BY THESE PRESENTS:
content: Whereas, Rogationist College is aware of the mandate of the 1987 Philippine Constitution as to the role of educational institution to inculcate patriotism and nationalism, foster love of humanity, respect for human rights, appreciation of the roles of national heroes in the historical development of the country, teach the rights and duties of citizenship, strengthen ethical and spiritual values, develop moral character and personal discipline, encourage critical and creative thinking, broaden scientific and technical knowledge, and promote vocational efficiency (Article XIV, Section 3 (2));a Whereas, the State to protect the rights of individuals, more particularly against sexual harassment especially on educational institutions, promulgated Republic Act 7877 otherwise known as “the sexual harassment act of 1995” wherein it was stated that it is the duty of the employer to provide proper decorum in the workplace and educational institution, and to provide the procedure for the settlement, resolution or prosecution of any act involving sexual harassment; Whereas, the Department of Education issued Department Order No. 40, Series of 2012, on May 14, 2012 otherwise known as “DepEd Child Protection Policy” with respect to Policy and Guidelines on Protecting Children in School from Abuse, Violence, Exploitation, Discrimination, Bullying and other Forms of Abuse;

section_title: KNOW ALL MEN BY THESE PRESENTS:
content: Whereas, Rogationist College in order to comply with the different laws, rules and regulation in relation to Sexual Harassment formulated its own rules of procedure in addressing the complaint on sexual harassment; Thus the foregoing rule is hereby adopted. Section 1. This shall be known as “RULES AND REGULATIONS IN RELATION TO CASES INVOLVING SEXUAL HARASSMENT”

It is the mandate of the 1987 the Philippine Constitution for educational institutions to inculcate patriotism and nationalism, foster love of humanity, respect for human rights, appreciation of the roles of national heroes in the historical development of the country, teach the rights and duties of citizenship, strengthen ethical and spiritual values, develop moral character and personal discipline, encourage critical and creative thinking, broaden scientific and technical knowledge, and promote vocational efficiency (Article XIV, Section 3 (2)); It is the duty of the State to protect the rights of individuals, more particularly against sexual harassment especially on educational institutions, promulgated Republic Act 7877 otherwise known as “the sexual harassment act of 1995” wherein it was stated that it is the duty of the employer to provide proper decorum in the workplace and educational institution, and to provide the procedure for the settlement, resolution or prosecution of any act involving sexual harassment; In order to protect the rights of individuals in education institution, the Department of Education issued Department Order No. 40, Series of 2012, on May 14, 2012 otherwise known as “DepEd Child Protection Policy” with respect to Policy and Guidelines on Protecting Children in School from Abuse, Violence, Exploitation, Discrimination, Bullying and other Forms of Abuse, which Rogationist College hereby adopts in toto.

It is the objective of Rogationist College to provide not only good and quality education but also to inculcate the values and teachings of its founder, Fr. Hannibal de Francia, in relation to morals, proper decorum and good behaviour. It is the policy of Rogationist College to free its environment from all acts of sexual harassment and condemns any act pertinent or related thereto for it is highly unacceptable behaviour, contrary to law and morals. However, considering the effect on the welfare of the child or employment of individuals complaint off, Rogationist College will undertake to consider all aspects of the complaint and all proceedings shall be treated with strict confidentially. Rogationist College shall consider due process in handling cases involving sexual harassment to protect not only the rights of the complainant but also of the person being charged, without prejudice to complying with the reportorial requirement mandated by Department Order No. 40, Series of 2012, issued by the Department of Education and separate criminal cases that may be instituted.

a. Child – refers to any person below eighteen (18) years of age or those over but are unable to fully take care of themselves from abuse, neglect, cruelty, exploitation or discrimination because of physical or mental disability or condition, including all students who are above 18 years of age but are enrolled in Rogationist College b. School personnel – means any person who works for Rogationist College, whether as: b.1 school head which refers to the chief executive officer or administrator of a public or private school or learning center b.2 other school officials or those occupying supervisory positions or positions of responsibility, and are involve in policy formulation or implementation in school academic personnel b.3 Academic personnel includes all school personnel who are formally engaged in actual teaching service or in research assignments, either in full time or part-time service, as well as those who possesses certain prescribed academic functions directly supportive of teaching, such as registrars, librarians, guidance counsellors, researchers and other similar persons. b.4 Other personnel include all other non-academic personnel in the school, whatever may be the nature of their appointment and status of employment. (as per Department Order No. 40, Series of 2012 of Department of Education)

c. Sexual Harassment ( as per R.A. 7877) - sexual harassment is committed by an employer, employee, manager, supervisor, agent of the employer, teacher, instructor, professor, coach, trainor, or any other person who, having authority, influence or moral ascendancy over another in a work or training or education environment, demands, requests or otherwise requires any sexual favor from the other, regardless of whether the demand, request or requirement for submission is accepted by the object of said Act. c.1 In a work-related or employment environment, sexual harassment is committed when: (1) The sexual favor is made as a condition in the hiring or in the employment, re-employment or continued employment of said individual, or in granting said individual favorable compensation, terms of conditions, promotions, or privileges; or the refusal to grant the sexual favor results in limiting, segregating or classifying the employee which in any way would discriminate, deprive or diminish employment opportunities or otherwise adversely affect said employee; (2) The above acts would impair the employee's rights or privileges under existing labor laws; or (3) The above acts would result in an intimidating, hostile, or offensive environment for the employee.

c.2 In an education or training environment, sexual harassment is committed: (1) Against one who is under the care, custody or supervision of the offender; (2) Against one whose education, training, apprenticeship or tutorship is entrusted to the offender; (3) When the sexual favor is made a condition to the giving of a passing grade, or the granting of honors and scholarships, or the payment of a stipend, allowance or other benefits, privileges, or consideration; or (4) When the sexual advances result in an intimidating, hostile or offensive environment for the student, trainee or apprentice. Any person who directs or induces another to commit any act of sexual harassment as herein defined, or who cooperates in the commission thereof by another without which it would not have been committed, shall also be held liable under this Act. d. Sexual Violence - refers to acts which are sexual in nature. It includes but not limited to: d.1 rape, sexual harassment, acts of lasciviousness, making demeaning and sexually suggestive remarks, physically attacking the sexual parts of the victims’ body d.2 forcing the child to watch obscene publications and indecent shows or forcing the child to do indecent sexual acts and/or to engage or be involved in, the creation or distribution of such films, indecent publication or material

d.3 acts causing or attempting to cause the child to engage in any sexual activity by force, threat of force, physical or other harm or threat of physical or other harm or coercion, or through inducements, gifts or favour. d.4 other acts of sexual nature that are prejudicial to the interest of the students and personnel.

Procedures for Filing a Complaint with the Discipline and Grievance Committee 1. A written complaint shall be filed as follows: a. by the complainant himself to the Office of the Rector, if the complainant is personnel of the school or is above 18 years of age. b. In the event that the complainant or aggrieved party is a child, the written incident report submitted by any student, personnel, parent or guardian or guidance counselor who has knowledge of the incident shall be treated as a complaint which incident report shall be immediately submitted to the Office of the Rector. c. By the complainant, though minor, but with the conformity by parent, guardian, teacher or guidance counselor. 2. After receipt of the complaint, the Office of the Rector has the authority to call the parties to the case for possible amicable settlement. In the event that there was failure of settlement, the Office of the Rector shall call for the convocation of the grievance committee, composed of the following: Chairman - Director of Student & Personnel Services Members - Director of Spiritual Affairs

Dean/TED Head/Principal Coordinator for Guidance & Counseling Office HRD (when a school employee is involved) Prefect of Discipline (when a student is involved) The Complaint/incident report shall be endorsed to the chairman of the grievance. 3. After the convocation of the Grievance Committee, the chairman shall send a copy of the complaint/incident report to the respondent/s who shall be given five (5) working days to answer in writing the complaint filed against him/them, informing of his/her right to the services of counsel in the preparation of the Answer. 4. If after five (5) days from receipt of the complaint/incident report and the respondent/s failed to answer, the same shall be treated as a waiver of his right to file an Answer and the Committee shall proceed with the case ex-parte. 5. However, should the respondent fail to reply within the prescribed period due to justifiable reasons, a non-extendable period of three (3) days shall be granted. 6. The Chair shall act as the presiding officer during the hearing. He shall commence the proceedings by reading the complaint/s and reply/ies filed before the Committee.

7. In the presentation of the evidence, the parties shall be given the rights to present their respective evidence and witness before the body. Witnesses are subject to cross-examination by the Committee but not by the other party. 8. In the event that in the course of the investigation, a new witness filed a statement in support of the complaint, the respondent shall be given a period of five (5) within which to file any answer to rebut or refute the claim, which answer shall be forwarded to the complainant. 9. In the presentation of evidence, the complainant shall first present his/her side followed by the respondent/s. 10. The Committee shall submit its findings and recommendations to the Rector, who in turn will submit the same to the House Council for final decision. 11. In all cases, the decisions of the House Council shall be final and the same shall executed by the Rector. Section 6. Penalty. The penalty of reprimand, suspension or termination may be imposed based on the gravity of the charge complained of. Section 7. Confidentiality clause. All proceedings and records of the case shall be treated with outmost confidentiality especially the identity of the victim, if he/she a minor.

Section 8. Reportorial Requirement of Department of Education. Report concerning the case must be prepared by the Human Resource Development and Management Office if it involves school personnel. For cases involving student/s, it is the duty of the Director for Student and Personnel Services to prepare the report to Department of Education.

section_title: KNOW ALL MEN BY THESE PRESENTS:
content: Whereas, Rogationist College as a Catholic School acknowledges its obligations to exercise reasonable supervision over the conduct of the student and to cultivate the best potentialities of the heart and mind of the students by committing to the formation of its members towards love of God and neighbor and promotion of proper decorum, good behavior and positive values; Whereas, the Department of Education issued Department Order No. 40, Series of 2012, on May 14, 2012 otherwise known as “DepEd Child Protection Policy” with respect to Policy and Guidelines on Protecting Children in School from Abuse, Violence, Exploitation, Discrimination, Bullying and other Forms of Abuse; Whereas, in line with the mandate of curtailing bullying, inside and outside of the school, REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10627, or the "Anti-Bullying Act of 2013", was passed to address growing concerns of bullying, and Rogationist College is one in promoting zero-tolerance on bullying; Whereas, Rogationist College in order to comply with the different laws, rules and regulation in relation to bullying formulated its own rules of procedure in addressing the complaint on bullying; Thus the foregoing rule is hereby adopted.
This shall be known as “RULES AND REGULATIONS IN RELATION TO CASES INVOLVING BULLYING IN ROGATIONIST COLLEGE”

It is the mandate of the 1987 the Philippine Constitution for educational institutions to inculcate patriotism and nationalism, foster love of humanity, respect for human rights, appreciation of the roles of national heroes in the historical development of the country, teach the rights and duties of citizenship, strengthen ethical and spiritual values, develop moral character and personal discipline, encourage critical and creative thinking, broaden scientific and technical knowledge, and promote vocational efficiency (Article XIV, Section 3 (2)); In order to protect the rights of individuals in education institution, the Department of Education issued Department Order No. 40, Series of 2012, on May 14, 2012 otherwise known as “DepEd Child Protection Policy” with respect to Policy and Guidelines on Protecting Children in School from Abuse, Violence, Exploitation, Discrimination, Bullying and other Forms of Abuse, as well as Republic Act No. 10627, or the "Anti-Bullying Act of 2013", which Rogationist College hereby adopts in toto.

It is the objective of Rogationist College to provide not only good and quality education but also to inculcate the values and teachings of its founder, St. Hannibal Mary di Francia, in relation to morals, proper decorum and good behaviour. It is the policy of Rogationist College to free its environment from all acts of bullying and condemns any act pertinent or related thereto for it is highly unacceptable behaviour, contrary to law and morals. However, considering the effect/s on the welfare of the child and employment of individuals, Rogationist College undertakes to consider all aspects of the complaint and all proceedings shall be treated with strict confidentiality. Rogationist College shall consider due process in handling cases involving bullying to protect not only the rights of the complainant but also of the person being charged, without prejudice to complying with the reportorial requirement mandated by Department Order No. 40, Series of 2012, issued by the Department of Education and separate criminal cases that may be instituted.

“Bullying” refers to any severe, or repeated use by one or more students of a written, verbal or electronic expression, or a physical act or gesture, or any combination thereof, directed at another student that has the effect of actually causing or placing the latter in reasonable fear of physical or emotional harm or damage to his property; creating a hostile environment at school for the other student; infringing on the rights of another student at school; or materially and substantially disrupting the education process or the orderly operation of a school; “Bullied” or “Victim” – refers to any student who experiences the acts of bullying or retaliation as defined by the Act or this IRR. “Bystander” – refers to any person who witnesses or has personal knowledge of any actual or perceived acts or incidents of bullying or retaliation as defined by this IRR. “Learning center” – refers to learning resources and facilities of a learning program for out-of-school youth and adults as defined in DepEd Order. No. 43, s. 2013. “Service provider” – refers to any person who is not a teacher or school personnel but who works in the school, such as, but not limited to, security guards, canteen personnel, utility workers, and transportation service personnel.

“Student” – refers to a person who attends classes in any level of basic education, and includes a pupil or learner as defined in DepEd Order No. 40, s. 2012. “Prompt Report” – refers to prompt reporting of incident of bullying from June 1 of the current year until March 31 of the following year in order to maximize the intervention, reformation and/or imposition of appropriate sanction/s of the school.

section_title: Section 5. Forms of Bullying, such as, but not limited to, the following:
content: 1. Any unwanted physical contact between the bully and the victim like punching, pushing, shoving, kicking, slapping, tickling, headlocks, inflicting school pranks, teasing, fighting and the use of available objects as weapons; 2. Any act that causes damage to a victim’s psyche and/or emotional well-being; 3. Any slanderous statement or accusation that causes the victim undue emotional distress like directing foul language or profanity at the target, name-calling, tormenting and commenting negatively on victim’s looks, clothes and body; 4. Cyber- bullying or any bullying done through the use of technology or any electronic means. The term shall also include any conduct resulting to harassment, intimidation, or humiliation, through the use of other forms of technology, such as, but not limited to texting, email, instant messaging, chatting, internet, social media, online games, or other platforms or formats as defined in DepEd Order No. 40, s. 2012; Bullying at a location, activity, function or program that is not school-related and through the use of technology or an electronic device or other forms of media that is not owned, leased or used by a school;

section_title: Section 5. Forms of Bullying, such as, but not limited to, the following:
content: 5. Social bullying or any deliberate, repetitive and aggressive social behavior intended to hurt others or to belittle another individual or group. 6. Gender-based bullying or any act that humiliates or excludes a person on the basis of perceived or actual sexual orientation and gender identity (SOGI). 7. Retaliation against a person who reports bullying, who provides information during an investigation of bullying, or who is a witness to or has reliable information about bullying.

section_title: Section 6. Place of Commission of bullying
content: Bullying can be committed on the following places: a. school grounds; b. property immediately adjacent to school grounds; c. school-sponsored or school-related activities, functions or programs whether on or off school grounds; d. school bus stops; e. school buses or other vehicles owned, leased or used by a school; or f. school buses or school services privately-owned but accredited by the school.

A. Immediate Responses 1. A victim or a bystander, or a school personnel who receives information of a bullying incident or retaliation, or any person who witnesses or has personal knowledge of any incident of bullying or retaliation, shall report the same to the Prefect of Discipline or Guidance Counselor. 2. The school personnel who was notified of a bullying incident or retaliation shall intervene, by: i. Stopping the bullying or retaliation immediately; ii. Separating the students involved; iii. Removing the victim or, in appropriate cases, the bully or offending student, from the site; iv. Ensuring the victim’s safety, by: - Determining and addressing the victim’s immediate safety needs; and - Ensuring medical attention, if needed, and securing a medical certificate, in cases of physical injury. - Bringing the bully to the Guidance Office or Office for Student Discipline. B. Reporting the Bullying Incident or Retaliation A written complaint shall be filed by any of the following to the Office for Student Discipline: 1. by the complainant/victim himself if the complainant is a personnel of the school or is above 18 years of age;

2. In the event that the complainant or aggrieved party is a child, the written incident report submitted by any student, personnel, parent or guardian or guidance counsellor or anyone who has knowledge of the incident shall be treated as a complaint which incident report shall be immediately submitted to the Office for Student Discipline; or 3. By the complainant, though minor, with the consent of the teacher, parent, legal guardian or guidance counselor The Prefect of Discipline who receives the report or information regarding a bullying incident or retaliation shall ask the victim or the bystander, or the school personnel who witnessed or has personal knowledge of the incident of bullying or retaliation, shall be asked to fill up the Intake Sheet as provided in DepEd Order No. 40, s. 2012. The Prefect of Discipline shall inform the Principal and Rector of all reports of incident of bullying received by the Office and of the actions taken in order to respond to the report on bullying. C. Fact-Finding and Documentation The Prefect of Discipline who receives the report or information regarding a bullying incident or retaliation shall perform the following:

1. Separately interviews in private the offending student/s, the victim/s and all other individuals who hold vital information regarding the parties or incidents. During the interview, students shall be asked to write down their account of the incident in the presence of their respective homeroom adviser or guidance facilitator/counselor. 2. Determines the levels of threats and develop intervention strategies. If the alleged bullying incident or retaliation or the situation requires immediate attention or intervention, or the level of threat is high, appropriate action shall be taken by the school within twenty-four hours (24) from the time of the incident. 3. Informs the parents/legal guardian of the offending student and the victim of the bullying incident and personally confers the parents/legal guardian of students involved to resolve any issue and to restore, as far as practicable, the relationships of the parties involved. 4. Carefully and thoroughly studies the case to determine the appropriate interventions to be provided to the victim and the offending student or disciplinary measure to be imposed to the offending student. 5. Submits to the Director of Student Support Services a comprehensive report on the result of interview or verification held with the students involved, conference made with the students’ parents/legal guardian and the appropriate interventions to be provided to the victim and the offending student or disciplinary measure to be imposed to the offending student.

6. Makes appropriate referral to the Child Protection Committee if the issue on bullying is not resolved among the parties or for purpose of further fact-finding. D. Due Process 1. The Director for Student Support Services shall call for the convocation of the Child Protection Committee, composed of the following: 1. Director for Student Support Services – Chairperson 2. Guidance Counselor/Teacher – Vice Chairperson 3. Representative of the Teachers as designated by the Faculty Members 4. President of the Parents Teacher Association 5. President of the Student Body Organization 2. The offending student/s and the parent/s or legal guardian/s shall be informed of the complaint in writing. 3. The students shall be given the opportunity to answer the complaint in writing within the school ground in the presence of the Child Protection Committee members, with the assistance of the parents or legal guardian. 4. As a rule, the period to reply shall not be extendable except for justifiable reasons. Said extension, if granted, shall not exceed three (3) calendar days. 5. In case of contradicting statements of material value, parties may be called by the Child Protection Committee and be subjected to clarificatory questioning by the Child Protection Committee members. Questions can only be propounded by the Child Protection Committee and not by any of the parties.

6. The Committee shall submit its findings and recommendations to the Office of the Rector for the decision and/or imposition of appropriate sanction, if any. 7. Parents can make an appeal to the School Board within 10 calendar days from receipt of the decision. Pending the appeal, intervention program, but not disciplinary action, shall commence. 8. The decision of the School Board shall be final. E. Referral The Rector or the Child Protection Committee may refer the victim/s and the bully/ies to trained professionals outside the school, such as social workers, psychologists, or child protection specialists, for further assessment and appropriate intervention measures, as may be necessary. The School Head or the designated school personnel shall notify the Women and Children’s Protection Desk (WPCD) of the local Philippine National Police, if he/she believes that appropriate criminal charges may be pursued against the bully or offending student.

If the student, after an investigation, is found to have knowingly made a false accusation of bullying, the said student shall be subjected to disciplinary actions or to appropriate interventions in accordance with the existing rules and regulations of the Department or the private school. Section 9. Incident of Bullying or Retaliation Involving Students from More than One School If an incident of bullying or retaliation involves students from more than one school, the school that was first informed of the bullying or retaliation shall promptly notify the appropriate administrator or school head of the other school so that both schools may take appropriate action.

Reports of incidents of bullying or retaliation initiated by persons who prefer anonymity shall be entertained, and the person who reported the incident shall be afforded protection from possible retaliation; provided, however, that no disciplinary administrative action shall be taken against an alleged bully or offending student solely on the basis of an anonymous report and without any other evidence. Moreover, it should be made clear to the person who made the report that when they report incidents of bullying they are giving factual and truthful information.

section_title: Section 11. Role/Duty of Child Protection Committee.
content: In addition to their duties and responsibilities provided by DepEd Order No. 40, s. 2012, the Child Protection Committee shall perform the following tasks: a. Conducts awareness-raising programs with school stakeholders in preventing and addressing bullying; b. Ensures that the anti-bullying policy adopted by the school is implemented; c. Monitors all cases or incidents related to bullying reported or referred by the teacher, guidance counselor or coordinator or any person designated to handle prevention and intervention measures mentioned by the preceding sections of this IRR; and d. Makes the necessary referrals to appropriate agencies, offices or persons, as may be required by the circumstances.

Written reprimand, community service, suspension, exclusion or expulsion, in accordance with existing rules and regulations of the school or of the Department for public schools, may be imposed, if the circumstances warrant the imposition of such penalty, provided that the requirements of due process are complied with. In addition to the disciplinary sanction, the bully shall also be required to undergo an intervention program which shall be administered or supervised by the school’s Child Protection Committee. The parents of the bully shall be encouraged to join the intervention program.

Complaints of bullying and other acts of abuse under DepEd Order No. 40, s. 2012 shall be within the exclusive jurisdiction of Rogationist College, and shall not be brought for amicable settlement before the Barangay, subject to existing laws, rules and regulations. Complaints for acts committed by persons not under the jurisdiction of the Disciplinary Authority of Rogationist College shall be referred to the appropriate authorities.

In bullying or peer abuse and other acts of abuse by a student, the identity or other information that may reasonably identify the student, whether victim or offender, shall be withheld from the public to protect his or her privacy.

Criminal and civil liability arising from bullying and other acts of abuse are separate and distinct, and shall not be a bar to the filing of an administrative case under these guidelines. If the bullying incident or retaliation resulted in serious physical injuries or death, the case shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Republic Act 9344 or the “Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act”, as amended, and its Implementing Rules and Regulations, in connection with other applicable laws, as may be warranted by the circumstances attendant to the bullying incident.
All rules and regulations inconsistent to the provision of the foregoing act are hereby repealed or modified accordingly.

This rules and regulations shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its publication by posting copies thereof in the school bulletin board or its publication in any school authorized publications, whichever comes first. Appendix I

section_title: ANTI-HAZING LAW OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES
content: Republic Act No. 8049 An Act Regulating Hazing and Other Forms of Initiation Rites in Fraternities, Sororities and Organizations and Providing Penalties Therefore. Be enacted by Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: Section 1. Hazing, as used in this Act, is an initiation rite or practice as a prerequisite for admission into membership in a fraternity, sorority or organization by placing the recruit, neophyte or applicant in some embarrassing or humiliating situations such as forcing him to do menial, silly, foolish and other similar tasks or activities or otherwise subjecting him to physical or psychological suffering or injury. The term "organization" shall include any club or the Armed Forces of the Philippines, Philippine National Police, Philippine Military Academy, or officer and cadet corp of the Citizen's Military Training and Citizen's Army Training. The physical, mental and psychological testing and training procedure and practices to determine and enhance the physical, mental and psychological fitness of prospective regular members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Philippine National Police as approved ny the Secretary of National Defense and the National Police Commission duly recommended by the Chief of Staff, Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Director General of the Philippine National Police shall not be considered as hazing for the purposes of this Act.

section_title: ANTI-HAZING LAW OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES
content: Section 2. No hazing or initiation rites in any form or manner by a fraternity, sorority or organization shall be allowed without prior written notice to the school authorities or head of organization seven (7) days before the conduct of such initiation. The written notice shall indicate the period of the initiation activities which shall not exceed three (3) days, shall include the names of those to be subjected to such activities, and shall further contain an undertaking that no physical violence be employed by anybody during such initiation rites. Section 3. The head of the school or organization or their representatives must assign at least two (2) representatives of the school or organization, as the case may be, to be present during the initiation. It is the duty of such representative to see to it that no physical harm of any kind shall be inflicted upon a recruit, neophyte or applicant. Section 4. If the person subjected to hazing or other forms of initiation rites suffers any physical injury or dies as a result thereof, the officers and members of the fraternity, sorority or organization who actually participated in the infliction of physical harm shall be liable as principals. The person or persons who participated in the hazing shall suffer:

section_title: ANTI-HAZING LAW OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES
content: 1. The penalty of reclusion perpetua (life imprisonment) if death, rape, sodomy or mutilation results there from. 2. The penalty of reclusion temporal in its maximum period (17 years, 4 months and 1 day to 20 years) if in consequence of the hazing the victim shall become insane, imbecile, impotent or blind. 3. The penalty of reclusion temporal in its medium period (14 years, 8 months and one day to 17 years and 4 months) if in consequence of the hazing the victim shall have lost the use of speech or the power to hear or to smell, or shall have lost an eye, a hand, a foot, an arm or a leg or shall have lost the use of any such member shall have become incapacitated for the activity or work in which he was habitually engaged. 4. The penalty of reclusion temporal in its minimum period (12 years and one day to 14 years and 8 months) if in consequence of the hazing the victim shall become deformed or shall have lost any other part of his body, or shall have lost the use thereof, or shall have been ill or incapacitated for the performance on the activity or work in which he was habitually engaged for a period of more than ninety (90) days.

section_title: ANTI-HAZING LAW OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES
content: 5. The penalty of prison mayor in its maximum period (10 years and one day to 12 years) if in consequence of the hazing the victim shall have been ill or incapacitated for the performance on the activity or work in which he was habitually engaged for a period of more than thirty (30) days. 6. The penalty of prison mayor in its medium period (8 years and one day to 10 years) if in consequence of the hazing the victim shall have been ill or incapacitated for the performance on the activity or work in which he was habitually engaged for a period of ten (10) days or more, or that the injury sustained shall require medical assistance for the same period. 7. The penalty of prison mayor in its minimum period (6 years and one day to 8 years) if in consequence of the hazing the victim shall have been ill or incapacitated for the performance on the activity or work in which he was habitually engaged from one (1) to nine (9) days, or that the injury sustained shall require medical assistance for the same period.

section_title: ANTI-HAZING LAW OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES
content: 8. The penalty of prison correccional in its maximum period (4 years, 2 months and one day to 6 years) if in consequence of the hazing the victim sustained physical injuries which do not prevent him from engaging in his habitual activity or work nor require medical attendance. The responsible officials of the school or of the police, military or citizen's army training organization, may impose the appropriate administrative sanctions on the person or the persons charged under this provision even before their conviction. The maximum penalty herein provided shall be imposed in any of the following instances: (a) when the recruitment is accompanied by force, violence, threat, intimidation or deceit on the person of the recruit who refuses to join; (b) when the recruit, neophyte or applicant initially consents to join but upon learning that hazing will be committed on his person, is prevented from quitting; (c) when the recruit, neophyte or applicant having undergone hazing is prevented from reporting the unlawful act to his parents or guardians, to the proper school authorities, or to the police authorities, through force, violence, threat or intimidation;

section_title: ANTI-HAZING LAW OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES
content: (d) when the hazing is committed outside of the school or institution; or (e) when the victim is below twelve (12) years of age at the time of the hazing. The owner of the place where hazing is conducted shall be liable as an accomplice, when he has actual knowledge of the hazing conducted therein but failed to take any action to prevent the same from occurring. If the hazing is held in the home of one of the officers or members of the fraternity, group, or organization, the parents shall be held liable as principals when they have actual knowledge of the hazing conducted therein but failed to take any action to prevent the same from occurring. The school authorities including faculty members who consent to the hazing or who have actual knowledge thereof, but failed to take any action to prevent the same from occurring shall be punished as accomplices for the acts of hazing committed by the perpetrators. The officers, former officers, or alumni of the organization, group, fraternity or sorority who actually planned the hazing although not present when the acts constituting the hazing were committed shall be liable as principals. A fraternity or sorority's adviser who is present when the acts constituting the hazing were committed and failed to take action to prevent the same from occurring shall be liable as principal.

section_title: ANTI-HAZING LAW OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES
content: The presence of any person during the hazing is prima facie evidence of participation therein as principal unless he prevented the commission of the acts punishable herein. Any person charged under this provision shall not be entitled to the mitigating circumstance that there was no intention to commit so grave a wrong. This section shall apply to the president, manager, director or other responsible officer of a corporation engaged in hazing as a requirement for employment in the manner provided herein. Section 5. If any provision or part of this Act is declared invalid or unconstitutional, the other parts or provisions thereof shall remain valid and effective. Section 6. All laws, orders, rules or regulations which are inconsistent with or contrary to the provisions of this Act are hereby amended or repealed accordingly. Section 7. This Act shall take effect fifteen (15) calendar days after its publication in at least two (2) national newspapers of general circulation. Approved; June 07, 1995 (Signed) Fidel V. Ramos President of the Philippines Appendix J Republic of the Philippines Office of the President

Series of 2003 SUBJECT : General Guidelines For The Conduct Of Random Drug Testing For Secondary And Tertiary Students Pursuant to Section 36 (c), Article III of Republic Act No. 9165, the following guidelines are hereby promulgated. The guidelines shall be applicable to the random drug testing of students in public and private secondary, tertiary /higher education institutions and post-secondary technical vocational schools. These guidelines outline the purposes of the random drug-testing program, as well as procedures and necessary consequences of a positive drug test result after confirmation. All procedures undertaken shall take into account the ideals of fairness and rehabilitation and not isolation of the drug dependent. The school must not violate the constitutional rights to due process, equal protection and self-incrimination. A. GUIDING PRINCIPLES IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF RANDOM DRUG TESTING IN SCHOOLS AND MANAGEMENT OF DRUG TEST RESULTS 1. Government recognizes the primary responsibility of the family, particularly the parents for the education and awareness of its members of the ill effects of dangerous drugs. 2. Parental involvement shall be maximized in the implementation of drug education, random drug testing, treatment and rehabilitation of drug users and dependents.

3. The school, with the assistance of Local Government Units (LGUs) and other agencies where the school is located, has the obligation to employ every reasonable means to provide a healthy and drug-free environment to its populace. 4. Cognizant of the right of the students to continue and complete their studies, the government and the schools shall give emphasis to the implementation of measures aimed at guidance and counseling together with the treatment and rehabilitation of any student found to have used or to be dependent on dangerous drugs. 5. Academic freedom of institutions of higher learning shall be respected in the implementation of random drug testing and all other pertinent provisions of RA 9165. 6. The implementation of drug abuse prevention and education programs in schools shall be intensified as an integral part of the over-all demand reduction efforts of the government. 7. The random drug testing shall be implemented as a collaborative undertaking of the government, the schools, the students and their parents. The whole process shall not in any manner be utilized to harass the students. 8. Random drug testing shall be implemented primarily for prevention and rehabilitation.

9. The drug-testing program shall guarantee and respect the personal privacy and dignity of the student. 10. The drug test results shall be treated with utmost confidentiality. 11. The test results shall not be used in any criminal proceedings.

section_title: B. PURPOSES OF RANDOM DRUG TESTING
content: 1. To determine the prevalence of drug users among the students 2. To assess the effectivity of school-based and community-based prevention programs 3. To deter the use of illegal drugs 4. To facilitate the rehabilitation of drug users and dependents 5. To strengthen the collaboration efforts of identified agencies against the use of illegal drugs and in the rehabilitation of drug users and dependents.

“Drug Counselor” shall mean a person trained in the techniques of guidance counseling particularly dealing with cases of drug dependency. The Drug Testing Coordinator shall designate such person. “Drug Testing Coordinator ” shall be the point person in the school tasked with handling random drug testing which shall be the principal of a secondary school, the administrator of a technical vocational education and training institution or the administrator appointed by the president/chief executive officer in tertiary institutions. “Parents” shall, for purposes of these guidelines, include court appointed guardians. “Random selection” refers to the unbiased process of selecting students who are to undergo drug testing. “Rehabilitation” is the dynamic process, including after-care and follow-up treatment, directed towards the physical, emotional/psychological, vocational, social and spiritual change/enhancement of a drug dependent to enable him/her to live without dangerous drugs, enjoy the fullest life compatible with his/her capabilities and potentials and render him/her to become a law-abiding and productive member of the community. “Schools” shall mean an institution that has as its primary purpose the education of students including secondary, tertiary and technical vocational education and training institutions.

“Selection Board” shall be the board constituted at the level of the school composed of the Drug Testing Coordinator as chairperson, one representative each from the students, faculty and parents as members. The authorized governing body duly recognized by their respective constituents shall choose the representatives from these stakeholders based on a set of selection criteria formulated for this purpose. In the absence of a parents’ association, the School Head may appoint any parent who shall be a member of the Selection Board. “Supervising Agency” shall refer to the government agency that exercises supervision over the school such as the Department of Education (DepEd), Commission on Higher Education (CHED), or the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA).

section_title: D. PROCEDURES IN THE CONDUCT OF RANDOM DRUG TESTING
content: 1. Notification a. The Supervising Agency through an appropriate order that includes these guidelines on random drug testing, shall inform all schools under its supervision about the government’s actions against illegal drugs. The schools’ administration shall be required to explain these provisions and their procedures to the school community and when applicable, include these in the schools’ handbook or listing of procedures. (The Supervising Agencies’ Memorandum Circulars should include a list of DOH-accredited Testing Centers/Laboratories.) b. All students and their parents shall be notified in writing on the process and manner by which the random drug testing shall be conducted. Such notification may be sent at any time during the school term. Failure to return the acknowledgment receipt shall not be a bar to the conduct of the drug testing. 2. Samples a. The Supervising Agency shall inform randomly selected schools on their inclusion in the random drug testing program. b. The whole student population of the school selected shall be included in the random sampling. c. The number of samples should yield a statistical 95% confidence level for the whole student population

section_title: D. PROCEDURES IN THE CONDUCT OF RANDOM DRUG TESTING
content: 3. Selection of Samples a. The Drug Testing Coordinator shall convene the Selection Board within five days from the receipt of notice from the Supervising Agency stating that the school is included in the program. b. On the day of the testing, the Selection Board shall conduct the random selection of those to be tested. c. The Selection Board shall ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the random selection process. d. The selection process shall be random through a lottery, which may be computerized, or in any other manner that shall be agreed upon by the Board e. The random selection of students and the drug testing shall be done on the same day. f. Prior to testing, the selected students shall be asked to reveal the prescription medicines, vitamins, food supplements that they had ingested within the past five (5) days. The Drug Testing Coordinator shall keep the listing and utilize this in the evaluation of the confirmatory drug test. g. The laboratory shall follow the DOH prescribed guidelines in the collection of urine specimens. Universal precautions shall be observed at all times. DOH Prescribed Guidelines shall be posted in strategic places/visible

section_title: D. PROCEDURES IN THE CONDUCT OF RANDOM DRUG TESTING
content: areas of the school. h. The monitor assigned to ensure the integrity of the collection process should be of the same sex as the student. i. The drug testing shall be done in the school and conducted by a duly accredited drug-testing laboratory. The school, through its respective health personnel, shall assist the Drug Testing Laboratory in the conduct of the drug testing. j. The Drug Testing Coordinator shall ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the random drug testing for the students, teachers, administration and personnel of the school. It is strongly recommended that the drug testing for students, the teachers, administration and personnel be done simultaneously. 4. Treatment of Random Drug Test Results a. The results of the test shall be strictly confidential. No school shall publish or post results whether positive or negative. b. Any person who violates the rules of confidentiality of the results and selection shall be liable under Section 72 of RA 9165 and such other appropriate laws. c. The laboratory shall place the drug test result in a sealed envelope and deliver the same via personal service to the Drug Testing Coordinator. The Drug Testing Coordinator shall then inform all the students tested individually of the test results.

section_title: D. PROCEDURES IN THE CONDUCT OF RANDOM DRUG TESTING
content: d. In case the test results are positive, the Drug Testing Coordinator shall inform both the student and parent concerned that a confirmatory test shall be conducted. The student shall be told to inform his/her parents of the scheduled conference with the Drug Testing Coordinator. The student shall be advised to refrain from revealing the test results to other persons. e. During the scheduled conference, the Drug Testing Coordinator shall relay to the parents full information on the process that shall be undertaken for the confirmatory test. In the event that the parents do not appear on the scheduled conference, the student shall be informed of the schedule of the confirmatory test. f. The confirmatory drug test shall be conducted in the same manner as the initial drug test. g. The results of the confirmatory test shall be transmitted by the laboratory in a sealed envelope and handed directly to the Drug Testing Coordinator. h. The Drug Testing Coordinator shall inform both the parents and the student of the results of the test. i. The Drug Testing Coordinator shall not delegate such task of informing the student and parent to any other person, nor shall the Drug Testing Coordinator reveal the results of the test to any person other than the student and parent.

section_title: D. PROCEDURES IN THE CONDUCT OF RANDOM DRUG TESTING
content: j. First time positive confirmatory drug test result shall not be a ground for expulsion or any disciplinary action against the student. k. The Drug Testing Coordinator shall refer the student and his/her parent to government-owned DOH-accredited facility or DOH-accredited government physician to determine the student’s dependency level. l. The student may opt for a private DOH-accredited facility or physician for this initial determination provided it is at his/her own expense. m. In the event that it is determined that the student is a drug dependent, the school may impose the appropriate sanctions against the student as provided for in the school’s Student Handbook and the Manual of Regulations for Private Schools, provided that in the case of public secondary schools, if the student is later on found to have been rehabilitated, the student shall then be allowed to re-enroll. n. The student shall then undergo a three (3) month observation and counseling period under the supervision of the DOH-accredited facility or physician in consultation with the parent. Such process of observation and counseling shall be done in coordination with the Drug Counselor of the school.

section_title: D. PROCEDURES IN THE CONDUCT OF RANDOM DRUG TESTING
content: o. At the end of the three months, it is hoped that with the counseling done, the student will be properly rehabilitated. If student shows no signs of improvement, recovery or fails the drug test the second time, the DOH- accredited facility or physician, may make a recommendation to the student, parent, and Drug Testing Coordinator to have the student referred to a DOH- accredited facility suited to the student’s level of dependency. If another drug testing is conducted for another period on the same student population, and the student is found positive the second time, the school shall proceed in accordance with Section 61, R.A. 9165. The parent and the student may choose to enroll the student in a private rehabilitation center or program or opt to avail of the rehabilitation services of the government through a DOH-accredited facility. If the parents refuse to act, the school shall proceed in accordance to Sec. 61 of RA 9165 without prejudice to the provision of Section 73, RA 9165. E. Reportorial Requirements of Results of the Random Drug Testing 1. The Drug Testing Coordinator, Drug Counselor and employees of DOH-accredited facilities, testing laboratories, shall not reveal the names of the students or test results to any other persons except to the student concerned or his/her parents.

section_title: D. PROCEDURES IN THE CONDUCT OF RANDOM DRUG TESTING
content: 2. The aggregate test results from each school which shall not include the identities of the students tested, shall be submitted by the School Head to the Division Superintendent of DepEd for secondary schools, the Regional Director of CHED for tertiary schools and Training Institution Administrator for TESDA for consolidation for the purpose of evaluating the efficacy and effectiveness of drug abuse prevention programs. F. Training of Guidance Counselors The Department of Education, Commission on Higher Education, Technical Education and Skills Development Authority, the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency and Dangerous Drugs Board in coordination with each other, shall formulate and conduct the training program for guidance counselors for the purpose of enhancing their skills in handling drug abuse prevention programs and handling drug dependency cases. G. Expenses of the Program The Department of Health, in coordination with the Supervising Agencies shall designate the drug testing laboratories that shall be utilized for purposes of the program. Payment of testing fees shall be done by the government thru Department of Health to the Drug Testing Laboratories. H. Enforcement of Compliance

section_title: D. PROCEDURES IN THE CONDUCT OF RANDOM DRUG TESTING
content: Students who refuse to undergo random drug testing shall be dealt with in accordance with the rules and regulations of the schools; provided that at no time shall refusal to undergo testing give rise to a presumption of drug use or dependency; provided further that the school may impose sanctions on such refusal other than the offense of drug use or dependency. Schools that refuse to implement the random drug testing program shall be liable under Section 32 of RA 9165 without prejudice to other administrative sanctions imposed by the Supervising Agencies. The Supervising Agency shall report the same to the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) and the Dangerous Drugs Board (DDB). I. Miscellaneous Provisions Separability clause. If any provision of these Guidelines or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held to be invalid, the other provisions of these Guidelines and the application of such provision to other persons or circumstances shall not be affected thereby. Effectivity. These Guidelines shall take effect immediately after its approval by the Dangerous Drugs Board. ADOPTED and APPROVED this 1st day of August, 2003 at Camp Crame, Quezon City.
